p.seg: Internal Chapters: Admonishing the Ruler
1.1 *Zhuāng Gōng Displays Courage and Strength, Disregarding Conduct. Yànzi Admonishes Him.*
Zhuāng Gōng displayed his courage and strength,
disregarding proper conduct.
He favored men of courage and strength,
showing no restraint in the state.
Noble relatives did not recommend the good,
close associates did not point out faults.
Therefore, Yànzi requested to see the Duke.
The Duke said,
"In ancient times, were there also those who established themselves in the world solely through courage and strength?"
Yànzi replied,
"Yīng has heard that
to lightly risk death to practice ritual is called courage,
to punish the violent without fearing the strong is called strength.
Therefore, the establishment of courage and strength
is to practice their ritual and righteousness.
Tāng and Wǔ used soldiers, but were not rebellious;
they annexed states, but were not greedy.
This is the principle of benevolence and righteousness.
To punish the violent without fearing the strong,
to replace the guilty without fearing the multitude,
is the conduct of courage and strength.
Those who possessed courage and strength in ancient times
practiced ritual and righteousness.
Now, if the ruler has no principle of benevolence and righteousness,
and his subjects have no conduct of replacing the guilty and punishing the violent,
But merely relying on courage and strength to establish oneself in the world,
then if the feudal lords practice this, their states will be endangered;
if commoners practice this, their families will be ruined.
In the past, when the Xià dynasty declined,
there were Tuī Chǐ and Dà Xì;
when the Yīn dynasty declined,
there were Fèi Zhòng and È Lái,
whose feet could run a thousand *lǐ*,
and hands could tear rhinoceroses and tigers.
They were entrusted with power based on their strength,
and they oppressed the world,
wielding their power and killing the innocent,
valuing courage and strength,
and disregarding righteousness and principle.
Therefore, Jié and Zhòu were destroyed,
and Yīn and Xià declined.
Now, you, Duke, pride yourself on courage and strength,
and disregard conduct.
You value men of courage and strength,
and have no restraint within the state.
You establish personal power and strength,
and your conduct is fundamentally licentious and tyrannical.
Your relatives do not recommend the virtuous,
those close to you do not point out your faults.
You contradict the virtue of the sage kings,
and follow the actions of rulers who brought about their own destruction.
I, Yīng, have never heard
of anyone who survives by using such methods."
1.2 "Duke Jǐng, Drunk with Wine, Wishes the Gentlemen to Dispense with Etiquette, Yàn Zǐ Admonishes"
Duke Jǐng, drunk with wine,
said:
"Today I wish to drink joyfully with you gentlemen,
please dispense with etiquette."
Yàn Zǐ abruptly changed his expression and said:
"Your words are a mistake!
Your ministers certainly desire that you be without etiquette.
Those with more strength will be able to overcome their superiors,
those with more courage will be able to assassinate their ruler,
but etiquette prevents it.
Birds and beasts govern with strength,
the strong violate the weak,
therefore the ruler changes daily.
Now if you discard etiquette,
then you are a bird or beast.
If your ministers govern with strength,
the strong will violate the weak,
and the ruler will change daily,
where will you be able to stand!
The reason why humans are valued above birds and beasts
is because they have etiquette;
therefore the "Odes" say:
'If a man has no etiquette,
why not die quickly.'
Etiquette cannot be without."
The Duke was intoxicated and did not listen.
After a short while, the Duke went out,
Yàn Zǐ did not rise;
the Duke came in, he did not rise;
when cups were passed, he drank first.
The Duke was angry,
his expression changed,
he pressed his hand down, glared, and said:
"Just now, did the Master teach me that being without propriety is unacceptable?
When I enter and leave, he does not rise;
When we exchange cups, he drinks first;
is this propriety?"
Yàn Zǐ stepped away from his mat, bowed twice, kowtowed, and requested:
"How could Yīng dare to speak with the ruler and then forget it?
I am simply demonstrating the reality of being without propriety.
If you, my lord, wish to be without propriety,
this is it!"
The Duke said:
"Good.
This is my fault.
Master, please return to your seat,
I have heard your instruction."
After three rounds of drinks,
the drinking party ended.
After this incident,
he regulated the laws and cultivated propriety in order to govern the state,
and the people became disciplined.
1.3 *Jǐng Gōng Yǐn Jiǔ Chéng Sān Rì Ér Hòu Fā Yàn Zǐ Jiàn* ("Duke Jǐng's Intoxication Lasting Three Days, Followed by Yàn Zǐ's Advice")
Duke Jǐng drank wine.
Chéng, it took three days before it manifested.
Yàn Zǐ saw him and said,
"Is Your Lordship suffering from illness due to wine?"
The Duke said,
"Yes."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"In ancient times, drinking wine
was only sufficient to facilitate communication and harmony.
Therefore, men did not gather for excessive merriment to hinder their affairs,
and women did not gather for excessive merriment to hinder their tasks.
When men and women gathered for merriment,
there was the Zhōu ritual of "five presentations" (of wine),
and those who exceeded it were punished.
The ruler personally adhered to this,
therefore there were no grievances outside (the court), and governance was effective,
and within (the court) there were no disorderly actions.
Now, Your Lordship drinks wine for one day,
and then sleeps for three days.
Will the governance of the state not cause resentment from those outside?
Will those on the left and right not cause disorder within?
Those who use punishments to defend themselves
encourage wrongdoing;
those who use rewards to encourage themselves
become lazy in doing good.
If the ruler departs from virtuous conduct,
the people will take rewards and punishments lightly,
and the reason for having a state will be lost.
I hope Your Lordship will moderate it!"
1.4 *Jǐng Gōng Yǐnjiǔ Qī Rì Bù Nà Xián Zhāng zhī Yán Yàn Zǐ Jiàn* (Duke Jing Drinks for Seven Days, Rejects Xián Zhāng's Advice, and Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him)
Duke Jǐng was drinking, for seven days and seven nights without stopping.
Xián Zhāng remonstrated, saying:
"Your Lordship has been drinking for seven days and seven nights,
I, Zhāng, wish for Your Lordship to give up drinking!
If not,
I, Zhāng, beg to die."
Yàn Zǐ entered to see the Duke,
and the Duke said:
"Zhāng admonished me, saying:
'I wish for Your Lordship to give up drinking!
If not,
I, Zhāng, beg to die.'
If I listen to him in this way,
then I am being controlled by a subject;
if I don't listen, then I pity his death."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"How fortunate that Zhāng met Your Lordship!
If Zhāng had met Jié or Zhòu,
Zhāng would have died long ago."
Thereupon, the Duke then gave up drinking.
1.5 *Jǐng Gōng Yǐnjiǔ Bù Xù Tiānzāi Zhì Nénggē Zhě Yàn Zǐ Jiàn* (Duke Jing Drinks and Does Not Worry About Natural Disasters, Brings in Able Singers, and Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him)
In the time of Duke Jǐng,
there was continuous rain for seventeen days.
The Duke was drinking,
Days and nights followed one another.
Yàn Zǐ petitioned to distribute grain to the people,
He petitioned three times,
But was not granted permission.
The Duke ordered Bǎi Jù to tour the state,
To find those skilled at singing.
Yàn Zǐ heard of this,
And was displeased.
Thereupon, he divided his family's grain among the commoners,
Placed his useful tools on the roads,
And walked to see the Duke, saying:
"It has been raining heavily for seventeen days!
In the villages, dozens of houses have collapsed,
In the neighborhoods, several families are starving,
The old and weak among the people,
Suffering from the cold, cannot obtain coarse cloth,
Starving, cannot obtain dregs and husks,
Broken down and discarded, they have nowhere to flee,
Looking around, they have no one to tell their woes.
Yet you, my lord, do not care,
But drink wine day and night,
And order the state to continue providing music without end.
The horses eat grain from the treasury,
The dogs are satiated with fodder and fattened meat,
And the concubines of the Three Protectors (high officials),
All have plenty of fine grain and meat.
Are the dogs, horses, and concubines
Not treated too generously?
The common people,
are they not impoverished?
Therefore, when the villages are impoverished and have no one to tell,
they have no joy with the ruler above;
when they are hungry and starving and have no one to tell,
they have no joy with the sovereign.
I, Yīng, holding tallies and counting them,
to follow the officials of the court,
the people are hungry, starving, impoverished, and destitute with no one to tell,
causing the ruler above to be dissolute, lose his foundation, and not care,
my crime, Yīng's, is great!"
He bowed twice and kowtowed,
requesting to leave on his own accord,
and then fled.
The duke followed him,
and overtook him on the road but could not catch him,
ordering to hasten a chariot to pursue Yàn Zǐ,
but it did not reach his home.
The grain and rice were exhausted by the people,
the carrying tools remained in the fields,
the duke drove up to him at Kāng Nèi.
The duke got out of his chariot and followed Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"I, your ruler, am guilty,
and you, sir, have abandoned and do not help me,
I, your ruler, am not worthy to have an agreement with you,
do you, sir, not consider the altars of the land and grain and the common people?
I wish for you, sir, to please spare me,
I, your ruler, request to offer the grain, rice, wealth and goods of the state of Qí,
Entrust it to the common people;
the amount, whether much or little, light or heavy,
will be according to your command, Master."
Thereupon, he bowed on the road.
Yànzǐ then returned,
ordering the officials to inspect the common people:
those families that possessed cloth and thread but were starving,
should be provided with enough to last a whole month;
those families that had no resources,
should be given food for a year;
those commoners who had no stored provisions,
should be given firewood and rafters,
enough to withstand the continuous rain.
He ordered Bǎi to inspect the commoners,
and those whose houses could not protect them,
should be given gold;
those who went to inspect for widowed and impoverished commoners who lacked resources,
had to finish in three days,
or those who were late would be punished for disobeying the order.
The Duke left his lodging,
reducing his meat and removing his wine,
his horses did not eat the government grain,
his dogs did not eat the fine meat,
he avoided fine clothes and frugal food,
and reduced the gifts to his drinking companions.
After three days,
the officials reported the completion to the Duke:
there were 17,000 impoverished families,
Used 970,000 *zhong* of grain,
13,000 cartloads of firewood and rafters;
destroyed 2,700 houses,
used 3,000 (units) of gold.
Only then did the Duke retire to his inner quarters for a meal;
lutes and zithers were not strung,
bells and drums were not displayed.
Yàn Zǐ requested that those around him who could order singing and dancing sufficient to cause lingering thoughts of Yú be dismissed,
3,000 attendants were sent away,
dismissed from the lower ranks,
commoners received three (units),
knights received four (units),
and they were sent beyond the border.
1.6 "Duke Jǐng Listens to New Music at Night and Does Not Hold Court; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him"
Yàn Zǐ went to court.
Dù Jiōng, looking towards the flock of sheep, waited at court.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Why does the lord not hold court?"
He replied:
"The lord indulged at night and cannot hold court."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Why?"
He replied:
"Liáng Qiū Jù introduced the singer Yú,
altering the music of Qí."
Yàn Zǐ withdrew from court,
ordered the master of ceremonies and the invocator to perform the rites and detain Yú.
The Duke, upon hearing this, became angry and said:
"For what reason did you detain Yú?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Because he used new music to corrupt the ruler."
The Duke said:
"The affairs of the feudal lords,
the administration of the officials,
I wish to ask you about these things.
The taste of wine and sweet liquor,
the sounds of metal and stone (instruments),
I hope that you, Master, will not participate in these.
As for music,
why must it be the old kind?"
He replied:
"When music is lost, ritual follows;
when ritual is lost, governance follows;
when governance is lost, the state follows.
When the state declines,
your servant fears that Your Lordship's perverse policies will be implemented.
There were songs,
Zhòu composed Běi Lǐ,
sounds like Yōu and Lì,
indicating that licentiousness and vulgarity lead to mutual destruction.
Why does Your Lordship lightly change the old ways?"
The Duke said:
"Unfortunately, I have the affairs of the state to manage,
and I speak without careful consideration;
I accept your instruction."
1.7 "Jǐng Gōng Yàn Shǎng Wú Gōng Ér Zuì Yǒu Sī, Yàn Zǐ Jiàn"
Jǐng Gōng held a banquet and rewarded people within the country.
There were three people who received ten thousand zhōng,
and five people who received one thousand zhōng.
He issued the order three times,
and the official in charge of accounts tallied it. The Duke was angry
and ordered the dismissal of the accounting official.
He issued the order three times,
and the chief judge tallied it. The Duke was displeased.
Yàn Zǐ went to see him.
The Duke said to Yàn Zǐ:
"I have heard that the ruler of a state
loves the people and can benefit them,
and hates the people and can alienate them.
Now, I love the people but cannot benefit them,
and hate the people but cannot alienate them.
I have lost the way of a ruler."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Yīng has heard that
when the ruler is upright and the ministers follow, it is called obedience;
when the ruler is biased and the ministers follow, it is called disobedience.
Now, you reward flattering ministers
and order officials to comply.
This is to make the ruler lose his way
and the ministers lose their duty.
The former kings established love
to encourage goodness,
and removed evil
In order to prohibit violence.
In the past, when the Three Dynasties rose,
those who benefited the state were loved,
and those who harmed the state were hated.
Therefore, because what was loved was clear, the worthy and good were numerous;
because what was hated was clear, the evil and perverse were eliminated.
Thus, the world was well-governed and peaceful,
and the people were harmonious and gathered together.
When they declined,
they valued ease and simplicity in their actions,
and comfort and pleasure for themselves.
Those who were agreeable to themselves were loved,
and those who opposed themselves were hated.
Therefore, because what was loved was clear, the evil and perverse flourished;
because what was hated was clear, the worthy and good were eliminated.
This scattered the people,
and endangered the state and its altars.
If the ruler above does not consider the rise of the sage kings,
and those below do not observe the decline of the lazy rulers,
ministers fear the ruler's perverse policies being implemented,
and officials dare not argue,
so that the state and its altars are overthrown,
and the ancestral temples are endangered."
The Duke said,
"I did not know this.
Please, I will follow the policy of the Chief Judge."
The state's revenue
that is collected has three sources.
1.8 《Duke Jing Trusts Slanderers and Flaws in Rewards and Punishments - Yànzǐ Advises》
Duke Jǐng trusted slanderers,
rewarded those without merit,
and punished the innocent.
Yànzǐ remonstrated, saying:
"I have heard that an enlightened ruler looks up to sages and trusts their teachings,
but I have not heard of listening to slanderers in order to administer punishments and rewards.
Now those around you are delighted and praise you, saying,
'Compared to the dead, let us strive to enjoy ourselves!
How can I practice benevolence and only increasingly tattoo the faces of the people!'
Wú ān néng wéi rén ér yù qíng mín ěr yǐ!'
Therefore, favored concubines within the palace
forcefully seize from the state,
favored officials outside the palace
falsely seize from the countryside,
and law-enforcing officers
jointly burden the people.
The people are worried, distressed, impoverished, and sick,
while the cunning scoundrels roam freely,
concealing their true feelings, covering up their wickedness,
and flattering their superiors.
Therefore, even if there are supremely wise and great sages,
how can they possibly overcome such slander!
That is why loyal ministers often suffer calamities and injuries.
I have heard that ancient scholars
can be gained,
"He cannot be abandoned;
he can be advanced (promoted);
he cannot be dismissed."
Your servant begs to flee from here."
Thereupon, he whipped his horse and went out.
The Duke sent Hàn Zǐxiū to pursue him,
saying,
"I, your ruler, am unbenevolent,
unable to follow your teachings,
to the point of this extreme.
Where will you, Master, rest your country and go?
I, your ruler, shall follow after you."
Àn Zǐ thereupon whipped his horse and returned.
His servant said,
"How swift was your departure just now!
How swift is your return now!"
Àn Zǐ said,
"This is not something you can understand.
The Duke's words were sincere."
1.9 *Jǐng Gōng Loves a Favored Concubine and Indulges Her Desires; Àn Zǐ Advises*
The prince of Dí, Wángzǐ Xiàn, served Duke Jǐng,
driving chariots with heavy loads.
The Duke watched it but was not pleased.
The favored person Yīng Zǐ desired to watch it,
and the Duke said,
"Wait until Àn Zǐ is sick in bed."
He stayed in the park on a terrace to watch it.
Yīng Zǐ was pleased with it,
Because of this request, he said:
"Give him a generous salary!"
The Duke agreed.
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 rose from his sickbed and met with the Duke.
The Duke said:
"The charioteering of Prince Xiàn 羡 of Zhái 翟 is excellent,
I am very pleased with it.
May I ask him to demonstrate it?"
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 said:
"The matter of charioteering
is not within my responsibility."
The Duke said:
"I am very pleased with it;
if I were to reward him with ten thousand zhōng 鍾 of grain, would that be enough?"
He replied:
"Formerly, the charioteering of the Wèi 衛 soldier Dōngyě 東野
pleased you, but it did not please Yīng Zǐ 嬰子.
You said you were displeased, and thus did not watch.
Now, the charioteering of Prince Xiàn 羡 of Zhái 翟
does not please you, but it pleases Yīng Zǐ 嬰子;
and you are pleased because of it.
To request this, and for you to grant it,
would be to let a woman make the rules.
Furthermore, you do not enjoy governing people,
but enjoy governing horses;
you do not generously reward worthy men,
but generously reward a charioteer.
In the past, the territory of your late predecessor Duke Huán 桓公 was smaller than it is now,
Cultivate law and order, broadly spread governance and education,
in order to dominate the various lords.
Now, you, as a lord, are unable to befriend even one other lord.
The year is bad, and there is famine;
on the roads, the dead are seen everywhere.
You do not worry or feel shame about this,
but only seek the pleasure of the ears and eyes;
you do not cultivate the meritorious achievements of your predecessors,
but only adorn the skills of charioteering.
Thus, your disregard for the people and forgetting of the state is extreme!
Moreover, the *Book of Odes* says:
"Loaded with matched teams and teams of four,
is where the lord arrives."
To drive with eight horses is certainly not according to regulations.
Now you are further increasing this,
its violation of regulations,
will it not be even greater!
Furthermore, if you, as lord, find pleasure in it,
the country will surely follow your example.
It will be inconvenient for hunting,
and impossible to travel far.
Yet the number of horses used will be many times greater.
This is not the way to govern one's subordinates.
Indulging in the pleasures of the ears and eyes
and not attending to the people's affairs,
this is what the sage kings prohibited.
If you, as lord, find pleasure in it,
the various lords will surely imitate you.
If you, my lord, do not possess profound virtue and good governance to extend to the various lords,
but instead replace it with deviancy,
this is not the way to treat the people as children,
make your name known,
reach far, and befriend neighboring states.
Furthermore, the virtuous and good are discarded and destroyed,
the orphaned and widowed are not supported,
and instead you listen to favored concubines, provide salary to officials to husband, and accumulate resentment,
this is the way to make enemies of the people.
The *Book of Poetry* says: "Wise men build up a city,
wise women tear down a city."
Now you, my lord, do not avoid what builds up the city,
but only engage in what tears down the city,
the day of the state's demise is approaching.
You must consider this!"
The Duke said: "Good."
Thereupon he did not resume the viewing,
and then dismissed and sent back the Dí prince Xiàn,
and distanced himself from the favored courtier Yīng Zǐ.
1.10 《Duke Jǐng instructs the tutors of his five sons and slips up, Yàn Zǐ remonstrates》
Duke Jǐng had five sons,
all those whom he employed to tutor them,
all had a hundred chariots.
Yàn Zǐ was one of them.
The Duke summoned their tutor and said:
"Work hard!
I will consider the one you tutor to be my heir."
Then they came to Yàn Zǐ,
Yàn Zǐ declined, saying:
"The ruler commands his subjects
to exert their strength, leaning on their shoulders.
How dare your subject not strive!
Now, in some family,
there is a powerful minister in the state,
and everyone commands him with the ruler's order, saying:
'We will make the one you tutor the heir.'
This is to separate from the tree and form factions,
a way to ruin the state.
Yīng dares not accept the command,
I hope the ruler will consider it!"
1.11《Duke Jǐng's Desire to Depose the Legitimate Son Yángshēng and Establish Tú – Yànzǐ's Admonishment》
Chún yú rén presented a daughter to Duke Jǐng,
who bore the young son Tú.
Duke Jǐng loved him.
The various ministers plotted to depose the prince Yángshēng and establish Tú.
The duke told Yàn Zǐ about this.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"It is not permissible.
To elevate the baseborn over the noble is
a harm to the state;
to set aside the heir and establish the younger is
the source of chaos.
Yángshēng is grown and the people support him.
Your Highness, do not change him!
Rank and position have their order,
Therefore, the lowly do not override the noble;
establishing a son has its proper rites,
therefore a son from a concubine does not disrupt the lineage.
I wish that Your Lordship would teach Tú with propriety and not let him fall into evil,
guide him with righteousness and not let him be submerged in profit.
Let the elder and younger act according to their proper ways,
let the lineage and those from concubines obtain their proper order.
How could Yáng Shēng dare not let Tú satiate himself with the taste of fine meat,
play with the sound of metal and stone,
and still have trouble?
To depose the elder and establish the younger,
this cannot be used to instruct those below;
to honor the son of a concubine and demean the main lineage,
this cannot be used to benefit the one who is loved.
If elders and youth have no distinction,
and lineages and those from concubines have no separation,
this is setting the foundation for thieves and planting the seeds of wickedness.
Your Lordship should consider this!
The enlightened rulers of old,
it wasn't that they didn't know about elaborate pleasures,
but they believed that excessive pleasure leads to sorrow;
it wasn't that they didn't know about establishing affection,
but they believed that losing righteousness leads to worry.
Therefore, they controlled music with moderation,
and established sons according to the Way.
As for those who rely on slander and flattery to serve their ruler,
they are not worthy of being trusted.
Now, Your Lordship uses the schemes of slanderous men,
Listening to the words of a rebellious man leads to
deposing the elder and establishing the younger.
Your minister fears that later generations, taking advantage of your mistake to further their own wickedness,
will depose the younger and establish the elder to achieve their own benefit.
May your lord consider this!"
The Duke did not listen.
When Duke Jǐng died,
the Tián clan killed Jūn Tú and established Yáng Shēng;
killed Yáng Shēng and established Jiǎn Gōng;
killed Jiǎn Gōng and seized the state of Qí.
1.12 《Duke Jǐng Intends to Execute the Prayer Officials to Apologize, but Yàn Zǐ Counsels Against It》
Duke Jǐng suffered from skin diseases and malaria,
which did not cease for a full year.
He summoned Huì Qiǎn,
Liángqiū Jù, and Yàn Zǐ and asked them,
saying:
"My illness is severe.
I have sent Shǐ Gù and Zhù Tuó to patrol the mountains, rivers, ancestral temples,
and sacrificial animals and jade objects,
nothing has been left unprepared,
their number always being more than that of the late Lord Huán,
Lord Huán once, and I twice.
The illness does not cease, but intensifies,
I wish to kill these two men to appease the Supreme God,
is that permissible?"
Huì Qiǎn,
Liángqiū Jù said:
"Kě." Àn Zǐ bù duì. "Acceptable." Àn Zǐ did not reply.
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
"Àn Zǐ hé rú?" "What does Àn Zǐ think?"
Àn Zǐ yuē: "Jūn yǐ zhù wèi yǒu yì hū?" Àn Zǐ said: "Does Your Lordship consider praying to be beneficial?"
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
"Rán." "Yes."
"Ruò yǐ wéi yǒu yì, "If you consider it beneficial,
zé zǔ yì yǒu sǔn yě. then cursing must also be detrimental.
Jūn shū fǔ ér yuǎn fú, Your Lordship neglects your advisors and distances yourself from those who remonstrate,
zhōng chén yōng sè, loyal ministers are blocked,
jiàn yán bù chū. and words of advice cannot get through.
Chén wén zhī, Your servant has heard it said,
jìn chén hēi, 'If close ministers are silent,
yuǎn chén yīn, and distant ministers are mute,
zhòng kǒu shuò jīn. Jīn zì Liáo Shè yǐ dōng, many mouths can melt metal.' Now, from east of Liáo Shè,
Gū Yóu yǐ xī zhě, to west of Gū Yóu,
cǐ qí rénmín zhòng yǐ, the number of people is great,
bǎixìng zhī jiù yuàn fěibàng, the common people's resentments, complaints, and slander,
zǔ jūn yú Shàngdì zhě duō yǐ. cursing Your Lordship to God on High are numerous.
Yī guó zǔ, If one state curses,
liǎng rén zhù, and two people pray,
suī shàn zhù zhě bù néng shèng yě. even the best prayer cannot prevail.
Qiě fú zhù zhí yán qíng, Furthermore, if a prayer directly states the situation,
zé bàng wú jūn yě; then it slanders our lord;
yǐnnì guò, if it conceals transgressions,
zé qī Shàngdì yě. then it deceives God on High.
Shàngdì shén, If God on High is divine,
zé bù kě qī; then He cannot be deceived;
God is not divine,
praying is also of no benefit.
I hope you will consider this.
Otherwise, punishing the innocent,
is why the Xià and Shāng dynasties were destroyed."
The Duke said:
"You have skillfully resolved my doubts,
add the cap!"
He ordered Huì Qiàn not to manage the affairs of the state of Qí,
Liángqiū Jù not to manage the affairs of guests,
and concurrently assigned them to Yàn Zǐ.
Yàn Zǐ declined,
but could not refuse the order,
accepted the position of minister, withdrew,
took charge of the government,
and after a month the Duke's illness improved.
The Duke said:
"In the past, my late lord Duke Huán,
considered Guǎn Zǐ powerful,
and gave him cities and grain,
to supply the fresh meat for the ancestral temple,
and reward his loyal ministers,
thus there were many loyal ministers.
You are now a loyal minister,
I ask to grant you Zhōu Kuǎn."
He declined, saying:
"Guǎn Zǐ had one excellence,
which Yīng is not as good at;
he had one flaw,
which Yīng cannot bear to do,
that is, to lavishly nourish the ancestral temple."
In the end, he declined and did not accept.
1.13 *Duke Jǐng is angry that the prayer of the border official is disrespectful, and Yàn Zǐ admonishes him*
Gōng (Duke) said:
"It is understandable if a humble subject offends the ruler,
but how can a ruler offend the people?"
Yàn Zǐ (晏子) remonstrated, saying:
"Your Lordship is mistaken!
If someone distant is at fault,
those close to him punish him.
If someone of low status is at fault,
those of high status punish him.
If the ruler offends the people,
who will punish him?
May I ask:
Jié (桀) and Zhòu (紂),
were they punished by the ruler?
Or were they punished by the people?"
Gōng (Duke) said:
"I am indeed stubborn."
Thereupon, he bestowed the town of Màiqiū (麥丘) upon the border official as his fief.
1.14 "Jǐng Gōng (景公) Wanted to Have a Chǔ (楚) Shaman Invoke the Five Emperors to Illuminate Virtue, Yàn Zǐ (晏子) Remonstrates"
The Chǔ (楚) shaman Wēi Dào Yì Kuǎn (微道裔款) requested to see Jǐng Gōng (景公),
and attended him for three days,
and Jǐng Gōng (景公) was pleased with him.
The Chǔ (楚) shaman said:
"Your Lordship is the master of bright spirits,
and a ruler of emperors and kings.
Your Lordship has been on the throne for seventeen years,
and the great task has not yet been accomplished,
The bright spirits have not yet arrived.
Please invite the Five Emperors
to illuminate the ruler's virtue."
Jǐng Gōng bowed twice and kowtowed.
The Chǔ shaman said:
"Please tour the nation's borders to observe the positions of the emperors." Reaching Niú Shān, he dared not ascend,
saying:
"The positions of the Five Emperors
are in the south of the state.
Please purify yourself before ascending."
The duke ordered the officials to provide the purification materials at the Chǔ shaman's location,
and Yì Kuǎn oversaw the matter.
Yàn Zǐ heard of this and went to see the duke, saying:
"Is Your Lordship ordering the Chǔ shaman to purify Niú Shān?"
The duke said:
"Yes.
I am inviting the Five Emperors to illuminate my virtue.
The spirits will bestow blessings upon me.
Will it be of some help?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Your words are excessive!
The ancient kings
possessed sufficient benevolence to pacify the world,
and their actions were broad enough to encompass the masses.
The feudal lords supported them,
considering them their leaders,
and the common people turned to them,
regarding them as their parents.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth and the four seasons are harmonious and do not err;
the stars, constellations, sun, and moon are orderly and not chaotic.
When virtue is profound and conduct is broad,
matching the heavens and emulating the seasons,
then one becomes a sovereign worthy of being emperor and king,
and master of the enlightened spirits.
In ancient times, people did not neglect virtuous conduct while engaging in numerous sacrifices,
nor did they disregard their own well-being while relying on shamans.
Now, with government in chaos and conduct perverse,
how can you seek the enlightened virtue of the Five Emperors?
Abandoning the worthy and employing shamans,
how can you seek the qualities of an emperor and king in yourself?
The people do not attain virtue lightly,
blessings do not descend carelessly.
For a ruler to become emperor and king,
is that not difficult?
Alas!
The position of the ruler is high,
but the matters discussed are lowly."
The Duke said:
"Yì Kuǎn, using a Chǔ shaman, instructed me, saying:
'Try to meet and observe him.'
I met him and was pleased,
believing in his way,
and acting according to his words.
Now, you, Master, criticize him;
I request to expel the Chǔ shaman and detain Yì Kuǎn."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"The Chu shaman must not be sent out." The Duke said:
"Why?"
He replied:
"If the Chu shaman is sent out,
the lords will surely receive them.
If Your Lordship believes in them,
and is excessively influenced internally,
you will be unaware;
if you send them out to influence the lords externally,
it would be unbenevolent.
Please send the Chu shaman east and detain Yì Kuǎn."
The Duke said:
"Agreed."
Therefore, it is said:
Send the Chu shaman east,
and detain Yì Kuǎn in the state.
1.15 《Duke Jǐng intended to sacrifice to the Spirit Mountain and the River God to pray for rain, Yàn Zǐ admonished him》
In Qí there was a great drought lasting a long time.
Duke Jǐng summoned his ministers and asked:
"It has not rained for a long time,
and the people are beginning to show signs of hunger.
I have sent people to divine,
and the misfortune lies in the high mountains and broad waters.
I wish to reduce the taxes and levies to sacrifice to Spirit Mountain,
is that permissible?"
The ministers did not respond.
Yàn Zǐ stepped forward and said:
"It is not permissible! Sacrificing to it will be of no benefit.
For Líng Shān is inherently formed of stone as its body,
and of grass and trees as its hair.
If Heaven does not rain for a long time,
its hair will be scorched,
its body will be hot.
Would it alone not desire rain?
What benefit is there in sacrificing to it?"
Jǐng Gōng said, "Not so.
I wish to sacrifice to Hé Bó, is that permissible?"
Yàn Zǐ said, "It is not permissible!
Sacrificing to it will be of no benefit. For Hé Bó takes water as his kingdom,
and fish and turtles as his people.
If Heaven does not rain for a long time,
the springs will flow downwards,
and all the rivers will dry up.
The kingdom will perish,
the people will be destroyed.
Would he alone not desire rain?
What benefit is there in sacrificing to him!"
Jǐng Gōng said, "What should be done now?"
Yàn Zǐ said, "If Your Lordship truly avoids the exposure of palaces and halls,
and shares the worries of Líng Shān and Hé Bó,
perhaps it will be fortunate and rain!"
Thereupon, Jǐng Gōng went out to the fields and exposed himself.
After three days, Heaven indeed sent down a great rain,
and the people all were able to plant in time.
Jǐng Gōng said, "Excellent!
The words of Yàn Zǐ,
how can they be without use!
They are truly virtuous."
1.16 "Duke Jǐng Desires to Perpetually Possess the Joy of Ruling a State, Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him"
Duke Jǐng was observing at the Zī River,
standing idly with Yàn Zǐ.
The Duke sighed deeply and said:
"Alas!
If the state could be preserved for a long time and passed on to my descendants,
would that not be joyful?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Yīng has heard that enlightened rulers do not establish themselves in vain,
and the people do not come without reason.
Now, Your Lordship has been disrupting the state with your policies,
and abandoning the people with your actions for a long time already,
and yet you wish to preserve it;
is that not difficult?
Yīng has heard that
those who can preserve a state for a long time
are those who can end well.
When feudal lords stand together,
those who can end well are the leaders;
when scholars study together,
those who can end well are the teachers.
In the past, our former ruler, Duke Huán,
when he was employing the worthy and praising virtue,
a perishing state relied on him to survive,
a state in danger looked to him for peace,
Therefore, the people rejoiced in his governance and the world esteemed his virtue.
He undertook distant expeditions to punish the violent.
Those who labored did not complain.
He drove those within the seas to come to court to the Son of Heaven,
and the feudal lords did not resent it.
At that time,
the conduct of an accomplished ruler could not surpass his.
But when he died and declined,
becoming negligent in virtue and indulging in pleasure,
becoming immersed in women and relying on Shù Diāo for counsel,
therefore the people suffered from his governance,
and the world criticized his conduct.
Therefore, he died in the barbarian palace and was not buried,
and worms emerged and were not gathered.
At that time,
the deaths of Jié and Zhòu could not have been more wicked.
The "Book of Poetry" says:
"There is none who does not have a beginning,
but few who have an end."
Those who cannot end well
do not fulfill their role as ruler.
Now you, my lord, treat the people like bandits and enemies,
see good as if avoiding heat,
disrupt governance and endanger the worthy,
are sure to be opposed by the masses,
indulge your desires upon the people,
and cruelly punish those below,
I fear it will reach your own person.
Yīng is old in years,
and cannot wait for your commands, my lord.
If my actions cannot be changed,
then I will hold my staff until I die."
1.17 《Jǐng Gōng Dēng Niú Shān Bēi Qù Guó Ér Sǐ Yàn Zǐ Jiàn》 (Duke Jing Ascends Mount Niu, Laments Leaving the State and Dying, and Yanzi Admonishes)
Duke Jǐng toured Mount Niú,
and facing north, overlooking the city of his state,
he wept, saying:
"How can I copiously leave this place and die!"
Ài Kǒng and Liángqiū Jù both followed him and wept.
Yàn Zǐ alone laughed at the side.
The Duke wiped his tears and looked at Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"I am filled with sorrow on this tour today,
Kǒng and Jù both follow me and weep,
but you alone laugh.
Why is that?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"If the worthy constantly guarded it,
then Tài Gōng and Duke Huán would have constantly guarded it.
If the brave constantly guarded it,
then Duke Zhuāng and Duke Líng would have constantly guarded it.
If these past lords constantly guarded it,
then how could my lord have obtained this position and stand here?
Because they successively occupy it,
and successively leave it,
until it came to your lordship,
and you alone weep for it,
this is unkind.
An unbenevolent ruler sees one thing,
a flattering minister sees two,
this is why this minister secretly laughs to himself."
1.18 "Duke Jǐng's Excursion to Mount Gōng, with Three Mistakes in One Day, Yàn Zǐ's Admonition"
Duke Jǐng went on an excursion to Mount Gōng,
and facing north, gazed at the state of Qí, saying:
"Alas!
If the ancients had not died,
what would it be like?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"In the past, the Supreme God considered the death of man as good,
the benevolent rest,
and the unbenevolent are subdued.
If the ancients had not died,
Duke Dīng and Duke Tài would possess the state of Qí,
Huán, Xiāng, Wén, and Wǔ would all assist them,
and you, my lord, would wear a bamboo hat and coarse clothes,
holding a hoe and crouching, walking among the fields,
who would have time to worry about death!"
The Duke angrily changed his expression,
displeased.
Not long after, Liáng Qiū Jù arrived riding six horses,
The Duke said:
"Who is that?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"It is Jù."
The Duke said:
"How do you know?"
He said:
"To gallop at full speed in the great heat,
the worst is the death of the horse,
the lighter is the injury to the horse.
If not Jù, who would dare to do such a thing!"
The Duke said:
"Jù is in harmony with me!"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"This is what is called being the same.
What is called harmony is,
if the ruler tastes sweetness, then the minister tastes sour,
if the ruler tastes blandness, then the minister tastes saltiness.
Now Jù, if the ruler tastes sweetness, he also tastes sweetness,
this is what is called being the same,
how can it be called harmony!"
The Duke angrily changed his expression,
displeased.
Before long,
at sunset,
the Duke looked to the west,
and saw a comet.
He summoned Bó Cháng Qiān
and ordered him to pray to dispel it.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"It is not possible!
This is a teaching from Heaven.
When the energies of the sun and moon,
and wind and rain are not timely,
When a comet appears,
Heaven shows it to the people as a sign of disorder.
Therefore, it is proclaimed as an ominous omen
to warn against irreverence.
Now, if you, my lord, were to establish written policies and accept remonstrance,
and seek out wise and virtuous men,
even if the comet did not disappear,
the star would vanish of its own accord.
Now, you, my lord, indulge in wine and excessive pleasure,
your government is not well-ordered and you are lenient with petty people,
you are close to slanderers and fond of actors,
you dislike written advice and distance yourself from wise and virtuous men.
How could you have time to worry about the comet!
An eclipse will soon appear again."
The Duke angrily changed his expression,
displeased.
When Yàn Zǐ passed away,
the Duke went out
and stood behind a screen, saying:
"Alas!
In the past, I followed the Master and traveled to Gōng Fù.
The Master would criticize me three times in one day.
Now, who will criticize me?"
1.19 "Duke Jǐng Travels on a Cold Road
and Does Not Care for a Corpse; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him."
Duke Jǐng traveled on a cold road and saw a dead, exposed corpse,
but remained silent and did not inquire.
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 admonished, saying:
"In the past, when my late lord, Duke Huán 桓公, went on a journey,
if he saw someone hungry, he would give them food,
if he saw someone sick, he would give them money.
He made sure that his commands did not exhaust the people's strength,
and his levies did not burden the people.
When the late lord was about to travel,
the people were all delighted and said,
'Will our lord be fortunate enough to visit our village?'
Now you travel to the cold and muddy roads,
oppressing the people within forty *lǐ* 里,
exhausting their wealth is not enough to cover the levies,
exhausting their strength is not enough to meet the demands of the corvée.
People are hungry, cold, and starving,
with corpses visible one after another,
and you do not inquire about it.
This is a failure of the ruler's way.
When wealth is depleted and strength is exhausted,
the people below have nothing with which to be close to those above.
When arrogance and extravagance prevail,
those above have nothing with which to be close to those below.
When those above and those below are alienated from each other,
and ruler and subject have no affection,
this is the reason why the Three Dynasties declined.
Now you are acting in this way,
and Yīng 嬰 fears for the danger to the ducal clan,
and believes it will be a blessing for those of other surnames."
The Duke said:
"Indeed! To care for those above and forget those below,
to rely heavily on extracting wealth and forget the people,
my sin is great indeed."
Thereupon, he collected the unburied corpses,
and distributed grain to the people.
According to the people within forty *lǐ*
who had not submitted to governance that year,
the Duke did not go out for three months.
1.20 *Jǐng Gōng Yī Hú Bái Qiú Bù Zhī Tiān Hán Yàn Zǐ Jiàn* (Duke Jǐng Wears a White Fox Fur Coat, Unaware of the Cold Weather; Yàn Zǐ Advises)
During the time of Duke Jǐng,
it snowed for three days without stopping.
The Duke wore a white fox fur coat
and sat on the steps at the side of the hall.
Yàn Zǐ entered to see him,
and after standing for a while,
the Duke said, "Strange!
It has snowed for three days, yet the weather is not cold."
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Is the weather not cold?"
The Duke laughed.
Yàn Zǐ said,
"I, Yīng, have heard that the wise rulers of old were full and knew of the hunger of the people,
were warm and knew of the cold of the people,
were at ease and knew of the toil of the people.
Now, you, my lord, do not know this."
The Duke said,
"Good! I, the lonely one, have received your instruction."
He then ordered the release of fur coats and the distribution of grain to those who were hungry and cold.
Those seen on the roads,
do not ask their village;
those seen in the neighborhoods,
do not ask their family;
according to the state's calculations,
do not mention their names.
Those scholars who were already employed received double monthly stipends,
and the sick received double annual stipends.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said:
"Yànzǐ is able to make clear what he desires,
and Jǐnggōng is able to carry out his good deeds."
1.21 《Duke Jǐng Marvels at Mars Dwelling in Xū and Not Leaving; Yànzǐ Admonishes》
During the time of Duke Jǐng,
Mars dwelled in Xū,
and did not leave for a full year.
The Duke marveled at this,
and summoned Yànzǐ to ask him, saying:
"I have heard that,
those who do good deeds, Heaven rewards them,
and those who do evil deeds, Heaven punishes them.
Mars,
is a heavenly punishment.
Now it remains in Xū,
who is it that should bear this?"
Yànzǐ said:
"Qí should bear it."
The Duke was displeased,
He said:
"There are twelve great states in the world,
all called feudal lords.
Why does Qí alone deserve this title?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Emptiness,
Qí is also a wilderness.
Moreover, the disasters that come down from heaven
are firmly rooted in wealth and strength.
Goodness is not employed,
decrees are not carried out,
worthy men are sent far away,
slanderers flourish instead,
the people harbor hatred and resentment,
and pray for blessings for themselves.
Eating meagerly and forcefully,
what harm is there in advancing to death!
Therefore, the arrangement of constellations is disorderly,
changing stars have sharp points,
the planet Mars retrogrades,
inauspicious stars are nearby,
worthy men are not employed,
how can one not perish!"
The Duke said:
"Can it be removed?"
He replied:
"What can be brought about can be removed; what cannot be brought about cannot be removed."
bùkě zhì zhě bùkě qù."
The Duke said:
"What should I, the lonely one, do about this?"
He replied:
"Why not eliminate the prisons where unjust accusations accumulate,
and let the people return to their fields;
distribute the wealth of the officials,
and bestow it upon the people;
aid the orphaned and widowed, and respect the elderly.
If you do these things,
all evils can be removed,
why would this calamity alone remain?"
The Duke said:
"Good."
After carrying this out for three months,
Mars moved.
1.22 "Duke Jǐng Preparing to Attack Sòng Dreams of Two Angry Men, Yànzǐ Advises"
Duke Jǐng raised an army to attack Sòng,
the army passed Mount Tài,
the Duke dreamed he saw two men standing and angry,
their anger was very great.
The Duke was afraid,
woke up, closed the gates and summoned a dream interpreter,
who arrived.
The Duke said:
"Tonight I dreamed of two men standing and angry,
I do not know what they said,
their anger was very great,
I still remember their appearance,
remember their voices."
The dream interpreter said:
"The army passed Mount Tài without performing sacrifices,
therefore the god of Mount Tài is angry.
Please quickly summon the praying scribes to sacrifice to Mount Tài, and then it will be alright."
The Duke said:
"Yes."
The next day,
Yàn Zǐ went to court and had an audience,
and the Duke informed him about what the dream interpreter had said.
The Duke said:
"The dream interpreter's words were:
'When the army passed Tài Shān but did not perform sacrifices,
therefore the god of Tài Shān is angry.'
Now I will send someone to summon a priest and historian to make offerings to it."
Yàn Zǐ lowered his head for a moment,
and replied:
"The dream interpreter does not understand,
this is not the god of Tài Shān,
it is the ancestor of Sòng, Tāng and Yī Yǐn."
The Duke was doubtful,
thinking it was the god of Tài Shān.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If the Duke doubts it,
then I, Yīng, will describe the appearance of Tāng and Yī Yǐn.
Tāng had fair skin and was tall,
his face had a beard,
"A face that is sunken above and full below,
a body that is stooped and a voice that is raised."
The Duke said:
"Yes,
that's it."
"Yī Yǐn was dark and short,
with disheveled hair and a beard,
a face that was full above and sunken below,
a body that was hunched and a voice that was low."
The Duke said:
"Yes,
that's it.
What now?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Now, Tāng,
Tài Jiǎ,
Wǔ Dīng, and Zǔ Yǐ,
were all great rulers of the world,
and should not be without descendants.
Now, only the state of Sòng remains,
and you are attacking it,
therefore Tāng and Yī Yǐn are angry,
please dismiss the army to pacify Sòng."
Duke Jǐng did not listen,
and ultimately attacked Sòng.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Attacking a guiltless state,
to anger the enlightened spirits,
It is not easy to proceed to continue accumulating.
Advancing the army is close to making mistakes.
These are things that *Yīng* does not understand.
If the army really advances,
the army will surely have calamity."
The army will advance and camp again,
the drums will be destroyed, and the general will die.
The Duke then took his leave from *Yàn Zǐ*,
disbanded the army,
and did not ultimately attack *Sòng*.
1.23 "Duke *Jǐng* Did Not Return to the State After Hunting for Eighteen Days, *Yàn Zǐ* remonstrated."
Duke *Jǐng* hunted at *Shǔ Liáng*,
for eighteen days and did not return.
*Yàn Zǐ* went from the capital to see the Duke.
When he arrived,
his clothes and hat were not proper.
Without changing his clothes and hat,
he hastened to the hunt.
The Duke saw *Yàn Zǐ* from afar,
got down and hastily tied his belt, saying:
"Master, why are you in such a hurry?
Could it be that something has happened to the state?"
*Yàn Zǐ* replied,
"Is it not urgent!
Although,
*Yīng* wishes to reply something.
The people of the state all think of you, my lord, as being at peace in the wilderness but not at peace in the state,
好獸而惡民， [hǎo shòu ér è mín,] Loving animals but hating the people,
毋乃不可乎？」 [wú nǎi bù kě hū?] Isn't that perhaps unacceptable?"
公曰： [gōng yuē:] The Duke said:
「何哉？ [hé zāi?] "What is the matter?
為夫婦獄訟之不正乎？ [wèi fūfù yù sòng zhī bùzhèng hū?] Is it because the lawsuits between husband and wife are not handled justly?
則泰士子牛存矣； [zé Tài shì Zǐniú cún yǐ;] Then the senior officer of Tài, Zǐniú, is present.
為社稷宗廟之不享乎？ [wèi shèjì zōngmiào zhī bù xiǎng hū?] Is it because the sacrifices to the gods of the land and grain and the ancestral temple are not properly offered?
則泰祝子游存矣； [zé Tài zhù Zǐyóu cún yǐ;] Then the chief prayer of Tài, Zǐyóu, is present.
為諸侯賓客莫之應乎？ [wèi zhūhóu bīnkè mò zhī yìng hū?] Is it because the feudal lords and guests are not being properly attended to?
則行人子羽存矣； [zé xíngrén Zǐyǔ cún yǐ;] Then the protocol officer, Zǐyǔ, is present.
為田野之不辟， [wèi tiányě zhī bù bì,] Is it because the fields are not being reclaimed,
倉庫之不實乎？ [cāngkù zhī bù shí hū?] and the granaries are not being filled?
則申田存焉； [zé Shēntián cún yān;] Then Shēntián is present.
為國家之有餘不足聘乎？ [wèi guójiā zhī yǒuyú bùzú pìn hū?] Is it because the state does not adequately employ those with surplus or insufficient resources?
則吾子存矣。[zé wú zi cún yǐ.] Then you, my son, are present.
寡人之有五子， [guǎrén zhī yǒu wǔ zǐ,] I have five ministers,
猶心之有四支， [yóu xīn zhī yǒu sìzhī,] just as the heart has four limbs.
心有四支， [xīn yǒu sìzhī,] When the heart has four limbs,
故心得佚焉。 [gù xīn dé yì yān.] the heart can thus be at ease.
今寡人有五子， [jīn guǎrén yǒu wǔ zǐ,] Now I have five ministers,
故寡人得佚焉， [gù guǎrén dé yì yān,] so I can be at ease.
豈不可哉！」 [qǐ bùkě zāi!"] How can that be unacceptable!"
晏子對曰： [Yàn Zǐ duì yuē:] Yàn Zǐ replied:
「嬰聞之， [Yīng wén zhī,] "I have heard that,
與君言異。 [yǔ jūn yán yì.] it is different from what you say.
若乃心之有四支， [ruò nǎi xīn zhī yǒu sìzhī,] If indeed the heart has four limbs,
而心得佚焉， [ér xīn dé yì yān,] and the heart can thus be at ease,
則可； [zé kě;] then that is acceptable.
To order the four limbs to be without purpose for,
eighteen days,
is it not too long!"
The Duke then stopped hunting and returned.
1.24 "Duke Jǐng Wanted to Execute the Countryman Who Startled the Bird, Yàn Zǐ Interceded"

bù yì yí hū!"

1.25 "Duke Jǐng's Beloved Horse Died, He Wanted to Execute the Horse Feeder, Yàn Zǐ Interceded"
Duke Jǐng ordered someone to raise his beloved horse,
it suddenly died of illness.
The lord was enraged
and ordered men to take up knives and dismember the horse keeper.
At this time, Yàn Zǐ was attending him.
Those on the left and right held knives and advanced.
Yàn Zǐ stopped them and asked the lord, saying:
"May I ask, in ancient times, when Yáo and Shùn dismembered people,
from which part of the body did they begin?"
The lord, terrified, said:
"Begin with me."
So, he did not dismember him.
The lord said: "Hand him over to the prison."
Yàn Zǐ said: ,
"Your servant requests to enumerate his crimes for you,
so that he knows his sins,
and then he can be delivered to prison."
The lord said:
"You may."
Yàn Zǐ enumerated them, saying:
"You have three crimes:
The lord ordered you to care for the horse, and you killed it,
that is crime number one, deserving of death;
moreover, you killed the lord's most cherished horse,
that is crime number two, deserving of death;
causing the lord to kill a man because of a horse,
the people will certainly resent our ruler when they hear of this,
the lords will certainly look down on our state when they hear of this,
you killed the lord's horse,
causing resentment to accumulate among the people,
and weakening our military strength in the eyes of neighboring countries,
this is the third crime deserving death.
Now you will be handed over to the prison."
The lord sighed and said:
Release him."

2.2 *Jǐng Gōng yù shā fàn suǒ ài zhī huái zhě Yàn Zǐ jiàn* (Duke Jing Wishes to Kill Someone Who Damaged His Beloved Locust Tree, and Yàn Zǐ Advises Against It)
Duke Jǐng had a locust tree that he loved,
and ordered officials to guard it carefully,
He planted a locust tree in the county.
He issued an order saying, "Those who harm the locust tree will be punished,
those who damage it will be put to death."
There was someone who didn't hear the order,
and, being drunk, harmed it.
The Duke heard of this and said,
"He violated my order first."
He ordered an official to arrest him,
and furthermore, to punish him.
The man's daughter went to bid farewell at the house of Yàn Zǐ,
and pretended, saying, "I, a lowly woman of the outer city walls,
request to have a word with the Prime Minister,
unable to restrain my desires,
I wish to be included amongst his concubines."
Yàn Zǐ heard this,
and laughed, saying,
"Is he indulging in lust?
Why would I, in my old age, engage in such pursuit?
However, there must be a reason for this."
He ordered her to be brought inside.
The woman entered the gate,
Yàn Zǐ saw her and
said,
"Strange! She has deep sorrow."
He went forward and asked her,
saying,
"What is it that you are worried about?"
She replied, "The lord planted a locust tree and declared an ordinance,
To violate it is to be punished;
to injure it is to die.
My father was unkind,
and did not hear the order;
he became drunk and violated it,
so the officials will impose punishment on him.
I have heard that
enlightened rulers, when governing a state and establishing policies,
do not decrease rewards,
nor increase punishments,
and furthermore, do not harm public law with private resentment,
do not injure the people for the sake of birds and beasts,
do not injure birds and beasts for the sake of grasses and trees,
and do not injure crops for the sake of wild grasses.
Now my lord wants to kill my father because of trees,
leaving me, a lone concubine,
this order will be practiced among the people and become law in the country.
However,
I have heard that
brave warriors do not bully the solitary and helpless with their numerous strength,
and enlightened and benevolent rulers do not defy what is right to do what they desire.
This is like governing fish and turtles oneself,
only removing what is smelly and stinky.
Mèi Mò lived next to people in the granary market,
and taught people to sit properly and rigidly.
Now, if your lord issues an order to the people
that can indeed be a law for the state,
and benefit later generations,
If that is the case, then my father's death was justified,
and it is fitting that I, his concubine, should collect his remains. How terrible!
But now the decree is not so;
because of the trees,
my father is condemned.
I fear this will damage the way officials are inspected
and harm the reputation of our enlightened ruler.
When neighboring states hear of this,
they will all say that our ruler loves trees and despises people. How can this be allowed?
I hope that the prime minister will examine my words and punish those who violate the law."
Yàn Zǐ said, "This is terrible!
I will speak of this to the ruler on your behalf."
He sent someone to escort her home.
The next day, at the early court session,
he reported to the duke, saying:
"Yīng has heard that
to exhaust the people's wealth and resources to indulge one's desires is called tyranny;
to exalt amusements
and make one's authority rival the ruler is called rebellion;
to inflict punishments and death that do not fit the crime is called wickedness.
These three are the great calamities for guarding the state.
Now, Your Grace, you exhaust the people's wealth and resources
to satisfy your extravagant culinary desires,
to amplify the music of bells and drums,
to maximize the splendor of palaces,
performing the greatest of tyrannies.
You exalt amusements,
issuing decrees protecting beloved pagoda trees,
Those riding past gallop,
those walking past hurry,
(your) majesty resembles a ruler,
to oppose it shows understanding;
those who offend the pagoda tree are punished,
those who damage the pagoda tree are killed,
the punishment and killing are disproportionate,
a deep harm to the people.
Your Lordship enjoys the state,
your virtuous conduct has not been seen by the masses,
yet three decrees are prominent in the state,
Yīng fears that you cannot govern the country and its people."
The Duke said:
"If not for the Great Officer teaching me, the little one
would almost have committed a great crime, burdening the state;
now you, Great Officer, have taught me,
this is a blessing for the state,
the little one accepts the order."
Yàn Zǐ withdrew,
the Duke ordered the hastening of abolishing the guard duty for the pagoda trees,
uprooting the trees placed in the districts,
abolishing the laws about damaging the pagoda trees,
and releasing the prisoners who offended the pagoda trees.
2.3 Duke Jǐng pursued and arrested someone who cut bamboo, and Yàn Zǐ admonished.
Duke Jǐng planted bamboo
and ordered officials to carefully guard it.
The Duke went out
Passing by,
there was someone cutting bamboo.
The Duke pursued him with a chariot,
caught and detained him,
intending to punish him.
Yàn Zǐ entered and met with him,
saying:
"Has Your Grace also heard of my former lord, Duke Dīng?"
The Duke said: "How was he?"
Yàn Zǐ said: "Duke Dīng attacked Qūchéng,
conquered it,
kept its wealth, and released its people.
The Duke himself oversaw the matter daily.
There was a cart carrying a dead person out.
The Duke found it strange
and ordered an official to inspect it.
Inside, there was gold and jade.
The official requested to kill the person
and confiscate the person's possessions.
The Duke said:
'To subdue a city with soldiers
and surround wealth with the masses is inhumane.
Moreover, I have heard that
a ruler
should be generous and kind to the people
and not personally pursue executions.'
He ordered them to release him."
The Duke said: "Good!"
Yàn Zǐ retired,
and the Duke ordered the release of the prisoners who were cutting bamboo.
2.4 *Jǐng Gōng Intends to Kill Soldiers Whose Training in Fighting Has Not Succeeded; Yàn Zǐ Advises Against It*
Jǐng Gōng ordered the soldiers to train in fighting,
which took place during the twelfth month when the ice was thick, and it was cold.
Many of the people were suffering from cold and hunger,
and the training was not successful.
The Duke angrily said,
"Kill two of the soldiers for me."
Yàn Zǐ said, "Yes."
After a short while, Yàn Zǐ said,
"In the past, when our former lord, Zhuāng Gōng, attacked Jìn,
the campaign resulted in the death of four soldiers.
Now you are ordering the killing of two soldiers,
which is half the number of the former campaign."
The Duke said, "Yes!
It is my fault."
He ordered the cessation of the execution.

Zhòng Ní wén zhī, Zhòng Ní heard of this,
He sighed and said:
"The good ministers of ancient times

When in court, they criticized their ruler's wrongdoings;

2.6 "Jǐng Gōng Intended to Beautify Chánglái, Yàn Zǐ Advised Against It"
Jǐng Gōng was building Chánglái, intending to beautify it.
A wind and rain arose.
Gōng and Yàn Zǐ entered and sat down to drink wine,
enjoying the music in the hall.
At the height of the drinking, Yàn Zǐ sang a song, saying:
"The ears of grain cannot be harvested,
the autumn wind arrives and they all fall;
the wind and rain do not kill them,
but the excessive building destroys them."
After the song, he looked around and shed tears,
bent his body and danced.
Gōng approached Yàn Zǐ and stopped him, saying:
"Today, Master has bestowed a warning upon me,
it is my fault."
Thereupon he stopped the drinking and dismissed the labor,

2.7 "Duke Jǐng Builds a Long Road in Zōu, Yàn Zǐ Advises"
Duke Jǐng built the Terrace of Lù Qǐn,
and for three years it did not cease;
he then engaged in the construction of Cháng Lái,
and for two years it did not cease;
he then constructed a long road for Zōu.
Yàn Zǐ advised, saying:
"The people's strength is exhausted!
Will Your Grace not let them rest?"
Duke Jǐng said: "The road is about to be completed,
I ask to complete it and then let them rest."
He replied:
"A ruler who exploits the people's wealth
will not gain their benefit;
one who exhausts the people's strength
will not gain their happiness.
In the past, King Líng of Chǔ built the Inclined Palace,
and for three years it did not cease;
he then built the Terrace of Zhāng Huá,
and for five years it did not cease;
and he then engaged in the construction of Gān Xī, for eight years,
until the people's strength was insufficient and it ceased on its own.
King Líng died in Gān Xī,
and the people did not return with their ruler.
Now Your Grace does not follow the righteousness of enlightened rulers,
but follows in the footsteps of King Líng,
Yīng was afraid that Your Lordship would engage in tyrannical acts against the people,
and would not experience the joy of prolonged enjoyment.
It would be better to stop it."
The Duke said, "Good!
If it weren't for you, Master,
I, this solitary one, would not have realized how deeply I have offended the people."
Thereupon, he ordered that the ruins not be left to decay,
and that the remaining materials not be collected.
He cut the planks and left the site.
2.8 *Jǐng Gōng Chūn Xià Yóu Liè Xīng Yì Yàn Zǐ Jiàn*
Duke Jǐng indulged in hunting in the spring and summer and also initiated the construction of a large terrace.
Yàn Zǐ remonstrated, saying,
"Undertaking construction projects and
engaging in hunting during the spring and summer
deprives the people of their farming season.
The state will become empty and weak.
It is not permissible."
Duke Jǐng said,
"I have heard that when the minister is virtuous, the state is well-governed,
and when the subject is loyal, the ruler can be at ease.
My years are few,
and I wish to indulge in what pleases me,
to fulfill what I desire.
You should rest."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"In the past, King Wén of Zhōu did not dare to indulge in pleasure trips in the fields,
Therefore, the state is prosperous and the people are at peace.
Chǔ Língwáng 楚靈王 did not abandon the campaigns at Gānxī 乾溪,
and he constructed the Terrace of Zhānghuá 章華之臺,
and the people rebelled against him.
Now, if Your Lordship does not change,
you will endanger the state and altars of the soil and grain,
and become a laughingstock to the feudal lords.
Your servant has heard that loyalty does not shun death,
and remonstrance does not avoid punishment.
If Your Lordship does not listen to your servant,
your servant will depart.”
Jǐng Gōng 景公 said:
“Yes, yes,
I will call off the levies.”
Before long,
Cháo Wéi Jiǒng 朝韋冏 dismissed the conscripted laborers and sent them home.
2.9 Jǐng Gōng 景公 Hunts, Rests, and Sits on the Ground; Yànzǐ 晏子 Uses His Mat to Remonstrate
Jǐng Gōng 景公 hunted, rested,
and sat on the ground to eat.
Yànzǐ 晏子 arrived later,
and his attendants pulled up reeds to use as a mat.
The Duke was displeased,
and said:
“I, your lord, sit on the ground without a mat,
none of you others have a mat,
and yet you alone pull up grass and sit on it, why is that?”
Yànzǐ 晏子 replied:
"I have heard that one does not sit on a mat when wearing armor and sitting in formation,
nor when dealing with lawsuits,
nor when a corpse is in the hall;
these three things all involve worry.
Therefore, I dare not sit on a mat while serving you in a state of worry."
The Duke said,
"Good."
He ordered his attendants to lower the mats, saying,
"The ministers may all sit on mats;
I, too, shall sit on a mat."
2.10 *Jǐng Gōng Hunts, Encounters a Snake and Tiger, Deeming it Ominous; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him*
Duke Jǐng went out hunting.
Going up a mountain, he saw a tiger.
Going down to a swamp, he saw a snake.
Upon returning, he summoned Yàn Zǐ and asked him,
"Today I went out hunting.
Going up a mountain, I saw a tiger.
Going down to a swamp, I saw a snake.
Could this be what is called an inauspicious omen?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"A state has three inauspicious omens;
these things are not among them.
To have a worthy man but not recognize him is one inauspicious omen;
to recognize him but not employ him is the second inauspicious omen;
to employ him but not entrust him with responsibility is the third inauspicious omen.
What is called inauspicious is like this.
Now, going up a mountain and seeing a tiger—that is the tiger's home.
Going down to a swamp and seeing a snake—that is the snake's burrow.
To see them in the tiger's home and the snake's burrow,
what is inauspicious about that!"
2.11 *Jǐng Gōng Builds a Terrace; Upon its Completion, He Wishes to Make a Bell; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him*
Duke Jǐng built a terrace.
The terrace completed,
and then he wanted to make a bell. Yànzǐ admonished him, saying:
"He who rules a state does not rejoice in the sorrow of the people.
If the ruler cannot control his desires,
having already built a terrace,
now wanting to make a bell,
this is a double levy upon the people;
the people will surely be sorrowful.
To levy the sorrow of the people
and take it as joy is inauspicious
and not the way to rule a state."
The duke then stopped.
2.12 *Jǐng Gōng wèi Tài Lǚ Chéng jiāng yǐ Yàn Xiǎng, Yànzǐ Jiàn* (Duke Jing Builds the Tài Lǚ Palace, Completes it, and Plans to Feast, Yànzǐ Admonishes)
Jǐng Gōng built the Tài Lǚ palace,
and said to Yànzǐ:
"I wish to feast with you, sir."
He replied:
"To feast without first sacrificing to the former ruler is not in accordance with ritual."
The duke said: "What is the point of ritual?"
He replied:
"Ritual is the guide for the people.
If the guide is disordered, the people will be lost.
"Disrupting discipline and losing the people is a dangerous path."
The Duke said, "Good."
And then he sacrificed accordingly.
2.13 《Duke Jǐng Makes Shoes Adorned with Gold and Jade, Yàn Zǐ Admonishes》
Duke Jǐng made shoes with yellow gold straps,
adorned with silver, connected with pearls,
with fine jade laces,
their length was one foot,
he wore them in the twelfth month to attend court.
Yàn Zǐ went to court, the Duke greeted him,
the shoes were heavy, he could barely lift his feet,
and asked:
"Is it cold?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Why does Your Lordship ask about the coldness of the sky?
Ancient sages made clothing
light and warm in winter,
light and cool in summer.
Now, shoes of gold and jade,
worn in the twelfth month,
are heavily cold.
Shoes that are heavy and unmeasured
are excessive burden,
they lose the natural feelings of life.
Therefore, the artisans of Lǔ do not know the moderation of cold and warmth,
the measure of lightness and heaviness,
To harm the upright and give birth to evil,
that is the first crime;
to make garments that are not constant,
and thus be laughed at by the feudal lords,
that is the second crime;
to use wealth without merit,
and thus cause resentment among the people,
that is the third crime.
I request that he be detained and the officials be made to assess him."
The Duke said:
"He suffered, please release him."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"It is not permissible.
I have heard that
those who afflict themselves to do good, their rewards are great;
those who afflict themselves to do wrong, their crimes are severe."
The Duke did not answer.
Yàn Zǐ went out and
ordered the officials to detain the Lǔ craftsman,
ordered men to send him to the border,
so that he could not enter.
The Duke removed his shoes
and never wore such garments again.
2.14 *Duke Jǐng Desires to Attract the Feudal Lords by Wearing the Garments and Living in the Dwelling of a Sage-King; Yàn Zǐ remonstrates*
Duke Jǐng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"I desire to wear the garments of a sage-king
and live in the dwelling of a sage-king;
"If this is so, will the feudal lords come?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"If they emulate his frugality, then it's acceptable;
but emulating his clothing and dwellings is of no benefit.
The Three Kings had different attire but still ruled;
it wasn't through their attire that they attracted the feudal lords.
It was through sincerity in loving the people,
and resoluteness in doing good,
that the world cherished their virtue and returned to their righteousness.
It's good that their clothing is frugal, and the masses are pleased.
As for hats and crowns, enough to cultivate reverence,
one shouldn't strive for their adornment.
As for clothing, enough to cover the body and ward off the cold,
one shouldn't strive for its beauty.
Clothing shouldn't strive for fineness in every corner and hem,
hats shouldn't have complicated angles and twisted patterns.
Clothing worn on the body should not be of mixed colors,
headwear should not be elaborately carved.
Furthermore, in ancient times there was one who wore patched clothing and a twisted collar and yet ruled the world.
His righteousness lay in loving life and hating killing,
being frugal with the higher classes and admiring the lower classes.
The world did not pay homage to his attire,
but all returned to his righteousness.
In ancient times, there was one who lived in wooden nests and caves and did not despise them,
giving rather than taking.
The world did not pay homage to his dwellings,
but all returned to his benevolence.
When the Three Dynasties made clothing,
To act with reverence is beneficial.
Headgear is sufficient to cultivate reverence,
and it is not cumbersome.
Clothing is sufficient to practice purity,
and it does not hinder movement.
The lightness or heaviness of clothing is convenient for the body,
and the expense of using resources is in accordance with the people's welfare.
The reason they did not build raised nests
was to avoid the wind;
the reason they did not build cave dwellings
was to avoid dampness.
Therefore, the construction of the Míngtáng (Bright Hall)
ensured that dampness from below
could not reach it;
and cold and heat from above
could not penetrate it.
Earthwork was not embellished,
and woodwork was not carved,
demonstrating frugality to the people.
But when it declined,
the extravagance of clothing excessively venerated,
the beauty of palaces excessively avoided dampness,
expending a great deal of labor,
and wasting a great deal of resources,
making the ruler an enemy of the people.
Now, if Your Lordship wants to emulate the clothing of the Sage Kings,
do not emulate their specific designs,
but emulate their frugality,
Then, although governance may not be achieved,
it may perhaps still be beneficial.
Now, Your Lordship exhausts the height of terraces and pavilions,
and pursues the depth of dirty ponds without stopping.
You strive for skillful carvings
and the splendor of ornate patterns without satisfaction,
thus, you are making yourself an enemy of the people.
If my concerns are realized,
I fear for the danger of the state,
and Your Lordship is not being fair.
Your Lordship wishes to summon the feudal lords,
is that not difficult?
Your Lordship's words are excessive."
2.15 *Duke Jing's Self-Conceit in the Nobility of his Attire and Leisure, Yàn Zǐ's Admonition*
Duke Jing built the Western Qu Huang,
its depth was axle-breaking,
three *rèn* in height,
with horizontal wood carvings of dragons and snakes,
and standing wood carvings of birds and beasts.
The Duke wore a *fǔ fú* robe,
and plain embroidered trousers,
one garment with all five colors;
wearing a ball jade girdle and a *qiě* cap,
with disheveled hair,
he stood facing south, arrogant.
Yàn Zǐ saw him,
and the Duke said, "In the past, how was the hegemony of Zhongfu?"
Yàn Zi lowered his head
and was not right. The Duke then said,
"In the past, what was the hegemony of Guǎn Wénzhòng like?" Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I have heard that,
only the Dí people compare themselves to dragons and snakes,
now you, my lord, lay wooden dragons and snakes horizontally,
erect wooden birds and beasts,
and thus your chamber is already complete,
what leisure do you have for hegemony!
Moreover, you praise the beauty of palaces,
and boast of the splendor of clothing,
with one garment having all five colors,
wearing jade balls on your belt, with disheveled hair,
and thus your chamber is already magnificent,
the ruler of ten thousand chariots,
but with your heart set on evil,
the spirit of the ruler is lost,
with whom can you plan for hegemony?" The Duke descended from the hall and approached Yàn Zǐ, saying,
"Liáng Qiūjù and Yì Kuǎn told me of the completion of the chamber,
and thus I secretly donned this attire,
to laugh with them,
and also to involve you, Master,
I ask to change the chamber and change the attire and respectfully listen to your commands,
is that acceptable?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Those two men are leading you, my lord, with evil,
how can you know the right way!
Moreover, if you do not cut a tree from its roots,
then shoots will grow again,
Gōng hé bù qù èr zǐ zhě, [Why doesn't the lord dismiss these two?]
wú shǐ ěrmù yín yān." [Don't let your ears and eyes be corrupted."]
2.16 *Jǐng Gōng wèi jù guān cháng yī yǐ tīng cháo Yàn Zǐ jiàn* [Duke Jing Makes Large Hats and Long Robes to Attend Court, Yàn Zǐ remonstrates]
Jǐng Gōng wèi jù guān cháng yī yǐ tīng cháo, jí shì jīn lì, [Duke Jing made large hats and long robes to attend court, glaring and standing stiffly,]
rì yàn bù bà. [and did not dismiss the court until late in the day.]
Yàn Zǐ jìn yuē: [Yàn Zǐ stepped forward and said:]
"Shèng rén zhī fú zhōng, [“The clothing of a sage is moderate,]
tuì ér bù zǎng, kěyǐ dǎo zhòng, [humble and not ostentatious, so that it can guide the masses.]
qí dòng zuò, [His actions,]
tuì shùn ér bù nì, [are humble and compliant and not contrary,]
kěyǐ fèng shēng, [so that they can nourish life.]
shì yǐ xià jiē fǎ qí fú, [Therefore, the lower people all imitate his clothing,]
ér mín zhēng xué qí róng. [and the people strive to learn his appearance.]
Jīn jūn zhī fú, [Now, your clothing,]
zǎng huá bù kěyǐ dǎo zhòng mín, [ostentatious and showy, cannot guide the masses.]
jí shì jīn lì, [Glaring and standing stiffly,]
bù kěyǐ fèng shēng, [cannot nourish life.]
rì yàn yǐ, [It is late in the day,]
jūn bù ruò tuō fú jiù yàn." [You would be better off taking off your robes and returning to leisure.”]
Gōng yuē: [The Duke said:]
"Guǎ rén shòu mìng." [“I accept your instruction.”]
Tuì cháo, [He withdrew from the court,]
suì qù yī guān, bù fù fú. [and then removed his clothing and hat and never wore them again.]
2.17 *Jǐng Gōng cháo jū yán xià bù yán Yàn Zǐ jiàn* [Duke Jing Maintains a Strict Court, the Lower Officials Do Not Speak, Yàn Zǐ remonstrates]
Yàn Zǐ cháo, fù yú Jǐng Gōng yuē: [Yàn Zǐ went to court and said to Duke Jing:]
"Is the court stern?"
The Duke said:
"If the court is stern, what harm does it cause to governing the state?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"If the court is stern, then inferiors will not speak;
if inferiors do not speak, then superiors will hear nothing.
If inferiors do not speak, then I would call it muteness;
if superiors hear nothing, then I would call it deafness.
Deafness and muteness, if they don't harm the state, what does!
Moreover, combine the smallness of a shēng and dòu to fill a granary;
combine coarse strands of floss silk to make a curtain.
The height of Mount Tài,
is not from a single stone;
it is high after accumulating low things.
Now, those who govern the world,
do not rely on the words of a single scholar;
there may be acceptance without use,
but how can there be rejection without acceptance!"
2.18 *Jǐng Gōng Climbs the Lù Qǐn Terrace, Does Not Finish, and Is Displeased; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him*
Duke Jǐng climbed the Lù Qǐn Terrace,
but could not finish and rested on the steps.
He angrily changed countenance,
displeased,
and said:
"Who made such a high terrace?
It greatly afflicts people!"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If you, my lord, wish to be frugal in your personal life, do not build high,
so that when the people praise your highness, they will not be punished.
Now, if you build high, they are punished for following;
if you build low, they are also punished.
May I venture to ask, is it permissible to treat the people like this?
In ancient times, the construction of palaces
was sufficient to provide for life,
and was not considered extravagant.
Therefore, they were frugal in their personal lives
and attuned to the people's needs.
But when the Xià dynasty declined,
its king Jié 背棄 (bèiqì) deserted virtuous conduct
and built xuán (璿) chambers and jade gates.
When the Yīn dynasty declined,
its king Zhòu 紂 built the Qīng (傾) Palace and the Língtái (靈臺).
Those who built low and narrow were punished,
and those who built high and large were rewarded.
Because of this, the nation was engulfed.
Now, you, my lord, are punishing both those who build high
and those who build low.
This is worse than the kings of Xià and Yīn!
The people's strength is exhausted,
and they cannot escape punishment.
I am afraid that the state will be lost
and that you, my lord, will not be able to enjoy [the offerings]!"
The duke said,
"Excellent!
I myself know that I have truly wasted wealth and burdened the people,
Thinking that he had achieved nothing,
and then resenting him for it,
this is my fault!
Without your (Ànzǐ's) teaching,
how could I possibly protect the state!"
Thereupon he descended, bowed twice,
and did not ascend the platform after all.
2.19 Duke Jǐng Ascends the Lùqǐn Platform to Gaze Upon the State and Sighs, and Ànzǐ Admonishes Him.
Duke Jǐng and Ànzǐ ascended the Lùqǐn (Roadside Dwelling) platform to gaze upon the state. The Duke looked sad and sighed, saying:
"If my descendants could possess this generation after generation,
would that not be wonderful!"
Ànzǐ said:
"I have heard that an enlightened ruler must devote himself to rectifying his government
in order to benefit the people,
and only then can his descendants enjoy it.
The *Book of Odes* says: 'Did King Wǔ not exert himself,
leaving plans for his descendants,
in order to give rest and protection to his sons?'
Now, Your Lordship dwells in ease and sloth,
and your oppressive policies harm the people daily,
and yet you utter such words.
Is this not going too far!"
The Duke said:
"Then who in later generations will hold Qí (state)?"
He replied:
"When an ox used for plowing dies,
Husbands and wives weep, but they are not blood relatives;
it is because the benefit is great.
If you want to know who holds the state of Qí,
then it is those who benefit from it, isn't it?"
The Duke said:
"Yes, how can it be changed?"
He replied:
"Change it with good government.
Now your bulls and horses are old in the stalls,
unable to bear service;
the carriages are worm-eaten in the great gates,
unable to be ridden;
clothes, furs, short jackets, and trousers,
are decayed in storage,
unable to be worn;
the sauces and preserved meats are rotten, unable to be sold;
the wines and sweet wines are sour, unable to be drunk;
the grain in the granaries is piled up and cannot be eaten;
and you heavily levy from the people,
but do not distribute it to relieve the starving people.
To hoard wealth and not use it
is inauspicious. If wealth is unguarded and lost,
then its retribution will surely arrive.
Secondly, if one is ignorant of the loss of wealth,
neglects it and does not distribute it to others,
then the people will surely take it upon themselves to distribute it.
Therefore, a ruler is better off seeking from himself
than seeking from others."
2.20 *Jǐng Gōnglù Qǐn Tái Chéng Féng Yú Hé Yuàn Hézàng Yànzi Jiàn Ér Xǔ*
Jǐng Gōng built a raised platform for the sleeping quarters (*lù qǐn zhī tái*).
Féng Yúhé encountered a bereavement,
and met Yànzi on the road,
bowing twice before his horse.
Yànzi alighted from his carriage and greeted him,
saying:
"Why do you command Yīng?"
He replied,
"The mother of Yúhé has died,
and the auspicious spot for her burial is under the eaves of the *lù qǐn* platform,
so I wish to request permission to bury her bones there."
Yànzi said,
"Alas!
This is difficult!
Even so, I, Yīng, will try to plead your case.
