I, the寡人 (guǎrén, a humble form of "I" used by rulers), have received your gift. May I ask how to pacify the country and its people?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I have heard that being arrogant towards the great and looking down upon the small will endanger the country,
being negligent in listening and excessive in collecting taxes
will cause the people to scatter.
Serving the great and nurturing the small
are the instruments for pacifying the country;
listening attentively and practicing frugality
are the methods for winning the people."
4.15 "Yàn Zǐ's Mission to Jìn: Duke Píng of Jìn Asks How the Former Ruler Won the People; Yàn Zǐ Responds with the Analogy of a Beautiful Deep Pool."
Yàn Zǐ was on a mission to Jìn.
Duke Píng of Jìn entertained him in a decorated chamber.
After it was quiet,
Yàn
Duke Píng asked him,
saying:
"In the past, how did my late ruler win the people?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"You, my lord, entertain our ruler and
extend your kindness to the envoys. Your attendants are at your side,
I am afraid and do not know how to answer."
Duke Píng said,
"I have heard of you, Grand Master, many times.
Now I have the opportunity to meet you,
and I wish to hear it to the end."
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Chén wén jūnzǐ rú měi,
a deep pool accommodates him,
the multitude returns to him,
like fish having something to rely on,
enjoying the utmost pleasure of swimming;
if the deep pool dries up,
the fish will flow away,
alas, that which went forth, was it not rain?
It cannot return."
The Duke further asked, saying:
"May I ask, which is more virtuous, Duke Zhuāng or the current ruler?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"The actions of the two rulers are different,
I dare not know."
The Duke said:
"The royal house has correctness,
the feudal lords have arbitrary rule,
therefore I desire to hear your, Grand Master's, words."
He replied:
"The former ruler, Duke Zhuāng, did not like to stay quietly,
he delighted in restraining food and drink, did not like bells and drums,
he loved weapons and making war, his soldiers shared the same hunger, thirst, cold, and heat,
the ruler's strength exceeded the measure of men,
he had one fault he could not stop,
therefore he could not avoid calamity.
Now, your ruler has great palaces,
beautiful terraces and pavilions, to avoid hunger, thirst, cold, and heat,
he fears disaster and reveres ghosts and spirits,
"Your virtues are sufficient to consume your own life,
but not sufficient to extend to your descendants."
4.16 *Jìn Píng Gōng Asks About the Extent of Qí Ruler's Virtuous Conduct; Yànzi Answers with Small Virtues*
Yànzi was sent as an envoy to Jìn.
Jìn Píng Gōng asked him,
"How is the virtuous conduct of your ruler,
in terms of its height and depth?"
Yànzi answered with "small virtues."
The Duke said,
"No, I am not asking about small virtues,
but asking about the height and depth of your ruler's virtuous conduct."
Yànzi respectfully replied,
"When feudal lords associate, they are introduced and meet each other,
and there are things hidden in their words.
Your lord gave me instructions in person, and your servant has nothing to hide.
My ruler has nothing to be praised."
Píng Gōng respectfully bid him farewell,
bowed twice, and returning, said,
"How close I was to making a mistake!
Who says the Qí ruler is unworthy!
An upright scholar is indeed in his court."
4.17 *Jìn Shū Xiàng Asks How Qí is Faring; Yànzi Answers that Qí's Virtue is Declining and the People are Returning to the Tián Clan*
Yànzi was visiting Jìn,
and Shū Xiàng attended the banquet and conversed with him.
Shū Xiàng said,
"How is Qí faring?"
Yànzi replied,
"This is the end of an era, and I do not know.
Will Qí become the property of the Tián clan!”
Shū Xiàng said:
“What do you mean?”
Yàn Zǐ said:
“The ruler has abandoned his people,
and they are returning to the Tián clan.
Qí's old four measures were:
*dòu*, *qū*, *fǔ*, *zhōng*;
four *shēng* make a *dòu*,
four of each [of the smaller measures]
to make a *fǔ*,
and ten *fǔ* make a *zhōng*.
The Tián clan's three measures
all increase by one [unit],
so the *zhōng* is very large.
They lend using the family measure,
and collect using the public measure.
Timber from the mountains is like that from the market,
and is not added to the mountain stores,
fish, salt, oysters and clams
are not added to the sea stores.
The people contribute three parts of their strength,
with two parts going to the public,
and they clothe and feed themselves with one part;
the public stores accumulate rotten things,
while the old and young freeze and starve;
in the cities of the state,
shoes are cheap but amputation is expensive;
The people suffer greatly,
perhaps they will be given respite.
In the past, the Yīn people carried out inappropriate executions,
slaughtering the people without ceasing.
Wén Wáng kindly favored the Yīn masses,
providing aid to the helpless.
Therefore, the world turned to him,
the people had no personal preferences, it was virtue that granted him power.
Now, the ducal house is arrogant and tyrannical,
while the Tián family is kind and benevolent.
They love the people like parents,
and the people flock to them like flowing water.
If you wish to avoid gaining the people, where will you hide?
Their elder,
Zhí Bǐng,
Yú Suì, Bó Xì,
and their minister, Hú Gōng Dà Jī,
are already in Qí.”
Shū Xiàng said:
“Even our ducal house
is in its declining years.
Warhorses are not harnessed,
the ministers have no military expeditions,
the ducal carriages have no riders, the soldiers have no leaders;
the common people are exhausted and worn out, the palaces are increasingly extravagant,
corpses from starvation can be seen on the roads, while the women are excessively wealthy;
when the people hear the duke's orders, they flee as if from bandits and enemies;
Luán Xì,
Xū Yuán,
Gū Xù, Qìng Bó,
have been reduced to menial servants; government is confined to private households,
the people have nothing to rely on,
and the ruler does not repent daily, indulging in pleasure to drown his sorrows;
how long will the ducal house, in its baseness, last!"
The inscription on the cauldron of calumny says:
'Shining brightly at dawn, yet future generations are indolent.'
How much more so when one is unrepentant every day – how can this last long!"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"In that case, what will you do?"
Shū Xiàng said:
"Human efforts are exhausted,
one can only wait for Heaven!
The ducal clan of Jìn is all but finished.
Xī has heard
that when the ducal house is about to decline,
its lineage branches will fall off first,
then the ducal line will follow.
Of Xī’s clan, eleven branches,
only the Yángshé lineage remains.
Moreover, Xī has no son.
The ducal house lacks moderation.
If I am lucky enough to die,
how can I hope to receive sacrifices?"
4.18 *Shū Xiàng asks Yàn Zǐ about how the virtue of Qí has declined, and Yàn Zǐ replies with 'advancing without losing loyalty and retreating without losing integrity'*.
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"Qíguó's virtue has declined,
what will you do now?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I, Yīng, have heard that serving an enlightened ruler means
to exhaust one's heart and strength to the end of one's life.
If one's ability is insufficient, then one should withdraw,
and not hold onto salary through deception.
Serving a slothful ruler means
to live leisurely to the end of one's life.
If one's strength is insufficient, then one should leave,
and not hold onto a precarious position through flattery.
Moreover, I, Yīng, have heard that when a virtuous person serves a ruler,
in advancement, one does not lose loyalty, and in withdrawal, one does not lose integrity.
Not to compromise in order to conceal one's loyalty
can be called not losing loyalty;
not to hold onto benefit to harm one's integrity
can be called not losing integrity."
Shū Xiàng said,
"Excellent!
The *Book of Poetry* has it,
'Advancing and retreating are both difficult.'
Is this what it means!"
4.19 *Shū Xiàng Asks How the Actions of Upright Officials and Evil People Are, and Yàn Zǐ Answers with How to Make Those Below Obey in Adversity*
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ,
"What is the righteousness of upright officials
and the conduct of evil people like?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Upright officials, in a position of power overseeing the masses, do not act out of personal bias.
行於國足養而不忘故； Xíng yú guó zú yǎng ér bù wàng gù; When active in a state, have sufficient sustenance and do not forget your origins;
通則事上，使卹其下， tōng zé shì shàng, shǐ xù qí xià, When successful, serve your superiors and ensure they care for their subordinates;
窮則教下，使順其上； qióng zé jiāo xià, shǐ shùn qí shàng; When unsuccessful, teach your subordinates to be obedient to their superiors;
事君盡禮行忠， shì jūn jìn lǐ xíng zhōng, Serve your ruler with utmost propriety and act with loyalty,
不匄爵祿， bù gài jué lù, do not beg for titles and stipends,
不用則去而不議。 bù yòng zé qù ér bù yì. if not employed, leave without complaint.
其交友也， Qí jiāo yǒu yě, As for their friendships,
論身義行， lùn shēn yì xíng, discuss personal righteousness and conduct,
不為苟戚， bù wéi gǒu qī, do not become intimate for petty reasons,
不同則踈而不悱； bù tóng zé shū ér bù fěi; if opinions differ, distance yourselves without resentment;
不毀進於君， bù huǐ jìn yú jūn, Do not slander others to advance yourselves before the ruler,
不以刻民尊於國。 bù yǐ kè mín zūn yú guó. Do not oppress the people to elevate the state.
故用於上則民安， Gù yòng yú shàng zé mín ān, Therefore, if employed by superiors, the people are at peace,
行於下則君尊； xíng yú xià zé jūn zūn; if acting among subordinates, the ruler is respected;
故得眾上不疑其身， gù dé zhòng shàng bù yí qí shēn, therefore, gaining the support of the masses, superiors do not doubt them,
用于君不悖於行。 yòng yú jūn bù bèi yú xíng. being employed by the ruler, they do not betray their conduct.
是以進不喪己， Shì yǐ jìn bù sàng jǐ, Therefore, in advancement, they do not lose themselves,
退不危身， tuì bù wēi shēn, in retreat, they do not endanger themselves;
此正士之行也。 cǐ zhèng shì zhī xíng yě. this is the conduct of an upright gentleman.
邪人則不然， Xié rén zé bù rán, The wicked are not like this:
用於上則虐民， yòng yú shàng zé nüè mín, When employed by superiors, they abuse the people,
行于下則逆上； xíng yú xià zé nì shàng; when acting among subordinates, they defy their superiors;
事君苟進不道忠， shì jūn gǒu jìn bù dào zhōng, Serving their ruler, they seek only advancement and do not speak of loyalty,
交友苟合不道行； jiāo yǒu gǒu hé bù dào xíng; in friendship, they seek only agreement and do not speak of conduct;
持諛巧以正祿， chí yú qiǎo yǐ zhèng lù, They use flattery and cunning to secure their salaries,
比姦邪以厚養； bǐ jiān xié yǐ hòu yǎng; they associate with the treacherous and wicked to enrich themselves;
矜爵祿以臨人， jīn jué lù yǐ lín rén, they boast of their titles and stipends to lord over others,
夸禮貌以華世； kuā lǐ mào yǐ huá shì; they exaggerate propriety to deceive the world;
If they are not trusted by their superiors, they will engage in frivolous criticism;
if they are not sincere with their friends, they will be fond of slander.
Therefore, if employed by their superiors, the people will worry;
if they act among their inferiors, the ruler will be in danger.
Thus, serving the ruler brings them close to punishment,
associating with friends brings them close to trouble,
gaining favor with superiors leads to humiliation,
their way of life heads toward criminal penalty.
Therefore, employed by superiors, they are executed;
acting among inferiors, they are assassinated.
Thus, making connections leads to disgrace,
causing trouble leads to danger;
this is the behavior of wicked people."
4.20 "Shū Xiàng asks about the meaning of serving a ruler and how a recluse should conduct himself; Yàn Zǐ responds that a great wise man has no favorites."
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ,
"The principles of serving a ruler,
and the meaning of how a recluse should conduct himself, what are they like?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"The principles of serving a ruler are:
intelligence and consideration sufficient to secure the state,
a great reputation sufficient to guide the people,
gentleness and harmony sufficient to embrace the masses,
not being incorruptible to gain a name for oneself with superiors,
not betraying the people in one's actions - this is the highest.
To be pure in governing oneself,
not embellishing faults to seek precedence,
not slandering or flattering to seek advancement,
not favoring what is private,
Not falsely claiming what one is capable of is second best;
exerting one's strength to uphold one's duty without laziness,
obeying one's superior and daring not to be remiss,
fearing one's superior, hence not acting carelessly,
dreading punishment, hence not avoiding responsibility, is the lowest.
These three are the ethical principles for serving one's ruler.
As for the great sages,
there is no difference between being in retirement and being employed;
they simply adapt to the needs of the time.
Then there are those called "jūnzǐ 君子" (gentlemen),
whose abilities are insufficient to aid their superiors,
whose retirement is not beneficial to their superiors,
who manage Táng 唐 gardens and examine simple shoes,
who respectfully care for the orders of their superiors, and only benefit their neighborhoods,
who do not boast in words and are not ashamed of their actions,
these are jūnzǐ 君子.
Those who do not take the ruler as their foundation,
nor the people as their worry,
who do not care for their families internally,
nor care for their associates externally,
who boast in words and are ashamed of their actions,
who confine themselves to hunger and cold,
and are inferior even to their peers,
these are called "eccentric and perverse people,"
whom the enlightened ruler forbids.
Those who, when advanced, cannot reach the standard of their superiors,
and when retired, cannot simply live in seclusion,
who find themselves in dire straits at the doors of the wealthy and greedy,
If one is resolved to engage in the work of the fields,
and yet worries constantly about the unpredictability of success and failure,
finding pleasure in the heart but unable to achieve successful outcomes,
and ultimately failing to complete the task,
such a person is called a subject who occupies a fief in vain,
and should be punished by an enlightened ruler.
If one has wisdom insufficient to benefit the ruler,
and abilities insufficient to serve the people,
but idly remains in position,
this is called disrespecting the ruler.
If one advances without regard for the proper path,
and seeks gain without knowing what is detestable,
this is called a rebellious traitor.
If one contributes nothing to the ruler,
and lacks the ability to serve the people,
while falsely portraying the righteousness of remaining in position,
and promoting a reputation of slighting the ruler,
this is called a disturber of the state.
When an enlightened ruler is on the throne,
these three will not escape punishment."
Shū Xiàng said:
"Virtue and vice are inherent in nature!
I have asked about this many times,
and have never found the answer myself."
4.21 "Shū Xiàng Asks About How To Act In A Chaotic World - Yàn Zǐ Responds By Saying To Consider The People As Fundamental"
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"When the world is in chaos and does not follow the Way,
and the ruler is biased and does not employ righteousness,
To act righteously causes the people to be abandoned;
to act crookedly causes the Way to be abandoned.
Is it right to act righteously and abandon the people?
Or is it better to hold onto the people and abandon the Way?
What about these two courses of action?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I, Yīng, have heard that
to be lowly without losing respect,
to be crooked without losing righteousness,
is to take the people as fundamental.
If one truly holds onto the people,
how could one abandon the Way!
If one truly abandons the people,
how could there be righteous action!"
4.22 "Shū Xiàng Asks, Which Intent is Highest and Which Action is Most Substantial; Yàn Zǐ Replies with Loving the People and Delighting the People"
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ,
"Which intent is highest?
Which action is most substantial?"
He replied,
"No intent is higher than loving the people,
no action is more substantial than delighting the people."
He asked again,
"Which intent is lowest?
Which action is most base?"
He replied,
"No intent is lower than oppressing the people,
no action is more base than harming oneself."
4.23 "Shū Xiàng Asks, What is the Effect of Frugality, Stinginess, and Love on Action? Yàn Zǐ Replies that Frugality is the Way of the Gentleman"
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"What about stinginess and begrudging love in conduct?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Thrift is the way of the gentleman,
stinginess and begrudging love are the conduct of petty people."
Shū Xiàng said:
"What do you mean?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Weighing wealth and poverty to regulate expenditure,
the rich do not hoard gold,
the poor do not borrow or lend; this is called thrift.
Accumulating much but being unable to share with others,
and richly nourishing oneself is called stinginess.
Being unable to share with others,
and also unable to nourish oneself is called begrudging love.
Therefore, thrift is the way of the gentleman;
stinginess and begrudging love are the conduct of petty people."
4.24 《Shū Xiàng Wèn Jūnzǐ zhī Dà Yì Héruò Yàn Zǐ Duì Yǐ Zūn Xián Tuì Bù Xiào》
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"What are the great principles of a gentleman?" Yàn Zǐ replied:
"The great principles of a gentleman are
harmony and accord without dependence,
broad-mindedness without fault-finding,
dignified reverence without craftiness,
gentleness and yielding without measuring,
strict honesty without harshness,
precise conduct without using brightness to defile,
In Qi, valuing talent does not mean abandoning the tired;
being wealthy and noble does not mean being arrogant towards others;
being poor and humble does not mean changing one's conduct;
respecting the virtuous does not mean dismissing the unworthy.
This is the great righteousness of a gentleman."
4.25 《Shū Xiàng Asks Yàn Zǐ Whether Those Who Scorn the World and Delight in Their Occupation Can Follow the Way; Yàn Zǐ Replies That They Are Deluded》
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"When advancing, they cannot serve their superiors;
when retreating, they cannot care for their families;
they scorn the world and delight in their occupation;
they seek fame through withered existence;
they do not doubt what they adhere to.
Can these be said to be capable of following the Way?"
Yàn Zǐ replied, saying:
"I have heard that those who were able to follow the Way in ancient times,
if the world can be straightened, then they straighten it;
if it cannot be straightened, then they yield.
When straightening, they do not lose the proper relationship between superiors and inferiors;
when yielding, they do not lose the principles of benevolence and righteousness.
When the Way is employed, they delight in their occupation along with the world;
when it is not employed, they have something to rely on and return to.
They do not flaunt their superiority to deceive the world,
nor do they seek fame through withered existence.
Therefore, the Way is that by which the world is governed
and the body is made secure.
Now, taking not serving superiors as the Way,
taking not caring for one's family as conduct,
Using "withered and desolate" as a reputation,
if the world practices it, there will be chaos,
if one's self practices it, there will be danger.
Furthermore, between Heaven and Earth,
even above and below, there is decline;
when an enlightened king first establishes himself,
he establishes rules for governing the country;
when governance and education are properly arranged, the people's conduct has principles.
Now, to consider not serving superiors as the Way,
this goes against the decline of Heaven and Earth;
to consider not caring for one's family as conduct,
this contradicts the Way of the former sages;
to use "withered and desolate" as a reputation,
then the world will block the path of governance and education.
Having such enlightenment, one cannot be subordinate;
encountering a chaotic world, one cannot govern chaos.
Speaking like this Way, it is called bewilderment;
acting like this Way, it is called madness.
The bewildered and the mad,
are like unworked wood and stone,
and moral principles have not been embraced."
4.26 "Shū Xiàng Asks, 'Under What Circumstances Can a Person Be Considered Honorable?' Yàn Zǐ Responds with 'Serving the Ruler with Loyalty and Being Filial to Parents'"
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"Under what circumstances can one be considered honorable?"
Yàn Zǐ replied, saying:
"Serve parents with filial piety,
have no regrets about past actions,
serve the ruler with loyalty,
No regrets for past words;
harmonious with brothers,
trustworthy to friends,
not flattering excessively,
not demanding gain;
words and deeds are not contradictory,
actions are not opposite to words;
when in a high position, governing the people is sufficient to honor the ruler; when in a low position, managing personal cultivation is sufficient to transform people. One's person has no faults,
zúyǐ zūn jūn, zài xià lì xiū,
zúyǐ biàn rén, shēn wú suǒ jiù,
one's conduct has no innovations: this can be called glory."
4.27 "Shū Xiàng Asks How a Person Can Preserve Themselves, Yàn Zǐ Answers by Not Desiring Luck"
Shū Xiàng asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"How can a person be said to preserve their person?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Being both intelligent and wise, to preserve oneself,
from morning to night not being lazy, to serve one person.'
Not being presumptuous, not desiring luck,
prioritizing what is difficult and then expecting success,
obtaining things when the time is right is what one should expect,
losing things is not one's fault,
this can be said to be preserving oneself."

4.28 "Zēng Zǐ Asks About Those Who Do Not Admonish Their Superiors or Care for the People But Withdraw to the Mountains and Valleys to Accomplish Righteous Deeds, Yàn Zǐ Asks How Can This Be Accomplished"
Zēng Zǐ asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"In ancient times, were there those who did not admonish their superiors,
Ignoring the people below,
retreating to live in mountain valleys,
is that how one perfects virtuous conduct?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Observing that they themselves have no ability,
and using unwillingness to admonish their superiors as an excuse,
that is called a preposterous idea.
If the ruler is confused and immoral, and virtuous principles are not practiced,
and crooked and biased cliques form,
and worthy people are not employed,
yet the gentlemen do not change their behavior,
but follow the crooked path in order to seek advancement,
therefore there are those who hide and those who do not hide.
If they act according to the law, they are gentlemen,
but as for discussing the ruler,
that is not acceptable.
As for not admonishing the ruler,
ignoring the people below,
and retreating to live in mountain valleys,
Yīng does not understand what about this is how one perfects virtuous conduct."
4.29 *Liángqiū Jù Asks Yàn Zǐ Why He Serves Three Rulers Who Disagree, Yàn Zǐ Replies That One Heart Can Serve a Hundred Rulers*
Liángqiū Jù asked Yàn Zǐ,
"You serve three rulers,
and the rulers do not have the same mind,
yet you all obey them,
do benevolent people really have many minds?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Yīng has heard that
To cherish and love without cease
can be used to employ the common people,
but violence and strength without loyalty
cannot be used to employ even one person.
"With one heart, one can serve a hundred rulers,
but with three hearts, one cannot serve even one ruler."
Zhòng Ní heard this and said:
"Young man, remember this!
Yàn Zǐ is one who serves a hundred rulers with one heart."
4.30《Bǎi Cháng Qiān Asks About the Way of Non-Extinction and Non-Wasting of the Body, Yàn Zǐ Responds with the Gentleman Who Nourishes the World》
Bǎi Cháng Qiān went from Zhōu to Qí,
and saw Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"Qiān is a humble historian of the Zhōu court.
Disregarding my unworthiness, I wish to serve you, a gentleman.
May I ask, if the correct way is practiced directly, it will not be tolerated by the world,
but to conceal the way and act dangerously is unbearable.
How does one ensure that the way is not extinguished
and the body is not wasted?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Excellent!
Are you asking about serving a ruler?
I have heard that,
to hold onto two laws simultaneously
is not acceptable;
to advance lightly and seek superficial agreement
is not trustworthy;
to be straightforward and outspoken without reservation
leads to swift harm;
If a new beginning is made to favor profit,
then there will be no harm.
Moreover, I, Yīng, have heard that the noble men who nourish the world,
do not advance when things are light,
do not retreat when things are heavy,
are restrained in conduct but do not boast,
yield profit but do not exaggerate,
display things but do not monopolize,
observe phenomena but do not force them,
the Way will not perish,
and their persons will not be wasted."
Inner Chapters, Miscellaneous Above
5.1 "Lord Zhuāng was displeased with Yàn Zǐ, Yàn Zǐ sat on the ground and argued with the Lord before returning."
Yàn Zǐ was a minister to Lord Zhuāng,
the Lord was displeased and was drinking,
he ordered Yàn Zǐ to be summoned.
Yàn Zǐ arrived,
entered the gate,
the Lord ordered the musicians to play a song, saying:
"It's over, it's over!
I, the lonely one, cannot be pleased,
what have you come for?"
Yàn Zǐ entered and sat down,
the musicians played three times,
then he realized they were referring to him.
Thereupon he rose,
He sat on the ground facing north.
The Duke said,
"Master, you are a guest at this mat.
Why do you sit on the ground?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Yīng has heard that those who are accused sit on the ground.
Now, I, Yīng, am about to litigate with you, my lord.
How dare I not sit on the ground?
I have heard it said that
when there is a multitude without righteousness,
strength without propriety,
fondness for bravery and hatred of the virtuous,
disaster will surely befall them.
You, my lord, are like this.
Furthermore, if my words are not heeded,
I wish to request permission to leave."
Thereupon, he hurried back home,
the person in charge of his household handed over his fief to the Duke,
and his wealth outside was dispersed in the market.
He said,
"If a gentleman has the ability to benefit the people,
then he advances in rank and salary,
not refusing nobility and wealth.
If he has no ability to benefit the people but lives as a sojourner,
he does not resent poverty and lowliness."
Then he walked east on foot
and tilled the land by the sea.
After several years,
Indeed, there was the disaster of Cuī Zhǔ.
5.2《Duke Zhuang Did Not Employ Yan Zi, Yan Zi Returned His Territory and Retired, Later There Was the Calamity of the Cui Clan》
Yàn Zǐ was a minister of Duke Zhuāng,
when his words were greatly used,
at every court session,
he was granted ranks and increased territory;
but soon he was not employed,
at every court session,
he returned the territory and ranks.
When the ranks and territory were all returned,
he left the court and rode in his carriage,
and sighed sorrowfully,
then laughed.
His servant said:
"Why do your sighs and laughter follow each other so often?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"I sigh because
I grieve that my lord will not escape disaster;
I laugh because
I am glad that I have preserved myself,
I will also not die."
Cuī Zhǔ indeed assassinated Duke Zhuāng,
Yàn Zǐ stood at the gate of Cuī Zhǔ's house,
his follower said:
"Shall we die?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Is it only my lord who is concerned!
"I will die!"
Someone said:
"Will you go?"
He said:
"Is it only my fault!
I will flee!"
Someone said:
"Will you return?"
He said:
"My lord is dead,
where can I return!
Those who rule the people,
how could they oppress the people,
the altars of the soil and grain are what they prioritize;
those who serve the lord,
how could they do it for their own sustenance,
the altars of the soil and grain are what they nourish.
Therefore, if the lord dies for the altars of the soil and grain,
then one should die for them,
if he flees for the altars of the soil and grain,
then one should flee for them;
if the lord dies for himself and flees for himself,
if not his close intimates,
who could bear this.
Moreover, there are those who have lords and assassinate them,
how can I die for him?
And how can I flee for him?
Where could I possibly return!"
The door opened and he entered.
Cuī Zǐ said:
"Why didn't you die?
Why didn't you die?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"When the calamity began,
I was not present;
when the calamity ended,
I was unaware of it;
why should I die?
Moreover, I have heard it said,
that one who takes flight as a course of action,
is not sufficient to preserve his lord;
one who considers death as righteousness,
is not sufficient to establish merit.
How could Yīng be like a maidservant?
To hang oneself and follow him!"
Thereupon he bared his shoulder and removed his hat,
sat down,
used the lord's corpse as a pillow and wept,
rose,
leapt three times, and went out.
People thought Cuī Zǐ would certainly kill him,
but Cuī Zǐ said:
"He is what the people hope for;
releasing him gains the people."
5.3 *Cuī Qìng Coerces the Qí Generals and Great Officers into an Alliance, Yàn Zǐ Does Not Participate*
Cuī Zhù, having already murdered Duke Zhuāng and installed Duke Jǐng,
Cuī Zhù 崔杼 and Qìng Fēng 慶封 assisted each other.
They coerced all the generals, high officials, prominent gentry, and common people at the edge of the pit in the Great Palace,
ordering that none could refuse to swear an oath.
They built an altar three *rèn* high,
and dug a pit beneath it.
A thousand armored soldiers were arranged in layers inside and outside of it.
Those who swore the oath all had to remove their swords to enter.
Only Yàn Zǐ 晏子 refused,
but Cuī Zhù 崔杼 allowed it.
For those who dared to refuse the oath,
a spear was held against their neck,
and a sword pressed against their heart,
forcing them to swear an oath, saying:
"Those who do not side with Cuī 崔 and Qìng 慶 but side with the ducal house,
shall receive misfortune.
If the speech is not rapid
and the finger does not draw blood, they shall die."
Seven people were killed.
Then it came to Yàn Zǐ 晏子.
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 held up a cup of blood,
looked up to the sky and sighed, saying:
"Alas!
Master Cuī 崔 acted without principle
and murdered his lord.
Those who do not side with the ducal house but side with Cuī 崔 and Qìng 慶,
shall receive this misfortune." He bowed his head and drank the blood.
Cuī Zhù 崔杼 said to Yàn Zǐ 晏子:
"If you change your words,
Then I will share the state of Qi with you.
If you do not change your words,
the halberd is already at
your neck,
the sword is already at your heart.
You should consider this!"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"To be coerced by a blade
and lose one's will,
is not courage;
to be swayed by profit
and betray one's ruler,
is not righteousness.
Cuī Zǐ!
Have you not read the *Book of Poetry*?
The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Luxuriant are the kudzu vines,
Spreading over the branches.
Serene and upright is the noble man,
Seeking happiness without turning away.'
Now, should I, Yīng, turn away and seek happiness?
Though a curved blade may hook me,
and straight weapons push me,
Yīng will not change."
Cuī Zhù was about to kill him,
when someone said:
"You must not!
You killed your ruler because he was unprincipled,
Now, if his minister is a man of virtue,
and you proceed to kill him,
it cannot serve as instruction."
Cuī Zǐ therefore released him.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If a high official commits a great act of unkindness,
and does a small act of kindness,
how can there be a balance?"
He hurried out,
grasped the mounting strap and got into his carriage.
His servant was about to gallop off,
but Yàn Zǐ patted his hand and said:
"Go slowly!
Do not lose composure; haste does not necessarily bring life,
slowness does not necessarily bring death.
A deer is born in the wild,
but its life is hung in the kitchen.
Yīng's life is tied to something."
He regulated the pace to proper rhythm and then departed.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"That son of theirs,
gives up his life without changing his resolve."
This refers to Yàn Zǐ.
5.4 *Yàn Zǐ Again Governs Ā and Gained the Trust of Duke Jǐng, Who Entrusted Him with State Affairs*
Duke Jǐng sent Yàn Zǐ to be the steward of Ā.
After three years, reports of his misdeeds were heard throughout the state.
Jǐng Gōng was not pleased and
summoned him and dismissed him.
Yàn Zǐ thanked him and said,
"Yīng knows his mistakes.
I ask to be allowed to govern Ā again.
In three years, praise will certainly be heard throughout the state."
Jǐng Gōng could not bear to do so and
again sent him to govern Ā.
In three years, praise was heard throughout the state.
Jǐng Gōng was pleased,
summoned him, and rewarded him.
Jǐng Gōng asked the reason for this.
He replied,
"In the past, when Yīng governed Ā,
I built footpaths,
and tightened the regulations of the city gates,
and the licentious people hated it.
I promoted thrift, diligence, filial piety, and brotherly love,
and punished laziness and idleness,
and the lazy people hated it.
When deciding cases, I did not avoid
the powerful and noble,
and the powerful and noble hated it.
What the attendants sought,
if lawful, I granted;
if unlawful, I denied, and the attendants hated it.
In serving nobles, I did not exceed the bounds of propriety,
and two slanders arose from within,
三年而毀聞乎君也。 After three years, his defamation was heard by the ruler.
今臣謹更之， Now, I, your subject, carefully changed it,
不築蹊徑， not building small paths,
而緩門閭之政， but relaxing the regulations of the gates and lanes,
而淫民說； and the dissolute people were pleased;
不舉儉力孝弟， not promoting frugality, diligence, filial piety, and brotherly respect,
不罰偷窳， not punishing laziness and indolence,
而惰民說； and the lazy people were pleased;
決獄阿貴強， deciding lawsuits by favoring the noble and powerful,
而貴彊說； and the noble and powerful were pleased;
左右所求言諾， agreeing to whatever the attendants sought,
而左右說； and the attendants were pleased;
事貴人體過禮， serving the noble people with behavior exceeding propriety,
而貴人說。 and the noble people were pleased.
是以三邪譽乎外， Therefore, the three evils praised him outside,
二讒譽乎內， and the two slanderers praised him inside,
三年而譽聞于君也。 and after three years, his praise was heard by the ruler.
昔者嬰之所以當誅者宜賞， Formerly, what Yīng should have been punished for should have been rewarded,
今所以當賞者宜誅， and now what should have been rewarded should be punished.
是故不敢受。」 Therefore, I dare not accept it."
Jǐng Gōng 知 Àn Zǐ 賢， Duke Jǐng knew that Àn Zǐ was wise,
迺任以國政， and then entrusted him with the state affairs,
三年而齊大興。 and after three years, Qí greatly prospered.
5.5 《Jǐng Gōng È Gùrén Àn Zǐ Tuì Guó Luàn Fù Zhào Àn Zǐ》 5.5 "Duke Jǐng Disliked Old Friend Àn Zǐ, Who Resigned and the State Became Chaotic, Then Duke Jǐng Summoned Àn Zǐ Again"
Jǐng Gōng 與 Àn Zǐ 立于曲潢之上， Duke Jǐng and Àn Zǐ stood on the winding pond,
Àn Zǐ 稱曰： Àn Zǐ said:
「衣莫若新， "Clothes are best when new,
People are not as good as those who are old and familiar."
The Duke said:
"Clothes are new,
indeed good;
people are old,
and know each other's feelings."
Yànzi returned,
and had someone bearing a load deliver a message to the Duke, saying:
"Yīng is old and feeble and incompetent,
please do not make me perform the duties of the strong."
The Duke governed the state himself,
and became weaker than Gāo Guó,
and the people were in great disorder.
The Duke was afraid
and summoned Yànzi again.
The lords feared his power,
and Gāo Guó submitted to his government.
Fields were cultivated and reclaimed,
and there was not enough land for sericulture and animal husbandry.
Silk was obtained from Yān,
horses were grazed in Lǔ,
and tributes were presented to the court.
Mòzǐ heard of this and said:
"Yànzi knows the Way,
and Duke Jǐng knows his straits."
5.6 《During the Famine in Qí, Yànzi Relied on the Lù Qǐn Project to Help the People》
During the time of Duke Jǐng there was a famine,
and Yànzi requested to distribute grain to the people,
The Duke did not permit it.
He intended to build a terrace at the road-side sleeping quarters.
Yàn Zǐ ordered the officials to increase the wages,
move the foundation far away,
delay the work,
and not rush it.
After three years, the terrace was completed and the people were enriched,
therefore the ruler delighted in excursions,
and the people had enough to eat.
The gentleman said:
"Politically, Yàn Zǐ only wanted to distribute grain to the people,
but if that was not possible,
then he relied on this matter to subtly influence politics."
5.7 《Duke Jǐng Desired to Demolish the Eastern Gate Embankment, Yàn Zǐ Said It Was Not Possible to Change the Ancient Ways》
Duke Jǐng ascended the eastern gate embankment,
the people carried him on their single-layered clothes up there.
The Duke said:
"This greatly harms the hooves of cattle and horses!
Why not lower it by six *chǐ*?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, my former lord Duke Huán,
was an enlightened ruler,
and Guǎn Zhòng was a worthy minister.
With a worthy minister assisting an enlightened ruler,
the eastern gate embankment remained intact.
If the ancients did not do it,
there must be a reason.
In early years, floodwaters would reach
Entering the Guǎng Gate,
one immediately descends six chi (feet);
if the people of the countryside were to prevent descending six chi,
then there would be no uniformity.
This is what is meant by "In ancient times, importance was placed on changing the ancient norms."
This is what it means."
5.8 *Jǐng Gōng* Pitied the Hungry; *Yàn Zǐ* Praised the Basis of Governing to Extend His Meaning
*Jǐng Gōng* was enjoying himself at the Shòu Palace,
and saw an old man carrying firewood,
who had a hungry look.
The Duke felt sorrow for him,
and with a sigh, ordered an official to provide for him.
*Yàn Zǐ* said:
"Your servant has heard that
delighting in the worthy and pitying the unworthy
is the foundation of protecting the state.
Now, Your Lordship loves the old,
and your kindness extends to all;
this is the foundation of governing the state."
The Duke smiled,
and had a joyful expression.
*Yàn Zǐ* said:
"The sage kings saw the worthy and delighted in them,
saw the unworthy and pitied them.
Now, I request that those elderly and weak who are not provided for,
and the widowers and widows who have no home,
be considered and given appropriate positions."
The Duke said:
"Yes."
Thereupon, the old and weak were provided for,
and the widowed and unmarried had homes.
5.9 《Duke Jǐng Probes Bird Nestlings and Returns Them Because They Are Weak, Yàn Zǐ Praises His Respect for the Old and Young in Celebration》
Duke Jǐng probed a bird nestling,
the nestling was weak,
so he returned it. Yàn Zǐ heard of this,
and entered the palace to see him at an unusual hour. The Duke was sweating and apprehensive,
Yàn Zǐ said:
"What is your lord doing?"
The Duke said: "I probed a bird nestling,
the nestling was weak,
so I returned it."
Yàn Zǐ retreated a few steps, faced north, bowed twice, and congratulated him, saying:
"My lord possesses the way of a sage king!"
The Duke said:
"I, the lonely one, probed a bird nestling,
the nestling was weak,
so I returned it,
what about this is in accordance with the way of a sage?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Your lord probed a bird nestling,
the nestling was weak,
and you returned it,
this is respect for the old and young.
Our lord is benevolent and loving,
extending even to birds and beasts,
how much more so to people!
This is the way of a sage king."
5.10 《Duke Jǐng Sees a Beggar on the Road, Yàn Zǐ Hints that the Duke Should Provide for Him》
Duke Jǐng saw an infant begging on the road,
The Duke said:
"This child has no home!"
Yànzǐ replied:
"Your Lordship exists,
how can he have no home?
Have an official care for him,
and report it when it is done."
5.11 "Duke Jǐng is Ashamed of the Humiliation by Yuè Guì, He Does Not Hold Court, Yànzǐ Praises His Uprightness and Asks for Him to be Rewarded"
Duke Jǐng at midday,
with disheveled hair,
riding a six-horse chariot,
driving a woman out of the main gate,
Yuè Guì struck his horses and turned them back,
saying:
"You are not my lord."
The Duke was ashamed and did not hold court.
Yànzǐ saw an attendant approaching slowly and asked:
"Why does Your Lordship not hold court?"
The attendant replied:
"Formerly, Your Lordship at midday,
with disheveled hair,
riding a six-horse chariot,
driving a woman out of the main gate,
Yuè Guì struck his horse and turned it back,
saying,
"You are not my lord."
The duke was ashamed and turned back,
failing to go out,
and therefore did not hold court."
Yàn Zǐ entered to see him.
Jǐng Gōng said,
"Formerly I, your unworthy servant, was at fault,
with disheveled hair,
riding a six-horse chariot,
to go out the main gate,
Yuè Guì struck the horse and turned it back,
saying,
"You are not my lord."
Thanks to the favor of you, my esteemed minister,
I was able to lead the people to guard the ancestral temple,
but now I am humiliated by Yuè Guì,
bringing disgrace to the state,
can I still be on par with the other lords?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Do not be upset about it!
I have heard that when those below do not offer straightforward criticism,
it means the one above is concealing his true nature;
when the people mostly avoid speaking frankly,
it means the ruler has arrogant behavior.
In ancient times, when an enlightened ruler was above,
those below mostly offered straightforward criticism;
君上好善，[Your lord is fond of goodness,]
民無諱言。[the people will have no words to hide.]
今君有失行，[Now, if your lord has misdeeds,]
刖跪直辭禁之，[Yuè Guì directly remonstrates and forbids them,]
是君之福也。[this is a blessing for your lord.]
故臣來慶。[Therefore, your servant has come to offer congratulations.]
請賞之，[I request that he be rewarded,]
以明君之好善；[to demonstrate your lord's fondness for goodness;]
禮之，[and that he be treated with respect,]
以明君之受諫。」[to demonstrate your lord's acceptance of remonstrance."]
公笑曰：[Gōng laughed and said:]
「可乎？」["Is that acceptable?"]
晏子曰：[Yàn Zǐ said:]
「可。」["It is acceptable."]
於是令刖跪倍資無征，[Thereupon, he ordered that Yuè Guì's wealth be doubled and that he be exempted from taxes,]
時朝無事也。[and that he attend court even when there was no business.]
5.12 《Jǐng Gōng Yè Cóng Yàn Zǐ Yǐn Yàn Zǐ Chēng Bù Gǎn Yǔ》[5.12 "Duke Jǐng Follows Yàn Zǐ to Drink at Night, Yàn Zǐ Claims He Dares Not Join"]
景公飲酒，[Duke Jǐng was drinking wine,]
夜移于晏子家，[and moved to Yàn Zǐ's house at night.]
前驅款門曰：[The vanguard knocked on the door and said:]
「君至！」["The lord has arrived!"]
晏子被玄端，[Yàn Zǐ, wearing a xuán duān robe,]
立于門曰：[stood at the door and said:]
「諸侯得微有故乎？[Could it be that the feudal lords have some reason?]
國家得微有事乎？[Could it be that the state has some affair?]
君何為非時而夜辱？」[Why does your lord disgrace [me] at night at an inappropriate time?"]
公曰：[The Duke said:]
"The taste of wine and sweet liquor,
the sound of metal and stone instruments,
I wish to enjoy these with you, Master."
Yàn Zǐ answered,
"Those who spread the mats and cushions,
and arrange the fǔ and guǐ vessels,
there are people for that.
I dare not participate in it."
The Duke said,
"Move on to the house of Sīmǎ Rángjū."
The vanguard knocked on the door,
and said,
"The Duke has arrived!"
Rángjū, wearing armor and helmet, holding a halberd, stood at the door and said,
"Could it be that the feudal lords have any military action?
Could it be that the high officials have any rebellion?
Why does the Duke deign to disgrace me at night, at an unusual hour?"
The Duke said,
"The taste of wine and sweet liquor,
the sound of metal and stone instruments,
I wish to enjoy these with you, Master."
Rángjū replied,
"Those who spread the mats and cushions,
and arrange the fǔ and guǐ vessels,
there are people for that.
I dare not participate in it."
The Duke said, "Move on to the house of Liángqiū Jù."
The vanguard knocked on the door,
He said:
"The ruler has arrived!"
Liángqiū Jù held a sè (zither) in his left hand,
and held a yú (reed pipe) in his right hand,
walking and singing as he came out.
The Duke said:
"How joyous!
This evening I shall drink.
Without those two men,
how could my country be governed?
Without this one subject,
how could I find pleasure in life?"
The gentleman said:
"Sage and worthy rulers
all have beneficial friends;
they do not have ministers who steal pleasures.
Duke Jǐng was not able to reach this standard,
therefore he employed both,
and barely managed to avoid ruin."
5.13 *Duke Jǐng Instructs Someone to Offer Food and Qiūyànzi Responds with Subjects of the Altars of Soil and Grain*
Yànzi was attending Duke Jǐng.
The morning was cold.
The Duke said:
"Please offer warm food."
Yànzi replied:
"Yīng is not a minister who receives your food offerings,
I dare to decline."
The Duke said:
"Please come in and put on fur robes."
He replied:
"Yīng is not a minister who serves on your lord's mats and cushions,
I dare to decline."
The Duke said:
"Then what is the master to me?"
He replied:
"Yīng is
a minister of the state."
The Duke said:
"What is meant by a minister of the state?"
He replied:
"A minister of the state
is able to establish the state,
distinguish the meaning of high and low,
and make them appropriate;
regulate the order of the various officials,
and make them suitable;
compose pronouncements and orders,
which can be distributed to the four quarters."
From then on,
if the ruler did not act according to propriety,
he would not see Yàn Zǐ.
5.14 *Yàn Zǐ's Feast with Duke Jǐng, Stopping the Steward's Levy and Wishing to Share Happiness with the People*
Yàn Zǐ was drinking wine with Duke Jǐng,
and ordered that the vessels must be new.
The steward said:
"The resources are insufficient,
I request to collect taxes from the people."
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 said:
"Stop!
For music (or pleasure),
the high and low share it together.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven shares it with the realm,
the feudal lords share it with their territories,
and from the grand masters downwards, each shares it with their colleagues;
there is no such thing as solitary enjoyment.
Now, the ruler enjoys his pleasure,
while the subordinates are hurt by the expense.
This is solitary enjoyment,
it is not permissible!"
5.15 "Yàn Zǐ 晏子 drank wine with Duke Jǐng 景公.
The duke called for fire, Yàn Zǐ 晏子 quoted poetry to decline."
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 drank wine with Duke Jǐng 景公. As the sun set,
the duke called for fire.
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 declined, saying:
"The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
'The slanted cap is awry',
speaking of a loss of virtue.
'Repeated dancing is disordered', speaking of a loss of composure.
'Already drunk with wine,
already sated with virtue.'
'Already drunk and leaving,
both will receive blessings',
This is the proper etiquette between host and guest.
“To get drunk and not leave
is called harming virtue,” this is the guest’s fault.
Yīng has already divined the day,
but not the night.”
The Duke said:
“Good.”
He raised his cup to offer a libation,
bowed twice, and then departed.
He said:
“How could he surpass me?
I have entrusted the state to Yàn Zǐ.
He uses his family wealth to support me,
not wanting him to be extravagant,
how much more so would he deliberate on state affairs with me!”
5.16 [The State of Jìn Desired to Attack Qí, So They Sent Someone to Observe Yàn Zǐ, Who Treated the Envoy with Propriety and Thwarted Their Plan]
Jìn Píng Gōng desired to attack Qí.
He sent Fàn Zhāo to observe it.
Jǐng Gōng feasted him.
When the drinking was at its height,
Fàn Zhāo said:
“I request that you discard your wine cup.”
The Duke said:
“Pour from my wine cup
and offer it to the guest.”
After Fàn Zhāo had drunk,
Yàn Zǐ said:
“Remove the cup,
changed it."
The wine vessels were prepared,
Fàn Zhāo pretended to be drunk,
displeased, he rose and danced,
saying to the Grand Music Master:
"Can you tune the music of Chéng Zhōu for me?
I will dance it for you."
The Grand Music Master said:
"Your humble servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo hurried out.
Duke Jǐng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"Jìn,
is a great state,
sending someone to come and observe our government,
now you anger the messenger of a great state,
what will become of us?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"As for Fàn Zhāo's character,
he is not ignorant and does not lack knowledge of etiquette,
I intended to test our lord, therefore I refused him."
Duke Jǐng said to the Grand Music Master:
"Why did you not tune the music of Chéng Zhōu for the guest?"
The Grand Music Master replied:
"The music of Chéng Zhōu,
is the music of the Son of Heaven,
if it is tuned,
it must be danced by the ruler of men.
Now Fàn Zhāo,
As a subject,
to want to perform the music of the Son of Heaven,
your servant, therefore, will not do it." Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Píng Gōng, saying:
"Qí is not yet ready to be attacked.
I wanted to test their ruler,
but Yàn Zǐ recognized it;
I wanted to violate their music,
but the Grand Music Master knew it."
Zhòng Ní heard of it and said:
"To know what is happening a thousand *lǐ* away without stepping outside the table of a feast,
that is what Yàn Zǐ is all about!
And the Grand Music Master is involved in it as well."
5.17 *Jǐng Gōng* Asked Dōngmén Wúzé about the Year's Harvests and He Answered with Ice; Yàn Zǐ Requested to Cease the Attack on Lǔ
*Jǐng Gōng* attacked Lǔ,
captured Xǔ,
and obtained Dōngmén Wúzé.
The Duke asked him:
"How are the harvests in Lǔ?"
He replied:
"The dark ice is congealed,
the sunlit ice is five inches thick."
*Jǐng Gōng* did not understand,
and told Yàn Zǐ about it.
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"He is a gentleman.
Asking about the year's harvests and answering with ice,
is proper.
When the yin water is excessive,
and the yang ice is five inches thick,
the cold and warmth are regulated.
When they are regulated, the laws and governance are fair.
When they are fair, the superiors and inferiors are in harmony.
When they are in harmony, the harvest is plentiful.
In years of plenty, with the multitude in harmony, if you attack,
your servant fears that it will exhaust the people and weary the soldiers,
and will not fulfill your intentions.
I beg you to treat Lǔ with courtesy to quell our resentment,
and send back those who are captured,
to show our virtue." The Duke said,
"Good."
And so he did not attack Lǔ.
5.18 《Duke Jǐng Sent Yàn Zǐ to Give Land to Lǔ, But the Envoy of Lǔ Did Not Accept It All》
Duke Jǐng gave the ruler of Lǔ land,
several hundred villages in the shady part of the mountains,
and sent Yàn Zǐ to deliver it.
The envoy of Lǔ, Zǐ Shū Zhāo Bó, received the land,
but did not accept it all.
Yàn Zǐ said,
"My ruler offers the land,
out of loyalty and integrity.
Why do you not accept it all?"
Zǐ Shū Zhāo Bó said,
"I received the order from my ruler, saying:
'When feudal lords meet each other,
Giving and yielding,
striving to be in the lowest position,
is the outward form of propriety.
Offering much,
striving to receive little,
is the substance of action.
Propriety forms the outward appearance beforehand,
action creates patterns afterward,
and this is the reason why relationships last long."
Moreover, I have heard that a gentleman does not exhaust another's joy,
nor deplete another's loyalty,
which is why I did not accept everything."
Yàn Zǐ returned to report to the duke,
who happily laughed and said:
"Is the lord of Lǔ still like this?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Your subject has heard that large states are greedy for reputation,
small states are greedy for substance;
this is a common worry of the feudal lords.
Now Lǔ abides in a humble position and is not greedy for honor,
declines substance and is not greedy for much,
acts with integrity and does not act for a hasty gain,
and adheres to righteousness and does not act for a hasty compromise,
does not exhaust another's joy,
nor deplete another's loyalty,
in order to preserve its relationship.
The lord's commitment to righteousness
is different from worldly customs,
"The state is spared from public calamity."
The Duke said,
"I persuaded the Lord of Lǔ,
so he gave us the land.
Now his actions are indeed like this.
I will send someone to congratulate him."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"No!
If you give the land with joy,
and then congratulate him on relinquishing it,
then the relationship will not be close,
The Duke said,
"Good."
Thereupon, he increased the value of the gifts to Lǔ,
making them unparalleled among the other lords,
and made the ceremonies elaborate,
unparalleled among the guests.
The gentlemen in Lǔ,
after this, understood that acting with integrity and declining land could bring great fame.
5.19 《Duke Jǐng's Excursion to Jì and Finding a Book in a Golden Pot, Whereupon Yàn Zǐ Used It to Admonish Him》
Duke Jǐng went on an excursion to Jì.
He obtained a golden pot, opened it and looked at it.
Inside was a red inscription,
which said,
"When eating fish, do not turn it over;
do not ride a slow horse."
The Duke said:
"Excellent!
Knowing how to speak like you,
to eat fish without turning it over,
is because one dislikes its smell;
to not ride a slow horse,
is because one dislikes it not going far enough."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"That is not so.
To eat fish without turning it over,
is to not exhaust the people's strength!
To not ride a slow horse,
is to not place the unworthy at one's side!"
The Duke said:
"Jǐ had books,
how did it perish?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"It perished because of this.
Yīng has heard that,
when a gentleman has a principle,
he hangs it at the gate.
Jǐ had these words,
but kept them in a pot.
If it did not perish, what was it waiting for!"
5.20 《Duke Jǐng Praises Duke Zhāo of Lǔ’s Departure from His Country and Regrets It; Yàn Zǐ Says It's Too Late》
Duke Zhāo of Lǔ lost his state and fled to Qí.
Duke Jǐng asked him,
saying:
when you abandoned your state so early?
By what path did you arrive here?"
Duke Zhāo replied,
"When I was young,
many people loved me,
but my body could not personally approach them;
many people admonished me,
but my will could not use them.
Therefore, there was no one to oppose me internally and no one to assist me externally.
There was not a single person to assist or oppose me,
but those who flattered me were very numerous.
It is like an autumn tumbleweed,
its roots are isolated, but its branches and leaves are beautiful.
Once the autumn wind arrives,
the roots will be uprooted."
Duke Jǐng understood his words
and spoke to Yàn Zǐ,
saying,
"If this man were to return to his state,
wouldn't he become a wise ruler of ancient times?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"That is not so.
The foolish often regret,
the unworthy consider themselves worthy,
a drowning person does not ask about the riverbank,
a lost person does not ask about the road.
Asking about the riverbank after drowning,
asking about the road after getting lost,
To ask for directions after getting lost
is like forging weapons hastily when facing a calamity,
or digging a well hastily when choking.
Even if it's done quickly, it will be too late."
5.21 *Jǐng Gōng Shǐ Lǔ Yǒu Shì Yǐ Zhòngní Yǐ Wéi Zhī Lǐ* (Duke Jing's Envoy to Lu; Confucius Believed He Understood Propriety)
Yàn Zǐ was sent as an envoy to Lǔ.
Zhòngní ordered his disciples to go and observe.
Zǐ Gòng returned
and reported,
"Who says that Yàn Zǐ is versed in propriety?
For the *Lǐ* says,
'When ascending stairs, do not skip steps;
in the hall, do not hasten;
when presenting jade, do not kneel.'
Now, Yàn Zǐ is doing the opposite of all these.
Who says that Yàn Zǐ is versed in propriety?"
Yàn Zǐ, having already completed his mission to the ruler of Lǔ,
withdrew and met with Zhòngní.
Zhòngní said,
"Regarding *Lǐ*,
when ascending stairs, do not skip steps;
in the hall, do not hasten;
when presenting jade, do not kneel.
Did you, sir, do the opposite of these?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Yīng has heard that between the two pillars
the ruler and subject have their positions,
the ruler performs one,
Your servant will follow those two principles.
Your lord came quickly,
therefore he ascended the stairs swiftly, hurried across the hall, and reached his position.
Your lord presented the jade humbly,
therefore he knelt to lower it.
Moreover, I have heard that,
"The great one does not step over the threshold,
the small one can enter and exit."
Yàn Zǐ exited.
Zhòng Ní saw him off with the rites due a guest.
Returning, he instructed his disciples, saying: "Not scheming for righteousness,
only Yàn Zǐ is able to practice it."
5.22 *Yàn Zǐ's Visit to Lǔ to Present Food: Two Shoulders of Pork Are Missing, He Does Not Seek the Culprit*
Yàn Zǐ went to Lǔ.
At the morning meal, he presented a gift of cooked food,
which included a pig.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Remove its two shoulders."
When the meal was presented at noon,
the pig's shoulders were missing.
An attendant said:
"The shoulders of the pig in the meal are gone."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"They have been released."
The attendant said:
"I can find the person who took them."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Stop.
I have heard it said,
"If you measure achievement without considering ability,
the people will be exhausted;
if you hoard surpluses and do not distribute them,
the people will become thieves.
Teach me how to correct these things,
do not teach me to seek out such people."
5.23 Zēng Zǐ is about to depart, Yàn Zǐ sees him off and presents him with good words
Zēng Zǐ is about to depart,
Yàn Zǐ sees him off and says:
"I, Yīng, have heard that,
a gentleman presents people with a carriage,
but it's not as good as presenting them with words. May I present you with words,
or a carriage?"
Zēng Zǐ said:
"Please, with words."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Now, the cartwheel,
it is straight wood from the mountains,
a good craftsman shapes it,
its roundness conforms to the compass,
even if it is dried out and exposed to the sun,
it will not return to its original state.
Therefore, a gentleman is careful about hidden shaping.
The jade of Hé Shì,
was rough stone found in a well,
but a good craftsman refined it,
Then it becomes a treasure for preserving the state.
Therefore, the noble man is cautious in what he cultivates.
Now, the *lán* plant,
takes three years to mature.
If soaked in bitter wine,
then the noble man will not approach it,
and the common person will not wear it.
But if soaked in *mí hǎi* (fermented minced meat sauce),
then it can be sold for a horse.
It's not that the *lán* plant itself is beautiful,
but what it is soaked in.
I hope that you will certainly seek what to be soaked in.
Yīng has heard,
that the noble man, in dwelling, must choose his neighborhood,
and in traveling, must associate with gentlemen.
Choosing a dwelling is to seek gentlemen,
and seeking gentlemen is to avoid misfortune.
Yīng has heard that currents constantly change substance,
and customs change nature,
so one must be cautious."
5.24 *Yàn Zǐ* Visits Jìn
*Dǔ Qí Lěi Yuè Shífù Jiě Zuǒ Cān Shú Zhī Yǔ Guī* (Saw in Qí *Lěi Yuè Shífù* being unbound from the left outer horse and redeemed to return)
*Yàn Zǐ* went to Jìn, reaching Zhōngmóu,
and saw a man wearing a tattered cap and an inside-out fur coat, carrying grass,
resting by the side of the road.
*Yàn Zǐ* thought he was a noble man,
and sent someone to ask him.
He said:
"What are you doing?"
He replied:
"I am Yuè Shífù."
Yànzǐ said:
"Why have you come here?"
He said:
"I was a servant
in Zhōngmóu,
and was being sent back."
Yànzǐ said:
"Why did you become a servant?"
He replied:
"I could not avoid the sharpness of cold and hunger on my body,
and therefore became a servant."
Yànzǐ said:
"How long have you been a servant?"
He replied:
"For three years."
Yànzǐ said: "Can you be redeemed?"
He replied:
"Yes."
Thereupon he unharnessed the left trace horse and gave it to him,
and then took him on the chariot and returned with him.
Upon arriving at his residence,
he entered without saying goodbye.
Yuè Shífù became angry and requested to sever their relationship.
Yànzǐ sent someone to respond, saying:
"I have never had the opportunity to befriend you, Master.
You have been a servant for three years.
Only today have I seen and redeemed you.
Am I not acceptable to you?
Why do you reject my kindness so vehemently?"
Yuè Shífù replied to him,
"I have heard that
a scholar yields to those who do not understand him
but extends himself to those who understand him.
Therefore, a gentleman does not undervalue a person's worth because of their achievements,
nor does he bend his principles for the sake of such achievements.
For three years I have been a servant,
and no one understood me.
Now you have redeemed me,
and I considered you someone who understood me.
Previously, when you rode in your carriage,
you did not bid me to join you,
and I thought you had forgotten.
Now you again enter without inviting me,
and you are treating me the same as those who enslaved me.
If I am still to be a servant,
I ask that you sell me to the world."
Yàn Zǐ came out to see him
and said,
"Earlier I saw the guest's appearance,
but now I see the guest's intention.
I have heard that
one who examines actions does not dwell on errors,
察實者不譏其辭， One who investigates reality does not criticize the words.
嬰可以辭而無棄乎！ Yīng can decline yet not abandon [his principles]!
嬰誠革之。」 Yīng will sincerely change it."
迺令糞灑改席， Thereupon, he ordered to sweep and sprinkle [the road], change the mats,
尊醮而禮之。 Respected [Yuè Shí Fù] with libations and treated him with courtesy.
越石父曰： Yuè Shí Fù said:
「吾聞之， "I have heard that,
至恭不脩途， The utmost respect does not require repairing the road,
尊禮不受擯。 And dignified courtesy does not accept being ushered in.
夫子禮之， If you, sir, treat me with such courtesy,
僕不敢當也。」 I, your servant, dare not accept it."
晏子遂以為上客。 Yàn Zǐ then treated him as a distinguished guest.
君子曰： The gentleman said:
「俗人之有功則德， "Common people, when they have accomplished something, feel they have virtue;
德則驕。 And feeling virtuous, they become arrogant.
今晏子有功， Now Yàn Zǐ has accomplished something,
免人于厄， Saving someone from distress,
而反詘下之， Yet instead he humbles himself before those below him,
其去俗亦遠矣。 How far he is from the common!
此全功之道也。」 This is the way to complete merit."
5.25 *Àn Zǐ*’s Charioteer, Moved by His Wife's Words, Restrains Himself, and *Àn Zǐ* Recommends Him to Be a Senior Officer
*Àn Zǐ* was the Chancellor of *Qí*.
Once, when he went out,
his charioteer’s wife peeked at her husband
from the doorway. Her husband was driving the Chancellor’s chariot,
holding a large canopy,
whipping four horses.
His spirit and appearance were exuberant,
very pleased with himself.
Later, when he returned home,
his wife asked to leave him.
The husband asked her the reason.
The wife said:
"*Àn Zǐ*'s height is not even six *chǐ*,
yet he is the Chancellor of the State of *Qí*,
and his name is known among the feudal lords.
Today I observed him when he went out;
his thoughts and considerations are profound,
and he always conducts himself with humility.
Now, you are eight *chǐ* tall,
yet you are merely a servant and charioteer;
moreover, your attitude
is self-satisfied.
That is why I ask to leave."
Afterwards,
the husband restrained himself.
*Àn Zǐ* found it strange and asked him about it.
The charioteer told him the truth.
*Àn Zǐ* recommended him to be a senior officer.
5.26 *Mǐn Zǐwǔ* Sees *Àn Zǐ*; *Àn Zǐ* Regrets Not Fully Expressing His Intentions
There was a wandering scholar from *Yān*
named *Mǐn Zǐwǔ*,
who went south to see *Àn Zǐ* in *Qí*.
His words had elegance,
and his skills had order.
That which is great can benefit the state,
and that which is small can benefit Yànzǐ;
it is the three hundred poems.
When facing Yànzǐ,
he was fearful and cautious and could not speak.
Yànzǐ feigned a sorrowful expression for him,
and opened up with a respectful demeanor,
and only then was he able to fully respond.
Yànzǐ straightened his mat and sat,
foregoing the morning court for some time.
Those at his side said:
"Just now, the guest from Yān was in attendance,
why were you so worried, Master?"
Yànzǐ said:
"Yān
is a state of ten thousand chariots,
and Qí
has roads of a thousand *lǐ*.
Mǐn Zǐwǔ considered a state of ten thousand chariots not worth mentioning,
and roads of a thousand *lǐ* not worth travelling far;
thus he is above tens of millions of people.
Yet even he could not exhaust his words with me,
how much more so those people of Qí who embrace goodness and die!
Those whom I fail to see,
are they not many!
If I lose this,
what is the point?"
5.27 Yànzǐ Asks for Rice for Běiguō Sāo to Feed His Mother; Sāo Kills Himself to Illustrate the Worthiness of Yànzǐ

5.28 *Jǐng Gōng Wishes to See Gāo Jiū, Yàn Zǐ Declines Because He is a Minister Who Serves for Pay*
Jǐng Gōng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"I have heard that Gāo Jiū associates with you.

Yàn Zǐ replied:
"I have heard that
those who fight for land

those who serve for pay

Gāo Jiū has been like a brother to Yīng for a long time,
but he has never interfered with Yīng's conduct

6.1 "Líng Gōng Forbids Women from Dressing as Men but Cannot Stop Them; Yàn Zǐ Requests to First Restrain His Own Household"
Líng Gōng was fond of women dressed as men,
so the people of the state all adopted this fashion.
The Duke sent officials to forbid it,
saying:
"Women dressed as men will have
their clothes torn and
their belts cut."
The sight of torn clothes and cut belts was continuous,
but it did not stop.
Yàn Zǐ had an audience with the Duke.
The Duke asked,
"I have ordered officials to prohibit women and men from dressing like women,
tearing and cutting their clothes and belts,
but they look at each other and do not stop. Why is this?"
Yànzǐ replied,
"You allow such dress inside [the palace],
but prohibit it outside.
This is like hanging a cow's head at the door
but selling horse meat in the market.
Why doesn't Your Grace prohibit it within [the palace]?
Then no one outside would dare to do it."
The Duke said,
"Good."
He ordered that such dress be forbidden within [the palace].
Before a month had passed,
no one in the state dressed that way.
6.2 "The People of Qí Love Hub-Bumping, and Yànzǐ Beguiles Them by Calling it Inauspicious to Forbid It"
The people of Qí greatly loved hub-bumping [chariot wheels],
colliding with each other as a form of amusement,
and forbidding it did not stop them.
Yànzǐ worried about this.
So he prepared a new chariot and fine horses,
went out and bumped hubs with people,
saying,
"Hub-bumping is inauspicious!
Perhaps my sacrifices are not reverent,
and my dwelling is not respectful?"
He got out of the chariot, abandoned it, and left.
After that, the people of the state then did not do it.
Therefore, it is said,
"If you prohibit something with laws,
but do not first act yourself,
the people cannot be stopped."
Therefore, to transform their hearts,
nothing is better than teaching."
6.3 "Duke Jǐng Dreams of Five Men Claiming Innocence, Yàn Zǐ Knows of Their Grievance"
Duke Jǐng hunted at Wúqiū.
The night was still early.
The duke sat and fell asleep,
and dreamed that there were five men facing north in reed huts,
claiming to be innocent.
The duke woke up,
summoned Yàn Zǐ and told him what he had dreamed.
The duke said:
"Could it be that I once killed the innocent
and executed the guiltless?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, the late ruler Duke Líng hunted,
and five men used nets to scare the beasts,
so he killed them,
cut off their heads and buried them.
He named the place
'The Mound of the Five Men'.
Could this be that place?"
The duke ordered men to dig and search for them,
zé wǔ tóu tóng xué ér cún yān. Then five heads were in the same hole and survived.
Gōng yuē: The Duke said:
"Xī!" "Alas!"
lìng lì zàng zhī. He ordered the officials to bury them.
Guórén bù zhī qí méng yě, The people of the state did not understand his delusion,
yuē: and said:
"Jūn mǐn bái gǔ, "The ruler pities the white bones,
ér kuàng yú shēng zhě hū, how much more so the living!
bù yí yú lì yǐ, He spares no effort,
bù shì yú zhī yǐ." He does not relinquish his wisdom."
Gù yuē: Therefore it is said:
Jūnzǐ zhī wèi shàn yì yǐ. It is easy for a virtuous person to do good.

6.5 *Jǐng Gōng Completes the Cypress Chamber, and the Music Master Kāi Speaks of the Dusk Chamber; Yàn Zǐ Discerns the Reason Why*
Duke Jǐng newly completed the cypress chamber,

The music master Kāi stroked the Gōng string on the left,

6.6 *Duke Jing Ails from Water, Dreams of Fighting the Sun, Yan Zi Teaches the Dream Interpreter How to Answer*
méng yǔ rì dòu Yàn Zǐ jiāo zhàn méng zhě yǐ duì》
Duke Jing ailed from water, and lay in bed for ten-odd days.
At night he dreamed of fighting two suns and not winning.
Yan Zi went to court.
The Duke said: "Last night I dreamed of fighting two suns,
and I, your ruler, did not win.
Am I going to die?"
Yan Zi replied:
"Please summon the dream interpreter."
He went out from the inner chambers,
and sent a man in a chariot to fetch the dream interpreter.
When he arrived, he said:
"Why have I been summoned?"
Yan Zi said:
"Last night,
he did not win.
The Duke dreamed of fighting two suns, and the Duke said:
'Am I going to die?'
Therefore, I ask you to interpret the dream for the ruler,
this is the reason."
The dream interpreter said:
"Please let me go back and prepare the written records."
Yan Zi said:
"Do not refute the writing.
Your Excellency has no illness elsewhere; the illness
is Yin.
The sun is
Yang.
One Yin cannot overcome two Yang;
Your Excellency's illness will soon be cured.
Use this to respond."
The dream diviner entered,
and the Duke said,
"I dreamed I fought with two suns and could not win.
Will I die?"
The dream diviner replied,
"Your Excellency's illness
is Yin.
The sun is
Yang.
One Yin cannot overcome two Yang;
Your Excellency's illness will soon be cured."
After three days,
the Duke's illness greatly improved,
and the Duke was about to reward the dream diviner.
The dream diviner said,
"This is not my power;
it was Yàn Zǐ who taught me."
The Duke summoned Yàn Zǐ
and was about to reward him.
Yàn Zǐ said,
"The interpretation of dreams aligns with my words,"
"therefore it is beneficial."
"If I were to speak for myself,"
"then I would not be believed."
"This is the power of dream interpretation,"
"I have no merit in it."
The Duke rewarded him twice,
saying,
"Yàn Zǐ does not take credit for others' achievements,"
"and the dream interpreter does not conceal others' abilities."
6.7 *Duke Jǐng's Sore: Yàn Zǐ Touches It and Answers, Whereupon He Realizes the Rudeness of His Ministers*
Duke Jǐng had a boil on his back.
Gāo Zǐ and Guó Zǐ requested to see him.
The Duke said,
"Their duty is to touch the boil."
Gāo Zǐ stepped forward and touched the boil.
The Duke said,
"Is it hot?"
He said,
"It is hot."
"How hot is it?"
He said,
"Like fire."
"What is its color like?"
He said,
"Like an unripe plum."
"How big is it?"
He said,
"Like a bean."
"What is the shape of the part that has broken off?"
He said:
"Like the sole of a shoe."
The two men left,
Yàn Zǐ requested an audience.
The Duke said:
"I am ill,
and cannot manage my clothes and cap to come out and meet you, Master.
Would you condescend to look upon me?"
Yàn Zǐ entered,
and called to the steward to prepare washing water,
and to the servant to prepare a towel,
to brush his hands and warm them,
to unroll the mat and lay out the cushion,
kneeling, he requested to touch the sore.
The Duke said:
"How hot is it?"
He said:
"Like the sun."
"What color is it?"
He said:
"Like blue jade."
"How large is it?"
He said:
"Like a *bì* (jade disc)."
"What is the shape of the part that has broken off?"
He said:
"Rú Guī."
Yàn Zǐ went out.
The Duke said:
"If I had not seen a gentleman,
I would not have known the boorishness of a rustic."
6.8 *Yàn Zǐ's Mission to Wú: The King of Wú Orders the Usher to Claim It Is the Son of Heaven Requesting an Audience; Yàn Zǐ Feigns Confusion*
Yàn Zǐ was on a mission to Wú.
The King of Wú said to the protocol officer:
"I have heard of Yàn Yīng;
he is skilled in argument and versed in etiquette in the north.
Order the usher, saying:
'When the guest is presented, announce that the Son of Heaven requests an audience.'"
The next day,
Yàn Zǐ had business.
The protocol officer said:
"The Son of Heaven requests an audience."
Yàn Zǐ was taken aback.
The protocol officer said again:
"The Son of Heaven requests an audience."
Yàn Zǐ frowned.
He said again:
"The Son of Heaven requests an audience."
Yàn Zǐ frowned three times,
and said:
"Your servant received the command of the ruler of my humble state
to be an envoy to where the King of Wú resides.
Due to my lack of intelligence, I am confused
Entering the court of the Son of Heaven,
may I presume to ask, where does the King of Wú exist?"
Thereupon the King of Wú said,
"Fūchāi requests an audience."
He was received with the rites due to a feudal lord.
6.9 *Yànzǐ's Mission to Chǔ: Chǔ Constructs a Small Gate; Yànzǐ Declares That Those Who Visit Dog Countries Enter Dog Gates.*
Yànzǐ was sent as an envoy to Chǔ. Because Yànzǐ was short,
the people of Chǔ constructed a small gate beside the large gate and invited Yànzǐ to enter.
Yànzǐ did not enter,
and said,
"Those who are sent to dog countries
enter through dog gates.
Now I am an envoy to Chǔ,
and I should not enter through this gate."
The usher then led him through the large gate,
and he met with the King of Chǔ.
The king said,
"Is there no one in Qí?
That you are sent as an envoy." Yànzǐ replied,
"In Línzī of Qí, there are three hundred wards.
Spreading out their sleeves, they make a canopy;
wiping their sweat, it becomes rain;
shoulder to shoulder, heel to heel, they are present.
Why would there be no one?"
The king said,
"In that case, why were you sent as an envoy?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Qí's envoys
each have their own role.
The worthy are sent to worthy kings;
the unworthy are sent to unworthy kings.
Yīng is the most unworthy,
therefore I was sent directly to Chǔ."
6.10 *Chǔ* King Wishes to Humiliate Yàn Zǐ by Calling a Thief a *Qí* Person; Yàn Zǐ Counters with Oranges
Yàn Zǐ was about to go as envoy to Chǔ.
The King of Chǔ heard of this
and said to his attendants,
"Yàn Yīng
is a man of Qí practiced in argument.
He is now coming.
I wish to humiliate him.
What should I do?"
The attendants replied,
"When he comes,
your servant will ask someone to tie up a person,
pass by the king while walking.
The king will say,
'What is this person doing?'
He will answer,
'He is a Qí person.'
The king will say,
'What crime has he committed?'
He will say,
'He committed theft.'"
Thereupon, Yàn Zǐ arrived,
the King of Chǔ bestowed wine on Yàn Zǐ,
as the wine reached its peak,
two officers bound a man and passed the king
and walked along, the king said:
"What is the bound man being done for?"
They replied:
"He is a man from Qí."
The king said:
said:
"What crime did he commit?" "He committed theft."
The king looked at Yàn Zǐ and said:
"Are the people of Qí inherently good at stealing?"
Yàn Zǐ left his mat, stepped down and replied:
"I have heard that,
if an orange grows south of the Huái River, it is an orange,
if it grows north of the Huái River, it is a trifoliate orange,
their leaves and appearance are similar,
but their fruit and taste are different.
What is the reason for this?
Their soil and water are different.
Now, the people who grow up in Qí do not steal,
but when they enter Chǔ, they steal,
could it be that the water and soil of Chǔ make the people good at stealing?"
The king laughed and said:
"A sage is not someone to joke with,
I have instead brought trouble upon myself."
6.11 《The King of Chǔ feasted Yàn Zǐ, presented oranges and placed a paring knife; Yàn Zǐ did not peel and ate it.》
Duke Jǐng sent Yàn Zǐ on a mission to Chǔ.
The King of Chǔ presented oranges,
and provided a paring knife.
Yàn Zǐ did not peel them but ate them whole.
The King of Chǔ said:
"Oranges should be peeled."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"I have heard that,
when presenting things to the ruler,
melons and peaches are not peeled,
and oranges and pomelos are not segmented.
Now, if a state of ten thousand chariots does not have such an order,
then I, your servant, dare not segment them;
otherwise,
it's not that I don't know [how]."
6.12 《Yàn Zǐ in plain clothes and with a simple cart, attends court, Tián Huán Zǐ attends Duke Jǐng's drinking, requesting to make him drink a penalty cup》
Duke Jǐng was drinking wine.
Tián Huán Zǐ was attending him.
He saw Yàn Zǐ,
and reported back to the Duke, saying:
"Please make Yàn Zǐ drink a penalty cup."
The Duke said:
"Why?"
Wú Yǔ replied:
"Yàn Zǐ wears clothes of black linen,
deer fur,
rides in a cart with a simple axle,
and drives a tired horse to court.
"This is a gift from a recluse."
The Duke said,
"Agreed."
Yàn Zǐ sat down,
and the wine server presented a goblet and offered it to him,
saying,
"The Duke orders you to drain the cup."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"What is the reason for this?"
Tián Huánzǐ said,
"The Duke has bestowed upon you the position of a high minister to honor your person,
and favored you with a million coins to enrich your family.
Among all the ministers, none is of a higher rank than you,
nor enjoys a greater stipend.
Yet now you wear a robe of black cloth,
a deerskin jacket,
a carriage with wooden axles,
and drive a worn-out horse to court.
This is a gift from a recluse.
Therefore, drain the cup."
Yàn Zǐ stepped aside and said,
"Should I drink first and then decline,
or decline first and then drink?"
The Duke said,
"Decline first and then drink."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"The Duke has bestowed upon me the position of a high minister to honor my person,
and I, Yīng, do not dare to receive it for my own glory,
It is to carry out your lord's orders;
to favor me with millions in order to enrich my family,
Yīng dares not receive it for personal enrichment,
but to distribute your lord's gifts.
I have heard that a wise ruler of old
would consider his minister at fault if he received generous gifts and did not care for his kinsmen;
that was a fault;
when facing affairs, he would hold his position;
