All the ministers want to abandon propriety to serve you,
and I, Yīng, fear that you yourself do not desire it.
Now, even a five-foot-tall child in the state of Qí
is stronger than I,
and could defeat you,
but they dare not cause disorder,
because they fear propriety and righteousness.
If superiors have no propriety,
they have nothing with which to command their inferiors;
if inferiors have no propriety,
they have nothing with which to serve their superiors.
Now, deer and elk are without propriety,
therefore fathers and sons share the same female.
The reason why humans are superior to birds and beasts
is because they possess propriety.
I, Yīng, have heard that
if a ruler lacks propriety,
he has nothing with which to oversee his state;
if a senior official lacks propriety,
his subordinates will not be respectful;
if father and son lack propriety,
their family will surely be unfortunate;
if brothers lack propriety,
they cannot remain together for long.
The *Book of Odes* says:
'A man without propriety,
why does he not quickly die?'
Therefore, propriety cannot be abandoned."
The Duke said,
"I, being dull and lacking virtue,
have been seduced and misled by those around me,
to the point of this situation.
I beg to kill them."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"What crime have those around you committed?
If the ruler lacks propriety,
then those who cherish propriety will leave,
and those who lack propriety will arrive.
If the ruler cherishes propriety,
then those who possess propriety will arrive,
and those who lack propriety will leave."
The Duke said,
"Good.
I will change my clothes and leather cap,
and receive your instructions anew."
Yàn Zǐ stepped aside and left,
standing outside the gate.
The Duke ordered men to sweep and sprinkle water, and change the mats,
and summoned his robes and cap to welcome Yàn Zǐ.
Yàn Zǐ entered the gate,
declined three times,
ascended the steps,
and performed the ceremony of three libations.
He tasted the wine and sampled the food,
bowed twice,
He announced his satiety and left.
The Duke descended and bowed,
seeing him off at the door.
Returning, he ordered the wine to be removed and the music stopped,
saying:
"I am doing this to demonstrate the teachings of Yàn Zǐ."
7.2 *Jǐng Gōng Hosts a Banquet on Mount Tài and Weeps; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes*
Duke Jǐng hosted a banquet atop Mount Tài. As the wine grew strong,
the Duke surveyed the land,
sighed deeply,
and tears streamed down his face.
He said:
"I, the寡人(guǎ rén, 'the lonely one,' a term used by rulers), am about to leave this grand and magnificent state and die!"
Those around him assisting in the lament and weeping numbered three.
They said:
"We are insignificant people,
and even we will dread death.
How much more so for you, 公(gōng, 'Duke')!
To abandon this state and die,
how can that be acceptable!"
Yàn Zǐ alone slapped his thigh,
looked up to the heavens and laughed loudly, saying:
"How joyful!
Today's drinking is!"
The Duke, greatly angered, said:
"I am in mourning,
and you alone laugh loudly.
Why is that?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"Today I saw one cowardly ruler,
and three flattering ministers,
which is why I laughed heartily."
The Duke said,
"What do you mean by 'flattering' and 'cowardly'?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"That in ancient times there was death,
allowing later generations of virtuous people to have rest because of it,
and the unworthy to be subdued because of it.
If the ancient kings had not known of death,
from the past, the former ruler, Grand Duke (Tàigōng), would still be here today,
and how would Your Lordship have obtained this state to mourn over it?
That flourishing has decline,
and life has death,
is the division of Heaven.
Things have what they must reach,
events have what is constant and natural,
this is the way of antiquity.
Why should it be grieved over?
To still grieve over death when reaching old age,
is cowardice;
those on the left and right who assist in the grief,
are flatterers.
Cowardice and flattery gather together,
therefore I laughed at it."
The Duke, ashamed, changed his words and said,
"I am not saddened by dying away from my country.
I have heard that,
when a comet appears,
the ruler of the country towards which it points will suffer.
Now a comet has appeared and points towards my country,
and that is why I am sorrowful."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Your actions are perverse and wicked,
you have no virtue towards the country,
when digging ponds and marshes,
you want them to be deep and wide;
when building terraces and pavilions,
you want them to be high and large;
your taxes are like robbery,
your executions are like those of an enemy.
Judging from this,
another ominous star will appear.
Is the appearance of a comet
something to be feared!"
Thereupon the Duke was afraid, and then returned,
filled up the ponds and marshes,
abandoned the terraces and pavilions,
reduced taxes,
relaxed punishments,
and after thirty-seven days the comet disappeared.
7.3 *Jǐng* Gōng Dreams of a Comet and Asks Someone to Divinate it. Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him.
Jǐng Gōng dreamt of a comet.
The next day,
he summoned Yàn Zǐ and asked him:
"I have heard that
where there is a comet, there will surely be a lost country.
Last night,
I dreamed of a comet.
I want to summon a dream interpreter to interpret it."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Your Majesty's living arrangements are without moderation,
clothing is without measure,
you do not listen to righteous advice,
starting affairs without end,
levying taxes without satisfaction,
treating the people as if they will be unable to bear it,
and all the people harbor resentment.
Ominous stars are about to appear,
why only worry about comets!"
7.4 《Duke Jǐng Asks What the Joy Would Be If There Were No Death in Ancient Times; Yàn Zǐ Admonishes》
Duke Jǐng was enjoying drinking wine,
and said:
"If there were no death in ancient times,
what would the joy be like?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"If there were no death in ancient times,
then the joy would belong to those ancient people,
what would Your Majesty gain from it?
In the past, the Shuǎng Jiū clan first lived on this land,
the Jì Zé clan followed them,
There was Féng Bólíng who acted accordingly,
the Púgū clan who acted accordingly,
and then Grand Duke (Tàigōng) who acted accordingly.
If in ancient times there was no death,
the pleasure of the Shuǎngjiū clan
would not be what you desired."
7.5 《Duke Jǐng Said that Liángqiū Jù Agreed with Him and Yànzǐ Advised Him》
Duke Jǐng returned from a hunt,
Yànzǐ was attending at Chuántái,
Liángqiū Jù arrived.
The Duke said:
"Only Jù agrees with me!"
Yànzǐ replied:
"Jù is only the same,
how can that be called harmony?"
The Duke said:
"Are harmony and sameness different?"
He replied:
"Different.
Harmony is like soup,
water, fire, vinegar, sauce, salt, and plum,
used to cook fish and meat,
heating it with firewood,
the cook harmonizes it,
regulating it with flavors,
supplementing what is insufficient;
to mitigate what is excessive,
the gentleman eats it,
To harmonize their minds.
The relationship between ruler and minister is also like this.
If the ruler says something is acceptable,
but there are objections to it,
the minister offers his objections
to perfect its acceptability.
If the ruler says something is unacceptable,
but there are merits to it,
the minister offers its merits
to remove its unacceptability.
Therefore, the government is fair and not intrusive,
and the people have no desire to contend.
Therefore, the *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
"There is also harmonized soup,
already prepared and smooth;
the assembled celebrants are silent,
at this time there is no contention."
The former kings' blending of the five flavors
and harmonizing the five sounds
was to harmonize their minds
and perfect their government.
Sounds are also like flavors:
One *qì* (vital energy),
two bodies,
three categories,
four substances,
five tones,
six lǜ (pitch pipes),
The seven musical notes,
the eight winds, and the nine songs
complement each other;
clear and turbid, small and large,
short and long, fast and slow,
sorrow and joy, strong and gentle,
slow and quick, high and low, near and far, close and sparse,
harmonize with each other.
A gentleman listens to them
to pacify his heart;
a peaceful heart and harmonious virtue.
Therefore, the *Book of Poetry* says:
'Virtuous sounds are flawless.'
Now, this official is not like that;
what you, the ruler, say is acceptable,
this official also says is acceptable;
what you, the ruler, say is unacceptable,
this official also says is unacceptable.
If you use water to dilute water,
who can eat it?
If it is as singularly focused as a *qin* or *se* lute,
who can listen to it?
Such uniformity is unacceptable."
The Duke said:
"Good."
7.6 *Duke Jǐng Orders the Ritualists to Ward Off a Comet, Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him*
In Qí there was a comet,
and Duke Jǐng ordered the ritualists to ward it off.
Yàn Zǐ 晏子 remonstrated, saying:
"It is of no benefit;
it will only invite deception.
The way of Heaven does not flatter;
it does not change its decrees.
How can you pray to avert it?
Moreover, the appearance of a comet
is to eliminate defilement.
If you, ruler, have no defiled virtue,
what need is there to pray to avert it?
If your virtue is defiled,
how will praying to avert it reduce it?
The *Shī* 詩 [Book of Odes] says:
'Oh, this King Wén 文王,
was cautious and reverent,
clearly serving the High God (Shàngdì 上帝),
and thus received abundant blessings.
His virtue was not perverse,
and therefore he received the states.'
If you, ruler, do not violate virtue,
the states will come to you.
Why worry about the comet?
The *Shī* 詩 says:
'I have nothing to reflect upon;
the Xià 夏 and Shāng 商 dynasties,
because of their disorder,
caused the people to ultimately flee and perish.'
If your virtue is perverse and disordered,
The people will flee into exile,
and the actions of the prayer officials and historians
will be of no help."
The Duke was pleased
and so stopped.
7.7 "Duke Jǐng's Illness, Liángqiū Jù and Yì Kuǎn Request the Execution of the Prayer Officials and Historians, Yàn Zǐ Advises Against It"
Subsequently, he suffered from malaria,
and Duke Jǐng contracted scabies, but did not recover within a year.
Many guests from the feudal lords
came to inquire about his illness.
Liángqiū Jù and Yì Kuǎn said to the Duke:
"We serve the spirits lavishly,
even more so than did the former rulers.
Now that you are ill,
causing worry for the feudal lords,
this is the fault of the prayer officials and historians.
If the feudal lords are unaware,
they will say that we are disrespectful.
Why don't you execute Zhù Gù and Shǐ Yín to use as an excuse to the guests?"
The Duke was pleased
and informed Yàn Zǐ.
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"At the covenant of Rì and Sòng,
Qū Jiàn asked Zhào Wǔ about the virtue of Fàn Huì.
Zhào Wǔ said:
'The affairs of that gentleman's family are well-managed;
Speaking in the state of Jìn,
exhausting their emotions without selfishness,
their invocators and historians officiating at sacrifices,
presented sincerity without shame;
their family affairs were without suspicion,
their invocators and historians did not pray for personal gain.'
Jiàn used these words to tell King Kāng,
King Kāng said:
'Gods and men have no grievances,
it is fitting that you, sir, should brightly assist five rulers,
and be considered the master of the feudal lords.'"
The Duke said:
"Jù and Kuǎn said that I am able to serve the spirits,
therefore I want to execute the invocators and historians,
you praise these words, why?"
He replied:
"If there is a virtuous ruler,
external and internal affairs are not neglected,
superiors and inferiors have no grievances,
actions are without violation of principles,
their invocators and historians recommend sincerity,
and have no shame in their hearts.
Therefore, the spirits enjoy the offerings,
and the state receives its blessings,
with the invocators and historians sharing in them.
The reason they are prosperous, blessed, and long-lived
is because they serve a sincere ruler,
and their words are faithful to the spirits.
If they happen to encounter a lecherous ruler,
both inside and outside (the court) are quite corrupt,
those above and below harbor resentment and hatred,
actions deviate from the proper path,
indulging desires and satisfying personal interests,
building high terraces and deep ponds,
striking bells and having dancing girls,
cutting down the strength of the people,
transporting and plundering their gathered wealth,
to complete his transgressions,
not caring for future generations,
being tyrannical, cruel, lewd and unrestrained,
acting licentiously beyond measure,
without any restraint,
not considering slander and curses,
not fearing ghosts and spirits,
the spirits are angry, and the people suffer,
without remorse in their heart.
Their invocators and historians recommend insincere offerings,
this is to speak of sins;
their offerings lack the proper number of beautiful items,
this is to falsely accuse;
advancing and retreating without proper ritual language,
then they feign devotion to seek favor,
therefore the ghosts and spirits do not accept (the offerings)
and bring disaster upon the state,
the invocators and historians are involved in it.
The reason for premature death, confusion, orphans, and disease
is because of the actions of the tyrant,
and their words are presumptuous and disrespectful toward ghosts and spirits."
Gōng said:
"In that case, what should be done?"
(He) replied:
"It cannot be done.
The trees of the mountains and forests
are guarded by Héng Lù;
the reeds and rushes of the marshes
are guarded by Zhōu Jiāo;
the firewood and kindling of the thickets
are guarded by Yúhòu;
the salt
and shellfish of the sea are guarded by Qíwàng.
The people of the districts and borders
are forced to follow his policies;
at the nearby passes,
he violently levies their private goods;
he forcibly seizes the wealth
of inheriting high officials;
he imposes regulations without limit,
and collects taxes without measure;
his palaces are renewed daily,
and his excessive pleasures are never abandoned;
his favored concubines within the palace recklessly plunder in the marketplace,
and his favored ministers outside the palace presumptuously issue orders in the countryside;
his private desires are indulged,
and if they are not satisfied, he responds accordingly.
The common people suffered from illness,
husbands and wives all cursed.
Prayers can be beneficial,
curses can also be harmful,
east of Liáo and Shè,
west of Gū and Yóu,
there are so many people!
Even if they are good at praying,
how can they overcome the curses of hundreds of millions of people!
History records that,
"If you, my lord, wish to be spared from being affected by curses, you must cultivate virtue."
The duke was pleased,
and ordered the officials to be lenient in their administration,
to destroy checkpoints and remove restrictions,
to reduce taxes and stop exactions,
and the duke's illness improved.
7.8 "Duke Jǐng Sees a Corpse on the Road and Feels Ashamed of his Lack of Virtue, Yànzǐ Advises Him"
Duke Jǐng's rewards extended to the inner palace,
embroidered silk covered terraces and pavilions,
beans and millet were fed to ducks and geese;
he went out and saw a corpse on the road,
and said to Yànzǐ:
"Why did this person die?"
Yànzǐ replied:
"This person died of starvation."
The duke said:
"Alas!
"My lack of virtue is truly great."
He replied:
"Your virtue is evident and manifest,
why do you say you have no virtue?"
Duke Jǐng said:
"What do you mean?"
He replied:
"Your virtue extends to the inner palace and terraces,
your playthings
are clothed in patterned embroidery;
your ducks and geese
are fed with beans and millet;
you indulge in personal pleasure within the palace,
extending it to the families of the inner palace.
Why do you say you have no virtue!
But I, your servant, wish to make a request of you:
From your own intentions,
your own heart of pleasure,
extend it and share it with the common people,
then what corpses would there be!
If you do not extend this,
and only indulge in personal pleasure within the palace,
causing wealth and goods to be accumulated in one place,
beans and millet, silk and cloth rotting in the granaries,
and benefits are not universally bestowed upon the common people,
and your public-mindedness does not extend to all the states,
then this is the reason why Jié and Zhòu perished.
The reason why the officers and people rebel is
It is due to partiality.
If Your Majesty examines the words of your servant Yīng,
promotes Your Majesty's great virtue,
and widely proclaims it to the world,
then (the deeds of) Tāng and Wǔ can be achieved.
Why worry about the death of a single starving person!"
7.9 《Lord Jǐng Wishes to Execute Someone Who Cut the Trees He Loved, Yàn Zǐ Admonishes Him》
Lord Jǐng ascended the viewing tower and looked out.
He saw a man cutting the trees at the Yōng Gate.
The lord ordered the officials to arrest him
and turned to Yàn Zǐ, urging him to execute the man.
Yàn Zǐ remained silent and did not respond.
The lord said:
"The trees at the Yōng Gate
are what I love very much.
Now they are being cut,
so I ordered you to execute him.
You remain silent and do not respond.
Why is that?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"I have heard that
when ancient rulers went out,
they cleared the road for ten *lǐ*,
not out of fear;
the crown had tassels in front,
to prevent seeing too much;
the ears were stuffed with cotton and jade pendants,
to prevent hearing too much;
Tài wore a belt weighing half a *jūn*,
and his shoes weighed double that,
because he didn't want to be light (fickle).
For crimes punishable by death,
if the ruler passed by at the midday court
he would pardon them.
Yīng has never heard of a ruler sitting in judgement of his own people himself."
The Duke said:
"Pardon him,
and do not let the Master speak again."
7.10 *Jǐng* Gōng, Sitting in the *Lù Qǐn*, Said "Who Will Possess This?", *Yàn Zǐ* Admonished.
Duke *Jǐng* sat in the *Lù Qǐn*,
and said:
"How beautiful is this chamber!
Who will possess it?"
*Yàn Zǐ* replied:
"It will be the *Tián* clan.
*Tián Wúyǔ* has already started building ramparts (for his family's eventual takeover)."
The Duke said:
"Then what should be done?"
*Yàn Zǐ* replied:
"Doing good is what Your Lordship encourages,
how can you forbid it?
The *Tián* clan is a family that beats the clapper at the country gate.
Fathers entrust it to their sons,
and elder brothers entrust it to their younger brothers,
and it has been so for three generations.
Timber from the mountains is like a market,
yet it is not depleted;
fish, salt, shellfish, and oysters
are not depleted from the sea;
the people's wealth flows towards them.
This year there is a calamitous famine,
and the harvest of *hāo* seeds and grass is not even half,
and there are dead people on the roads.
In Qí, the old four measures were *dòu*,
four *dòu* made a *qū*,
four *qū* made a *fǔ*,
ten *fǔ* made a *zhōng*.
The Tián family's four measures
each have one added to them.
They lend using the household measure,
and collect using the public measure,
thus the means by which the people buy their lives is exhausted.
Now the duke's family is arrogant and wasteful,
while the Tián family is benevolent and generous.
Where will the country's favor ultimately go?
Even though the Tián family has no virtue, they bestow upon the people.
The duke's family levies heavily, while the Tián family bestows generously.
The *Shī* (*Classic of Poetry*) says:
"Although he has no virtue to give you,
you sing and dance."
The Tián family's generosity
Folk songs and dances indeed;
they are where the country returns to;
is it not fitting indeed!"
7.11 "Duke Jing's Platform Completed, Pénchéng Shì Wishes to Jointly Bury His Mother, Yànzǐ Advises and is Permitted"
Duke Jǐng spent the night in the palace of Lùqǐn.
In the middle of the night,
he heard a man crying in the west.
The duke felt sorrow for him.
The next morning at court,
he asked Yànzǐ, saying:
"I, your ruler, heard a man crying in the west last night.
His voice was very mournful,
his spirit very sorrowful.
What is he doing?
I feel sorrow for him."
Yànzǐ replied, saying:
"In the west outer city lives a commoner scholar named Pénchéng Shì.
He is a filial son to his father,
and an obedient younger brother to his elder brother.
He was also once a disciple of Kǒngzǐ.
Now his mother has unfortunately died,
her coffin is temporarily placed awaiting burial,
his family is poor,
he is old,
his son is starving,
and he fears he lacks the strength to arrange a joint burial.
That is why he is sad."
The duke said:
"Please go and offer condolences on my behalf,
and inquire about the location of the secondary burial."
Yàn Zǐ received the order and went to offer condolences,
and asked about the location of the secondary burial.
Pénchéng Shì bowed twice,
kowtowed and did not rise,
saying:
"The secondary burial is entrusted to the palace's main sleeping quarters,
hoping to become a servant in the underworld,
holding writing tablets and grasping a brush,
serving beneath the right steps in the palace,
wanting to be sent off on a certain day,
but have not yet received the ruler's intention.
Impoverished and distressed, I have no way to plan,
spreading dry lips and a withered tongue,
with a scorched heart and burning insides,
now that you, my lord, deign to grace it with your presence,
I hope you can make a plan for it."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Indeed. This is a very important person,
but I fear the ruler may not allow it."
Pénchéng Shì jumped up and said:
"It all rests with the ruler!
Moreover, I have heard that,
the King of Yuè loved bravery,
and his people regarded death lightly;
King Líng of Chǔ loved slender waists,
and his court had many starving people;
Zǐ Xū 忠其君， Zǐ Xū was loyal to his lord,
故天下皆願得以為臣； therefore everyone in the world wished to have him as their minister.
Zēng Shēn、 Zēng Shēn,
Xiào Jǐ 愛其親，故天下皆願得以為子。 and Xiào Jǐ loved their parents, therefore everyone in the world wished to have them as their children.
今為人子臣， Now, being a subject and a son,
而離散其親戚， yet causing the separation and scattering of his relatives,
孝乎哉？ is this filial piety?
足以為子臣乎？ Is he worthy of being a son and a subject?
若此而得祔， If he is enshrined after death in such a manner,
是生臣而安死母也； it would mean valuing the living subject and neglecting the dead mother;
若此而不得， If he is not enshrined in such a manner,
則臣請輓尸車而寄之於國門外宇溜之下， then I, your minister, request to drag his corpse in a cart and leave it under the eaves outside the city gate,
身不敢飲食， and I myself will not dare to eat or drink,
擁轅執輅， holding the shaft and grasping the reins,
木乾鳥栖， until the wood dries and birds nest on it,
袒肉暴骸， exposing my flesh and bones,
以望君愍之。 hoping that you, my lord, will have pity on him.
賤臣雖愚， Though I, your humble minister, am foolish,
竊意明君哀而不忍也。」 I secretly believe that a wise ruler would grieve and be unable to bear it."
Yàn Zǐ 入， Yàn Zǐ entered,
復乎公， and reported to the duke.
公忿然作色而怒曰： The duke angrily changed his expression and said in anger:
「子何必患若言而教寡人乎？」 "Why must you worry about such words and lecture me?"
Yàn Zǐ 對曰： Yàn Zǐ replied:
「嬰聞之， "I have heard that,
忠不避危， loyalty does not avoid danger,
愛無惡言。 and love has no harsh words.
且嬰固以難之矣。 Moreover, I was indeed prepared for difficulty because of this.
Now you, my lord, are building pleasure grounds for sightseeing,
having already seized what belongs to others,
and further forbidding their burials.
This is not rén (benevolence).
Indulging your heart and listening arrogantly,
not caring about the people's worries,
This is not yì (righteousness).
How can you not listen?"
Thereupon, he recounted the words of Pénchéng Shì.
The Duke sighed deeply and said:
"Alas!
Do not speak further."
Then he ordered several hundred men to bare their upper bodies and remove their hats,
and women with hairpins in their hair,
to open the gate for funerals,
to welcome Pénchéng Shì.
Shì removed his mourning garments,
put on a cap with silk tassels,
and a black collar,
and went to see the Duke.
The Duke said:
"I have heard it said,
'Five sons are not enough to fill a corner,
but one son can fill the court.'
Is this not you, my son!"
Thereupon, Pénchéng Shì dared not cry in his duties,
and served with propriety.
When he finished, he left the gate,
Then he raised his voice.
7.12 *Duke Jing Builds the Longlai Terrace, Yanzi Dances and Admonishes*
Duke Jǐng built the Longlai Terrace, and Yàn Zǐ attended and sat with him.
After three rounds of drinks,
Yàn Zǐ rose to dance and said:
"The year is already late,
but the grain is not yet harvested,
in a daze, what is to be done!
The year is already cold,
but the labor is not stopped,
distressed, what is to be done!"
He danced three times,
and tears fell, wetting his lapel.
Duke Jǐng was ashamed,
and therefore stopped the labor on the Longlai Terrace.
7.13 *Duke Jing Ordered Zhú Zōu to Manage Birds, but They Were Lost; the Duke Was Angry and Was About to Punish Him, Yanzi Admonished*
Duke Jǐng loved hunting with arrows,
and ordered Zhú Zōu to manage the birds, but they were lost.
The Duke was angry,
and ordered the officials to kill him.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Zhú Zōu has three crimes,
please enumerate his crimes and then kill him."
The Duke said:
"You may."
於是召而數之公前， Thereupon, he summoned him and enumerated his faults before the Duke,
曰：
"Zhú Zōu!
汝為吾君主鳥而亡之， You were appointed by our lord to be in charge of the birds, and you let them escape.
是罪一也； This is your first crime.
使吾君以鳥之故殺人， To cause our lord to kill someone for the sake of birds,
是罪二也； this is your second crime.
使諸侯聞之， To cause the feudal lords to hear of this,
以吾君重鳥而輕士， and think that our lord values birds more than people,
是罪三也。」 this is your third crime."
數燭鄒罪已畢， Having finished enumerating Zhú Zōu's crimes,
請殺之。 he requested to have him killed.
公曰：
"Do not kill him!
寡人聞命矣。」 I have received instruction."

7.14 《Jǐng Gōng Wèn Zhì Guó zhī Huàn, Yàn Zǐ Duì Yǐ Nìng Rén Chán Fū Zài Jūn Cè》 7.14 Title: *Duke Jǐng Asks About the Calamities of Governing a State, Yàn Zǐ Responds that Flatterers and Slanderers are at the Ruler's Side*
景公問晏子曰： Duke Jǐng asked Yàn Zǐ,
「治國之患亦有常乎？」 "Are there constant calamities in governing a state?"
對曰： He replied:
「佞人讒夫之在君側者， "Those flatterers and slanderers who are at the ruler's side,
好惡良臣， who are biased against good ministers,
而行與小人， and act with petty men,
此國之常患也。」 these are the constant calamities of a state."
公曰： The Duke said:
「讒佞之人， "Slanderous and flattering people
則誠不善矣； are certainly not good.
雖然， However,
則奚曾為國常患乎？」 why are they a constant calamity for the state?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If the ruler considers them as ears and eyes but they indulge in deceptive matters,
then the ruler's ears and eyes are being deceived.
When those above confuse the ruler's ears and eyes,
those below cause all the ministers to lose their positions,
is this not truly a cause for concern!"
The Duke said:
"Is it like this!
I will remove them."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Your Grace cannot remove them."
The Duke became angry, changed his expression, and was displeased,
saying:
"Why do you underestimate me so much!"
He replied:
"How dare I be negligent!
Those who can ingratiate themselves with the ruler
possess talents that are truly extraordinary.
Those who harbor great dishonesty within
must meticulously cultivate small acts of sincerity on the outside,
in order to achieve their great dishonesty.
When present, they seek the ruler's desires and are skilled at accommodating them;
if the ruler resents good ministers,
they list their past mistakes and exaggerate them;
when absent, they exert power to acquire wealth.
What close confidant
would not be swayed by great profit
and instead strive for utmost righteousness with the ruler?
"It is difficult to know this."
The Duke said:
"Then what did the former sages do?"
He replied:
"The former sages in their governance,
carefully received guests,
heard matters of state without delay,
worried that the days were not long enough, all the ministers were able to fully express their sincerity,
how could slander and flattery find room for their private interests!"
The Duke said:
"Then, Master, assist me in stopping them,
and I too will strive not to employ them."
He replied:
"The slanderous and flattering people at your side,
are like rats in the shrine.
There is a proverb that says:
'Shrine rats cannot be smoked out.'
Slanderous and flattering people,
hide behind your majesty to protect themselves,
therefore, it is difficult to remove them."

7.15 *Jǐng Gōng Wèn Hòushì Shú Jiāng Jiàn Yǒu Qí Zhě, Yàn Zǐ Duì Yǐ Tián Shì* (Duke Jing asked who would inherit the state of Qi in later generations, and Yanzi replied that it would be the Tian family)
Duke Jǐng and Yàn Zǐ stood above Qū Huáng,
gazing out over the state of Qí,
Duke Jǐng asked Yàn Zǐ,
"Who in later generations will inherit the state of Qí?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"This is not something that a humble subject dares to discuss."
The Duke said:
"Is it necessarily so?"
"If those who gain never lose,"
"then Yú (虞) and Xià (夏) would exist forever."
Yàn Zǐ (晏子) replied,
"I have heard that being able to understand things with one's own insight is
wisdom;
predicting something and then having it come true is
foresight.
Now, wisdom and foresight
are matters for a gentleman;
how could I be capable of understanding them!
However,
please allow me to present my views on governance:
When the ruler is strong and the ministers are weak,
that is the foundation of governance;
when the ruler initiates and the ministers harmonize,
that is the flourishing of instruction;
when punishment resides with the ruler,
that is the discipline of the people.
Now, Tián Wúyǔ (田無宇) for two generations has had merit in the state,
but the benefits he receives are small,
while the ducal house takes the majority,
and the state's power is concentrated in it.
If the positions of ruler and minister are easily interchanged,
how can there be no decline?
I have heard it said,
'When the ministers are rich, the ruler perishes.'
Judging from this,
After his death, it will not be long,
the state of Qi,
will it be the state of the Tián clan?
Yīng is old and cannot wait for the affairs of the duke,
if the duke should pass away,
the government will not be in the ducal house."
The Duke said:
"If so, what should be done?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Only ritual can stop it.
As for ritual,
family favors should not extend to the state,
the people should not be lazy,
wealth should not be transferred,
artisans and merchants should not change their professions,
scholars should not be excessive,
officials should not flatter,
and grandees should not collect public profits."
The Duke said:
"Good.
Now I know that ritual can govern a state."
He replied:
"Ritual's ability to govern a state has been around for a long time,
standing alongside heaven and earth.
The ruler commands and the minister is loyal,
the father is kind and the son is filial,
the elder brother loves and the younger brother respects,
the husband is harmonious and the wife is gentle,
The mother-in-law being kind and the daughter-in-law listening,
is the principle of propriety.
The ruler commands and is not disobeyed,
the minister is loyal and not divided,
the father is kind and teaches,
the son is filial and remonstrates,
the elder brother loves and is friendly,
the younger brother respects and is obedient,
the husband is harmonious and righteous,
the wife is gentle and virtuous,
the mother-in-law is kind and compliant,
the daughter-in-law listens and is yielding,
this is the essence of propriety."
The Duke said:
"Excellent!
I, your unworthy subject, now know the esteem for propriety."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Propriety is
how the former kings oversaw the world
and cared for their people,
therefore, it is esteemed."
7.16 "Yàn Zǐ's Envoy to Wú, the King of Wú Asks About the Conduct of a Gentleman, Yàn Zǐ Replies with Not Perishing Together with a Chaotic State"
Yàn Zǐ was on a mission to Wú.
The King of Wú asked:
"What is the conduct of a gentleman like?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"He cherishes the ruler when he is virtuous,
political affairs are returned to him,
Not cherishing the salary of a tyrant,
not occupying a position in a chaotic state,
a gentleman retreats upon seeing the signs, not perishing
together with a chaotic state,
not dying together with a tyrant."
7.17 "The King of Wú asked the ruler of Qí: 'How can you tolerate such arrogance and violence from your ruler?' Yàn Zǐ replied, 'How can I possibly use the Way to feed such a person?'"
Yàn Zǐ was on a mission to Wú,
and the King of Wú said:
"I, the lonely one, have been consigned to this remote and uncivilized land,
and rarely see the conduct of gentlemen that instructs.
Please, let us speak privately without it being considered a crime."
Yàn Zǐ abruptly withdrew from his position.
The King of Wú said:
"I have heard that the ruler of Qí is both deceitful and arrogant,
both uncouth and violent.
Yet you tolerate him,
why is that so?"
Yàn Zǐ hesitated and replied:
"I have heard it said,
'One who cannot understand trivial matters
and is incapable of handling coarse matters
will certainly be burdened with toil;
one who cannot achieve great things
and will not do small things
will certainly be poor;
one who is unable to bring people to him with great deeds
and is unable to reach people's doors with small deeds
will surely be troubled.
This is why I serve.
Someone like me,
how could I use the Dao to feed people!"
Yàn Zǐ exited,
the king laughed and said:
"Alas!
Today I criticized Yàn Zǐ,
it is like being naked and criticizing a tall pillar."
7.18《Sīmǎ Zǐqī asks whether there are those who do not involve the ruler or care for the people, yet still seek fame; Yàn Zǐ replies that it is unbenevolent.》
Sīmǎ Zǐqī asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"Are there officials who do not involve the ruler,
do not care for the people,
simply reside in inaction and seek fame?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"I have heard that,
those who have the ability to support the ruler and benefit the people, but do not do it,
are called unbenevolent.
As for the unbenevolent seeking fame,
I have never heard of it."
7.19 《Gāo Zǐ asks, you served Líng Gōng, Zhuāng Gōng, and Jǐng Gōng, and all respected you; Yàn Zǐ replies that it was with one heart.》
Gāo Zǐ asked Yàn Zǐ, saying:
"You served Líng Gōng,
Zhuāng Gōng, and Jǐng Gōng,
and all respected you.
Were the hearts of the three rulers the same?
Or was your heart different for each of them?"
Àn Zǐ replied:
"Excellent!
Inquiring about serving a ruler,
I have heard that with a single mind one can serve a hundred rulers,
but with three minds one cannot serve even one ruler.
Therefore, the minds of three rulers are not one single mind,
but my mind is not three different minds.
Moreover, when I was with Duke Líng,
I tried my best but could not establish his government.
I was only able to preserve my limbs to follow my ruler.
When Duke Zhuāng promoted warriors
and valued courage and strength,
wanting to reject righteousness and pursue wickedness,
I could not stop him,
so I retired and lived in the countryside.
I have heard that
if one's advice is not heeded,
one should not accept their salary;
if one does not manage their affairs,
one should not share their troubles.
I have already acted on this with Duke Zhuāng.
The current ruler
values pleasure over the state,
treats the people poorly and is lavish in his own sustenance,
excessively taxes and levies,
and issues excessive orders and demands.
I cannot stop him.
How could I possibly know how to preserve myself and serve such a ruler!"
7.20 *Àn Zǐ* Re-Governs *Dōng'ē*, Submitting Accounts. Duke *Jǐng* Welcomes and Congratulates, *Àn Zǐ* Declines
*Àn Zǐ* governed *Dōng'ē*.
For three years,
Duke *Jǐng* summoned him and reprimanded him, saying:
"I thought you were capable,
and sent you to govern *Dōng'ē*.
Now you govern and cause disorder.
You should withdraw and examine yourself.
I will inflict a great punishment upon you."
*Àn Zǐ* replied:
"I ask to change my methods and ways to govern *Dōng'ē*.
If I do not govern well in three years,
I ask to die for it."
Duke *Jǐng* agreed.
Thereupon, the next year when the accounts were submitted,
Duke *Jǐng* welcomed him and congratulated him, saying:
"Very good!
You have governed *Dōng'ē* well!"
*Àn Zǐ* replied:
"When I previously governed *Dōng'ē*,
recommendations and requests were not acted upon,
bribes did not arrive,
and the fish in the ponds
benefited the poor people.
At that time,
the people were not hungry,
but you, my lord, instead blamed me.
Now, when I later governed *Dōng'ē*,
Requests and entrustments are carried out,
bribes arrive,
and heavy taxes are collected,
storehouses are lacking in supplies,
he favors those around him,
and the fish in the ponds
enter the houses of the powerful.
At this time,
more than half the people are starving,
yet you, my lord, instead welcome and congratulate me.
I, your foolish servant, am unable to govern Dōng'ē again,
and wish to request my retirement,
to make way for a more capable man."
He bowed twice,
and left.
Jǐng Gōng then descended from his mat and apologized, saying:
"Zǐ Qiáng, govern Dōng'ē again,
Dōng'ē,
is your Dōng'ē,
I will no longer interfere with it."
7.21 "The Grand Diviner Deceives Jǐng Gōng that He Can Move the Earth, Yànzǐ Knows It is False, He Makes the Diviner Understand the Duke Himself"
Jǐng Gōng asked the Grand Diviner,
"What can your way do?"
He replied:
"I can move the earth."
The Duke summoned Yànzǐ and told him,
saying:
"I asked the Grand Diviner,
Said: "What ability does your doctrine have?"
He replied:
"It can move the earth."
"Can the earth be moved?"
Yàn Zǐ remained silent and did not answer.
He went out and saw the chief diviner, saying:
"In the past, I saw the hooked star between the four heart stars.
Will the earth move?"
The chief diviner said:
"Yes."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If I speak of it,
I fear that you will die for it;
If I remain silent and do not answer,
I fear that the ruler will be alarmed.
If you speak,
Both ruler and minister will benefit.
One who is loyal to the ruler,
Must he necessarily harm others?"
Yàn Zǐ departed,
The chief diviner hurried in to see the duke,
saying:
"Your servant cannot move the earth,
The earth is indeed about to move."
Chén Zǐyáng heard of it,
and said:
"Yàn Zǐ remained silent and did not answer because
he did not want the chief diviner to die;
He went to see the Grand Diviner because
he feared the ruler's anxiety.
Yàn Zǐ
is a benevolent man,
one could say he is loyal to his sovereign and kind to his inferiors."
7.22 *Someone Presented a Letter Slandering Yàn Zǐ, Who Retired to Farming; When the State Was Not Well-Governed, Yàn Zǐ Was Recalled*
Yàn Zǐ served as prime minister to Duke Jǐng,
and his method of evaluating people was this:
when he saw someone virtuous, he would promote them,
regardless of whether they were desired by the ruler;
when he saw someone wicked, he would dismiss them,
regardless of whether they were loved by the ruler;
he conducted himself without selfishness,
and spoke frankly without reservation.
Someone submitted a letter, saying:
"Dismissing and appointing without fully consulting the ruler is called 'usurping authority';
it is called 'being presumptuous';
speaking without reservation before the ruler
is called 'being disrespectful'.
If the practices of usurpation and disrespect exist,
then the proper relationship between ruler and minister is abolished,
I do not know how Yàn Zǐ can be considered a loyal minister."
The Duke thought this was true.
When Yàn Zǐ entered the court,
the Duke's expression was displeased.
Therefore, Yàn Zǐ returned home,
fully loaded his belongings,
and sent someone to decline his position, saying:
"Yīng, a man of old age, is muddleheaded and incompetent.
I dare not undertake the affairs of the strong."
He declined and did not become a minister,
retiring to live in poverty,
plowing the eastern seacoast.
Under the hall grew goosefoot and weeds,
and outside the gate grew brambles and thorns.
After seven years,
Yān and Lǔ were in conflict,
the people were bewildered and in chaos,
and his family had no savings.
The Duke governed the state himself,
his authority was slight among the lords,
and his person was weak before the Gāo
and Guó families.
The Duke was afraid
and summoned Àn Zǐ again.
Àn Zǐ arrived,
and the Duke returned to him the salary of seven years in one go,
yet his family had no hidden wealth.
Àn Zǐ stood firm,
the lords feared his authority,
the Gāo and Guó families submitted to his administration,
Yān and Lǔ offered tribute,
and the small states attended court from time to time.
Only after Àn Zǐ died did things decline.
7.23《Àn Zǐ Shǐ Gāo Jiū Zhì Jiā Sān Nián Ér Wèi Cháng Bì Guò Zhú Zhī》
After three years, he had never corrected my faults, so I dismissed him."
Yàn Zǐ sent Gāo Jiū to manage his household, but after three years, Gāo Jiū resigned.
The guest-master remonstrated, saying:
"Gāo Jiū has served you, Master, for three years,
and you have not rewarded him with rank or position, and now you dismiss him.
May I venture to ask what his crime is?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"To assist a person in establishing himself
only a sage can do that.
Those who lean to the left and those who lean to the right are those who are narrow and petty.
If those who lean to the left and those who lean to the right are not removed,
the four cardinal virtues will be askew.
Now, this man has served me for three years,
but he has never corrected my faults.
That is why I dismissed him."
7.24 *Jǐng Gōng praises Duke Huán's enfeoffment of Guǎn Zhòng and offers Yàn Zǐ a fief, which he declines.*
Jǐng Gōng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"In the past, my late lord, Duke Huán,
granted Guǎn Zhòng Hú and Gǔ,
with seventeen districts.
He recorded it on silk,
confirmed it with documents,
and announced it to the feudal lords,
as a hereditary fief for his descendants.
I am unwilling to fall short of my late lord.
Now, I will grant you a fief, Master,
extend to his descendants."
Àn Zǐ declined, saying:
"In the past, sagely kings rewarded the worthy based on their merits,
the worthy obtained them,
the unworthy lost them,
embracing virtue and cultivating propriety,
without any neglect or sloth.
Now, if those who serve the ruler and avoid punishment,
why should their descendants be given any share in it?
If those who are ministers of Qí must have a rewarded estate,
then how will the ruler of Qí provide for the altars of the state and the silks for the feudal lords?
I, Yīng, beg to decline."
And so he did not accept.
7.25 《Duke Jǐng sent Liángqiū Jù to deliver a thousand pieces of gold fur to Àn Zǐ, who firmly declined to accept it》
Duke Jǐng bestowed upon Àn Zǐ a fox-white fur coat and a black leopard fur coat,
worth a thousand pieces of gold,
and sent Liángqiū Jù to deliver them.
Àn Zǐ declined and did not accept them,
three times.
The Duke said:
"I have these two,
and I intend to wear them,
but now that you, sir, do not accept them,
I dare not wear them.
Rather than keeping them locked away,
wouldn't it be better to wear them out on my body?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"If the ruler were to grant [me such an honor],
assigning me, Yīng, to oversee the administration of the hundred officials,
with the ruler wearing fine clothes above,
and ordering me, Yīng, to wear them below,
that cannot serve as instruction."
He firmly declined and did not accept.
7.26 *Yàn Zǐ Wears Deer Hide to Court, and Jǐng Gōng Laments His Poverty; Yàn Zǐ Claims He Is Adorned*
Yàn Zǐ served as the minister of Jǐng Gōng,
wearing cloth clothes and a deer hide to court.
Gōng said:
"If your, Fūzǐ's, family
is so impoverished,
what is this bad garment you are wearing!
I, the lonely one, did not know,
this is my, the lonely one's, fault."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Yīng has heard that
those who consider the needs of others before clothing and feeding themselves
do not consider greed and obscurity as wrong;
those who consider the needs of others before acting
do not consider wickedness and deviancy as a burden.
Yīng is unworthy,
and my family is even less worthy than I am,
yet five hundred families rely on me to perform sacrifices to their ancestors.
I, Yīng, am still able to wear cloth clothes and a deer hide to court,
am I not then adorned!"
再拜而辭。 He bowed twice and took his leave.
7.27 《Zhòngní Chēng Yànzǐ Xíng Bǔ Sān Jūn Ér Bù Yǒu Guǒ Jūnzǐ Yě》 7.27 *Zhongni Praises Yanzi, Who Aided Three Rulers But Did Not Take Credit, Was Indeed a Gentleman*
仲尼曰： Zhòngní said:
「靈公汙， "Líng Gōng was corrupt,
晏子事之以整齊； Yànzǐ served him with order and propriety;
莊公壯， Zhuāng Gōng was strong,
晏子事之以宣武； Yànzǐ served him by promoting martial valor;
景公奢， Jǐng Gōng was extravagant,
晏子事之以恭儉： Yànzǐ served him with respect and frugality:
君子也！ He is a gentleman!
相三君而善不通下， Serving three rulers yet his goodness did not reach the lower ranks,
晏子、細人也。」 Yànzǐ is a petty man."
晏子聞之， Yànzǐ heard of this,
見仲尼曰： and went to see Zhòngní, saying:
「嬰聞君子有譏於嬰， "Yīng heard that the superior man has criticisms of Yīng,
是以來見。 therefore I have come to see you.
如嬰者， Someone like Yīng,
豈能以道食人者哉！ how could I be one who nourishes others with the Way!
嬰之宗族待嬰而祀其先人者數百家， Hundreds of families of Yīng's clan rely on Yīng to perform sacrifices to their ancestors,
與齊國之閒士待嬰而舉火者數百家， and hundreds of unemployed scholars of the state of Qí rely on Yīng to make a living;
臣為此仕者也。 I serve in office for this reason.
如臣者， Someone like me,
豈能以道食人者哉！」 how could I be one who nourishes others with the Way!"
晏子出， Yànzǐ went out,
仲尼送之以賓客之禮， Zhòngní saw him off with the rites of a guest,
再拜其辱。 and bowed twice to apologize for his disrespect.
反，命門弟子曰： Returning, he instructed his disciples, saying:
"He rescues the people's lives without boasting,
and performs deeds beneficial to three rulers without claiming credit.
Yàn Zǐ is truly a gentleman."
Outer chapters not in accordance with classical teachings.
8.1 "Zhòng Ní (Confucius) met Duke Jǐng, and Duke Jǐng wanted to grant him a fief, but Yàn Zǐ thought it was not permissible."
Zhòng Ní (Confucius) went to Qí,
and met Duke Jǐng.
Duke Jǐng was pleased with him
and wanted to grant him the fief of Ěr Jī,
and told Yàn Zǐ about it.
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"It is not permissible.
He has wide sleeves that are excessively compliant,
and cannot be used to teach inferiors;
he loves music, indulging the people,
and cannot be made to personally govern;
he establishes doctrines and builds enterprises,
and cannot maintain his office;
lavish funerals ruin the people and impoverish the state,
prolonged mourning conceals grief and wastes days,
and he cannot be made to care for the people;
what is difficult to put into practice is within himself,
and what is transmitted lacks substance externally,
therefore, he is different in attire,
strives for appearance,
and cannot guide the masses and train the common people.
Since the destruction of the great sages,
周室之卑也，[Zhōu shì zhī bēi yě,] The House of Zhou declined,
威儀加多，[wēi yí jiā duō,] ceremonial pomp increased,
而民行滋薄；[ér mín xíng zī báo;] but the people's conduct grew more depraved.
聲樂繁充，[shēng yuè fán chōng,] Musical performances flourished,
而世德滋衰。[ér shì dé zī shuāi.] but hereditary virtue declined.
今孔丘盛聲樂以侈世，[Jīn Kǒng Qiū shèng shēng yuè yǐ chǐ shì,] Now, Kǒng Qiū promotes music to indulge the age,
飾弦歌鼓舞以聚徒，[shì xián gē gǔ wǔ yǐ jù tú,] embellishes string music, songs, drums, and dances to gather followers,
繁登降之禮[fán dēng jiàng zhī lǐ] elaborates the rites of ascending and descending
以示儀，務趨翔之節以觀眾，[yǐ shì yí, wù qū xiáng zhī jié yǐ guān zhòng,] to display ceremony, and emphasizes the rules of hastening and circling to attract attention.
傳學不可以儀世，[chuán xué bù kě yǐ yí shì,] Transmitting learning cannot regulate the age,
勞思不可以補民，[láo sī bù kě yǐ bǔ mín,] exhausting thought cannot benefit the people,
兼壽不能殫其教，[jiān shòu bù néng dān qí jiào,] even a long life cannot exhaust his teachings,
當年不能究其禮，[dāng nián bù néng jiū qí lǐ,] a lifetime cannot master his rites,
積財不能贍其樂，[jī cái bù néng shàn qí yuè,] accumulated wealth cannot support his music,
繁飾邪術以營世君，[fán shì xié shù yǐ yíng shì jūn,] elaborately embellishes heterodox arts to manipulate rulers,
盛為聲樂以淫愚其民。[shèng wéi shēng yuè yǐ yín yú qí mín.] and greatly promotes music to debauch and delude the people.
其道也，[Qí dào yě,] His way,
不可以示世；[bù kě yǐ shì shì;] cannot serve as a model for the world;
其教也，[qí jiào yě,] his teachings,
不可以導民。[bù kě yǐ dǎo mín.] cannot guide the people.
今欲封之，[Jīn yù fēng zhī,] Now, if you want to enfeoff him,
以移齊國之俗，[yǐ yí Qí guó zhī sú,] to change the customs of the state of Qí,
非所以導眾存民也。」[fēi suǒ yǐ dǎo zhòng cún mín yě."] it is not the way to guide the multitude and preserve the people."
公曰：[Gōng yuē:] The Duke said:
「善。」[Shàn.] "Good."
于是厚其禮而留其封，[Yúshì hòu qí lǐ ér liú qí fēng,] Therefore, he increased the ceremonial gifts and kept the fief for him,
敬見不問其道，[jìng jiàn bù wèn qí dào,] respectfully received him but did not inquire about his way.
仲尼迺行。[Zhòng Ní nǎi xíng.] Zhòng Ní then departed.
8.2 *Jǐng Gōng* Ascends the *Lù Qǐn*, Hears a Crying Sound, Asks *Liáng Qiūjù*, *Yàn Zǐ*'s Response
*Jǐng Gōng* [景公] ascended the *Lù Qǐn* [路寢],
and heard a crying sound.
He said:
"The crying sound I hear,
what is it for?"
*Liáng Qiūjù* [梁丘據] replied:
"It is the followers of *Lǔ Kǒngqiū* [魯孔丘] who are engaged in exaggerated speech.
They are knowledgeable in rites and music,
and meticulous in mourning attire.
When their mother died,
they buried her with great extravagance,
observed mourning for three years,
and cried with great intensity."
The Duke said:
"Isn't that commendable!"
And his expression showed pleasure. *Yàn Zǐ* [晏子] said:
"In ancient times, the sages,
it's not that they didn't know how to elaborate on the rituals of ascending and descending,
to create detailed rules and regulations,
and to perform complicated numerical calculations to teach the people,
but they considered it troublesome and time-consuming.
Therefore, they designed the rites not to be excessively focused on expediting matters.
It's not that they didn't know how to wield shields and axes, and play bells, drums, flutes, and zithers to delight the masses,
but they considered it wasteful and labor-intensive.
Therefore, they designed the music not to be excessively focused on harmonizing the people.
It's not that they didn't know how to exhaust the wealth of generations and the resources of the state to honor the dead,
To weep and mourn with prolonged grief,
those who do not do this,
know that it does not help the dead but deeply harms the living,
therefore, they do not use it to guide the people.
Now, judging people, decorating rituals, and complicating matters,
envying pleasures and indulging the people,
revering the dead to harm the living,
these three things,
are what the sage kings forbade.
Worthy people are not employed,
virtue is destroyed, and customs flow into corruption,
therefore, these three evils can be practiced in the world.
Right and wrong, worthy and unworthy are mixed,
the superiors speak wildly and falsely,
therefore, likes and dislikes are not enough to guide the masses.
These three things,
are the policies of a confused world,
the teachings of a singular affair.
Why does Your Grace not observe this?
You accept it with your ears and rejoice in it with your face?"
8.3 "Zhòngní saw Duke Jǐng, Duke Jǐng said: Why doesn't the master see my steward?"
Zhòngní traveled to Qí,
and saw Duke Jǐng.
Duke Jǐng said:
"Why doesn't the master see my steward?"
Zhòngní replied:
"I have heard that Yàn Zǐ served three rulers and was able to be compliant,
this is because he has three hearts,
所以不見也。」Suǒyǐ bù jiàn yě." Therefore, he was not received."
Zhòngní departed,
Duke Jǐng used his words to tell Yàn Zǐ,
Yàn Zǐ replied saying:
"Not so!
It's not that Yīng has three minds,
it's that the three rulers had one mind,
all three rulers desired the peace of their state,
therefore Yīng was able to comply.
Yīng has heard that,
if something is right and he says it's wrong,
or if something is wrong and he says it's right,
it's still wrong.
Kǒng Qiū must be dwelling on this single-mindedness."
8.4 "Zhòngní in Qí, saw Duke Jǐng but did not see Yàn Zǐ, Zǐgòng posed a question"
Zhòngní went to Qí,
saw Duke Jǐng but did not see Yàn Zǐ.
Zǐgòng said:
"To see the ruler but not see those who administer the government,
is that acceptable?"
Zhòngní said:
"I have heard that Yàn Zǐ served three rulers and complied with them,
I doubt his character."
Yàn Zǐ heard of this,
and said:
"Yīng is just a commoner of Qí,
if he doesn't correct his actions,
and doesn't recognize his faults,
Unable to establish oneself independently.
Yīng has heard that
those who are fortunate are seen and loved,
and those who are unfortunate are seen and hated.
Slander and praise are grouped together,
sound and echo respond to each other;
they follow those whose actions are seen.
Yīng has heard that
serving three lords with one mind
is called being compliant;
serving one lord with three minds
is called being uncompliant.
Now, without having seen Yīng's actions,
you deem him uncompliant.
Yīng has heard that
a *jūnzǐ* stands alone and is not ashamed of his shadow,
sleeps alone and is not ashamed before his soul.
Kǒngzǐ uprooted trees and obliterated tracks,
not considering it a disgrace;
was impoverished in Chén and Cài,
not considering it a hardship.
If a person is rejected without knowing the reason,
it's like a dweller of the marshes rejecting axes,
or a dweller of the mountains rejecting nets.
These words come from your mouth,
yet you do not understand your own predicament.
Initially, I esteemed and valued the *rú* (Confucian scholars),
but now I regard the *rú* with suspicion."
Zhòngní heard of this and
said,
"There is a saying:
Words once spoken leave your mouth,
and cannot be stopped from traveling far;
conduct, once fixed upon the body,
cannot be hidden from the public eye.
I privately discussed Yàn Zǐ without fully considering the ruler's faults,
my sin is almost complete!
I have heard that a gentleman makes a friend of someone who surpasses him,
and a teacher of someone he does not measure up to.
Now, I misspoke about the master, and the master
criticized me,
thus, he is my teacher."
Thereupon, he had Zǎi Wǒ convey his apologies,
and then Zhòngní went to see him.
8.5 《Duke Jǐng Going Hunting Asks Yàn Zǐ Whether There are Any Among the Crowd Like Kǒngzǐ》
Duke Jǐng went hunting,
and it was cold,
so he covered himself with furs.
He looked around and asked Yàn Zǐ, saying,
"Among this crowd of people,
could there be anyone like Kǒngzǐ?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"There could be one like Kǒngzǐ, but there is not;
if there were one like Shùn, then Yīng would not recognize him."
The Duke said,
"The fact that Kǒngzǐ does not measure up to Shùn is obvious,
"Why is it said, 'If there is Kǒngzǐ 孔子 there, there is none;
if it is like Shùn 舜, then even a babe would not recognize him'?"
Yànzǐ 晏子 replied,
"This is precisely why Kǒngzǐ 孔子 does not measure up to Shùn 舜.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 only performs one role at a time.
When he is among the common people,
his mistakes are apparent,
how much more so when he is among gentlemen!
Shùn 舜, when among the common people,
aligns himself with the gentry;
when among gentlemen,
he aligns himself with the gentlemen;
when with sages,
he is naturally the material of a sage.
This is precisely why Kǒngzǐ 孔子 does not measure up to Shùn 舜."
8.6 "Zhòng Ní 仲尼 as Prime Minister of Lǔ 魯, Duke Jǐng 景 of [Lǔ] worried; Yànzǐ 晏子 replied telling him not to worry."
Zhòng Ní 仲尼 became prime minister of Lǔ 魯.
Duke Jǐng 景 of [Lǔ] was worried about this, and said to Yànzǐ 晏子,
"A neighboring state having a sage is
a cause for worry for an enemy state.
Now that Kǒngzǐ 孔子 is the prime minister of Lǔ 魯, what should be done?"
Yànzǐ 晏子 replied,
"Your lord need not worry.
The lord of Lǔ 魯
is a weak ruler,
and Kǒngzǐ 孔子
is a sage prime minister.
君不如陰重 Kǒngzǐ, It would be better for you, my lord, to secretly value Kǒngzǐ,
設以相齊， and appoint him to assist Qí.
孔子強諫而不聽， If Kǒngzǐ strongly remonstrates but is not heeded,
必驕魯而有齊， he will surely be arrogant towards Lǔ, yet possess Qí.
君勿納也。 Do not admit him, my lord.
夫絕於魯， For, having severed ties with Lǔ,
無主于齊， and not being accepted by Qí,
孔子困矣。」 Kǒngzǐ will be in dire straits."
居朞年， After a full year had passed,
孔子去魯之齊， Kǒngzǐ departed Lǔ for Qí,
景公不納， but Duke Jǐng did not accept him,
故困於陳蔡之間。 therefore he was stranded between Chén and Cài.
8.7 《景公問有臣有兄弟而強足恃乎晏子對不足恃》 8.7 《Duke Jǐng Asks Whether a Powerful Minister or Brother is Reliable; Yànzǐ Replies that They are Not》
景公問晏子曰： Duke Jǐng asked Yànzǐ, saying:
「有臣而強， "If I have a powerful minister,
足恃乎？」 is he reliable?"
晏子對曰： Yànzǐ replied, saying:
「不足恃。」 "He is not reliable."
「有兄弟而強， "If I have a powerful brother,
足恃乎？」 is he reliable?"
晏子對曰： Yànzǐ replied, saying:
「不足恃。」 "He is not reliable."
公忿然作色曰： The Duke angrily changed his expression, saying:
「吾今有恃乎？」 "Do I now have something to rely on?"
晏子對曰： Yànzǐ replied, saying:
「有臣而強， "Having a powerful minister,
無甚如湯； none was worse than Tāng;
Having brothers and being strong,
is not as bad as Jié.
Tāng assassinated his ruler,
Jié caused his elder brother to flee.
How can one rely on people as being sufficient?
It is possible to avoid ruin!"
8.8 *Jǐng Gōng Tours Niú Shān and is Slightly Happy, Requesting Yàn Zǐ for One Wish*
Jǐng Gōng toured Niú Shān,
and was slightly happy.
The Duke said:
"I request Yàn Zǐ for one wish."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"No,
what would Yīng wish for?"
The Duke said:
"Yàn Zǐ, one wish!"
He replied:
"I wish to have a ruler and be regarded with awe,
to have a wife and be returned to,
to have a son who can be left behind."
The Duke said:
"Good!
Yàn Zǐ's wish;
(please) state another wish."
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"I wish to have a ruler who is enlightened,
to have a wife who is talented,
the household not be poor,
Having good neighbors.
Having a ruler who is wise,
daily accommodating Yīng's actions;
having a wife who is capable,
then causing Yīng not to forget;
the family not being poor,
then not resenting what friends know;
having good neighbors,
then daily seeing gentlemen:
these are Yīng's wishes." The duke said:
"Excellent!
These are Àn Zǐ's wishes."
Àn Zǐ replied:
"Your servant wishes to have a ruler who can be assisted,
to have a wife who can be divorced,
to have a son who can be scolded."
The duke said:
"Excellent!
These are Àn Zǐ's wishes."
8.9 [Jǐng Gōng Had a Large Bell Made, Àn Zǐ, Zhòng Ní, and Bǎi Cháng Qiān Knew It Would Be Destroyed]
Jǐng Gōng had a large bell made,
intending to hang it.
Àn Zǐ,
Zhòng Ní, and Bǎi Cháng Qiān, these three men went to court,
and all said:
"The bell will be destroyed."
It was struck,
and indeed it was destroyed.
Gōng zhào sān zǐ zhě ér wèn zhī. The Duke summoned three men and asked them about it.
Yàn Zǐ duì yuē: Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Zhōng dà, "The bell is large,
bù sì xiān jūn ér yǐ yàn, and instead of being used to sacrifice to the former rulers, it is used for feasting.
fēi lǐ, This is not proper ritual.
shì yǐ yuē zhōng jiāng huǐ." Therefore, I say the bell will be destroyed."
Zhòng Ní yuē: Zhòng Ní said:
"Zhōng dà ér xuán xià, "The bell is large and hangs low.
chōng zhī qí qì xià huí ér shàng báo, When struck, its sound reverberates downward and then rises thinly upward.
shì yǐ yuē zhōng jiāng huǐ." Therefore, I say the bell will be destroyed."
Bǎi Chángqiān yuē: Bǎi Chángqiān said:
"Jīn gēngshēn, "Today is a gēngshēn day,
léi rì yě, a day of thunder.
yīn mò shèng yú léi, No sound surpasses thunder.
shì yǐ yuē zhōng jiāng huǐ yě." Therefore, I say the bell will be destroyed."
8.10 《Tián Wúyǔ fēi Yàn Zǐ yǒu lǎo qī Yàn Zǐ duì yǐ qù lǎo wèi zhī luàn》 8.10 《Tián Wúyǔ Criticizes Yàn Zǐ for Having an Old Wife; Yàn Zǐ Replies That Abandoning the Old is Called Disorder》
Tián Wúyǔ jiàn Yàn Zǐ dúlì yú guīnèi, Tián Wúyǔ saw Yàn Zǐ standing alone inside his chambers.
yǒu fùrén chū yú shì zhě, A woman came out of the room.
fà bānbái, Her hair was streaked with white,
yī zī bù zhī yī ér wú lǐ qiú. and she wore a black cloth garment without a fur lining.
Tián Wúyǔ jī zhī yuē: Tián Wúyǔ ridiculed him, saying:
"Chū yú shì hé wéi zhě yě?" "Who is this coming out of the room?"
Yàn Zǐ yuē: Yàn Zǐ said:
"Yīng zhī jiā yě." "She is a member of Yīng's family."
Wúyǔ yuē: Wúyǔ said:
"Wèi wèi zhōng qīng, "Your position is that of a senior minister,
shí tián qīshí wàn, and you receive seventy thousand mu of land as sustenance.
hé yǐ lǎo qī wèi?" Why do you have an old wife?"
He replied,
"Yīng has heard that,
to dismiss the old,
is called disorder;
to take in the young,
is called licentiousness.
Moreover, to forget righteousness upon seeing beauty,
to lose moral principles while in wealth and high position,
is called going against the proper way.
How can Yīng have licentious behavior,
disregard moral principles,
and go against the ways of the ancients?"
8.11 "A Craftswoman Wishes to Enter the Service of Yàn Zǐ, But Yàn Zǐ Declines"
There was a craftswoman who entrusted herself to the household of Yàn Zǐ.
She said,
"Your handmaiden
is a rustic from the wilds of Dōngguō.
I wish to enter your service
and be counted among the lower ranks."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Only now do I realize my lack of virtue!
In ancient times, those who governed
had scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants living separately,
men and women were distinct and did not intermingle,
therefore scholars had no corrupt behavior,
and women had no licentious affairs.
Now, I am entrusted with the nation and its people,
and if you wish to rush to me,
Bù Bìsè must have seen that my actions lacked integrity."
Thereupon, he ceased visiting.
8.12 *Jǐng Gōng Wanted to Execute the Featherman, but Yàn Zǐ Thought Killing Him Inappropriate*
Gōng Jǐng was handsome.
A featherman looked at Gōng Jǐng with impropriety.
The duke said to his attendants,
"Ask him,
why does he look at me with such impropriety?"
The featherman replied,
"To speak is to die,
and not to speak is also to die;
I secretly admire your beauty."
The duke said,
"He finds me attractive?
Kill him!"
Yàn Zǐ entered at an inopportune time
and said,
"I have heard that Your Lordship is angry with a featherman."
The duke said,
"Yes.
He finds me attractive,
therefore I will kill him."
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I have heard that rejecting desire is immoral,
and disliking love is inauspicious.
Even if he finds you attractive,
it is not appropriate to kill him according to the law."
The Duke said:
"How disgusting!
If it were to be bathed,
I would have people hold its back."
8.13 *Duke Jǐng asked Yàn Zǐ about the water in the East Sea that is red, and Yàn Zǐ answered in detail*
Duke Jǐng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"In the middle of the East Sea,
there is water that is red,
in it there are jujubes,
they flower but do not bear fruit,
why is that?"
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"In the past, Duke Mù of Qín rode a dragon to govern the world,
and wrapped steamed jujubes in yellow cloth,
and reached the East Sea and discarded the cloth,
that yellow cloth,
is why the water is red;
the steamed jujubes,
is why they flower but do not bear fruit."
The Duke said:
"Why did I question you in detail?"
He replied:
"Yīng has heard that,
those who ask in detail,
should also be answered in detail."
8.14 *Duke Jǐng asked if there was anything extremely large and extremely small in the world, and Yàn Zǐ replied*
Duke Jǐng asked Yàn Zǐ:
"Is there anything extremely large in the world?"
Yàn Zǐ answered,
"Yes.
The péng's foot swims through floating clouds,
its back towers over the blue sky,
its tail rests in the celestial expanse,
it leaps and pecks in the Northern Sea,
its neck and tail cough into heaven and earth! Yet, it is utterly unaware of the location of its six wings."
The Duke said,
"Is there anything extremely small in the world?"
Yàn Zǐ answered,
"Yes.
In the Eastern Sea, there is an insect
that nests in a mosquito's eyelash,
breeds twice and flies twice,
and the mosquito is not alarmed.
Your servant, Yīng, does not know its name,
but the fishermen of the Eastern Sea call it Jiāo Míng."
8.15 *Zhuāng Gōng Plans to Attack Jǔ, and the People of Jǔ Deceive [The Duke] by Claiming Yàn Zǐ is Present, and Then [The Duke] Stops*
Zhuāng Gōng closed the gates and planned to attack Jǔ.
The people of the state thought there was disorder,
and all grasped long weapons and stood at the crossroads.
The Duke summoned Suī Xiū to be his minister and asked,
"I closed the gates and planned to attack Jǔ.
The people of the state thought there was disorder,
and all brandished long weapons and stood at the crossroads.
What should I do?"
Xiū answered,
"If there is truly no disorder but the state thinks there is,
then benevolent men would not exist.
Please issue an order to the state,
saying, "Yàn Zǐ is here."
The Duke said:
"Agreed."
He issued an order to the state:
"Whoever says that the state is in turmoil,
Yàn Zǐ is here."
Thereupon they all dispersed their troops and returned home.
The gentleman said:
"Indeed, conduct must be diligently cultivated.
That Yàn Zǐ's presence brings peace of mind to the people
is not something achieved in a single day,
but is something that is seen in the present and trusted by the future.
Therefore, Yàn Zǐ held the position of a minister,
and brought peace to the hearts of the myriad people."
8.16 《When Yàn Zǐ died, Duke Jǐng hurried to him, wept in sorrow, and then left》
Duke Jǐng was traveling in Zī,
when he heard that Yàn Zǐ had died.
The Duke rode in an extravagant carriage, wearing elaborate clothes, and drove rapidly.
Because he thought he was too slow,
he got out of the carriage and ran;
realizing that it was not as fast as the carriage,
he got back in.
By the time he arrived at the state,
he had gotten out and run four times,
weeping as he went.
Upon arriving, he prostrated himself before the corpse and wailed,
He said:
"You, Daifu (Dàifu), reproach me, the lonely one, day and night,
not overlooking even an inch.
Yet I, the lonely one, still indulge in excesses and do not restrain myself,
and the grievances and sins heavily accumulate upon the people.
Now, Heaven sends calamity upon the state of Qí (齊),
not adding it to me, the lonely one,
but adding it to you, Fūzǐ (夫子).
The altars of the state of Qí (齊) are in danger.
To whom will the people turn for help!"
8.17 《Yàn Zǐ Sǐ Jǐng Gōng Kū Zhī Chēng Mò Fù Chén Gào Wú Guò》 (晏子死景公哭之稱莫復陳告吾過) [Yàn Zǐ Died, Duke Jǐng Wept, Saying That No One Would Again Point Out His Faults]
When Yàn Zǐ (晏子) died, Duke Jǐng (景公) held a jade object and placed it on Yàn Zǐ (晏子) while weeping,
his tears soaked his collar.
Zhāng Zǐ (章子) remonstrated, saying:
"This is not in accordance with ritual."
The Duke said:
"What use is ritual?
In the past, when I, the lonely one, was with Fūzǐ (夫子) on the high ground of the public domain,
he refused to listen to me, the lonely one, three times in a single day.
Now, who can do that?
If I lose Fūzǐ (夫子), I will perish.
What ritual is there to speak of?"
He removed the jade, and continued weeping,
expressing his sorrow fully before leaving.
8.18A 《Yàn Zǐ Méi Zuǒyòu Yú Xián Zhāng Jiàn Jǐng Gōng Cì Zhī Yú》 (晏子沒左右諛弦章諫景公賜之魚) [After Yàn Zǐ Died, the Attendants Flattered; Xián Zhāng Remonstrated When Duke Jǐng Gave Him Fish]
Seventeen years after Yàn Zǐ (晏子) passed away,
Jǐng Gōng 景公 feasted his ministers with wine.
The duke shot an arrow,
and missed the target.
Those in the hall loudly praised his shot,
as if from a single mouth.
The duke turned pale and sighed,
throwing down his bow and arrows.
Xián Zhāng 弦章 entered.
The duke said,
"Zhāng 章!
Since I lost Yàn Zǐ 晏子, I have never heard of my faults."
Zhāng 章 said, "I have heard that the ruler favors subservience and enjoys his ministers' food.
The inchworm eats yellow and becomes yellow,
eats green and becomes green. Perhaps you feast on the words of flatterers."
The duke said,
"Well said."
He gifted Xián Zhāng 弦章 fifty cartloads of fish.
Xián Zhāng 弦章 returned home,
the fish carts blocking the road.
Zhāng 章 stroked his servant and said,
"Those who praised the shot earlier,
all desire this fish."
He firmly declined to accept them.

8.18B 《Qún Shū Zhì Yào yǐn Yàn Zǐ méi zuǒ yòu yú Xián Zhāng jiàn Jǐng Gōng cì zhī yú》 《群書治要引晏子沒左右諛弦章諫景公賜之魚》(The Essentials of Governance Extracted from Various Books: After Yàn Zǐ's Death, Flatterers Surrounded Him; Xián Zhāng Admonished Duke Jǐng and Was Given Fish).
The duke said,
"Zhāng 章!
Since I lost Àn Zǐ,
it has been seventeen years now,
and I have never heard of my faults.
Now, in a shooting competition, my faults are pointed out,
and those who praise me do so as if with one voice."
Xián Zhāng replied,
"This is because your ministers are unworthy.
Their wisdom is insufficient to know your faults,
their courage is insufficient to offend your face.
However, there is one thing:
I have heard that if the ruler likes something,
then his ministers will submit to it;
if the ruler craves something,
then his ministers will eat it.
When the inchworm eats yellow,
its body becomes yellow;
when it eats green,
its body becomes green.
Could it be that you still enjoy listening to flattering words?"
The duke said,
"Good."
8.18C 《Tàipíng Yùlǎn Rénshì Bù Liùshíqī Yǐn Àn Zǐ Méi Zuǒyòu Yú Xián Zhāng Jiàn Jǐng Gōng Cì Zhī Yú》
The duke bestowed fifty chariots of fish upon Xián Zhāng.
Xián Zhāng returned,
and the fish carts blocked the road.
Zhāng stroked the hand of his driver and said,
"Formerly, Àn Zǐ resigned from rewards in order to correct the ruler,
therefore, mistakes were not concealed.
Now, the various ministers flatter to seek benefit,
if I were to accept the fish,
it would be to go against the righteousness of Àn Zǐ
and follow the desires of flattery."
He firmly declined the fish and did not accept it.
The gentleman said:
"Xián Zhāng's incorruptibility
is a remnant of Àn Zǐ's conduct."
Lost Writings from the Àn Zǐ Chūnqiū
9.1 The Son of Heaven uses the world to honor all worthy men with a sacrifice at the beginning of the season.
Quoted in the Kǒng Commentary of the "Wáng Zhì" section of the Lǐjì (Book of Rites).
9.2 Truly a gentleman,
straight speech is his duty.
Quoted in Wáng Yīnglín's Shī Kǎo (Examination of Poetry).
9.3 A widow plants orchids,
they grow but are not fragrant;
a stepson obtains food,
he becomes fat but not radiant.
Quoted in the Tàipíng Yùlǎn, volume 849.
9.4 My family has always been poor,
during the day we suffer from working hard,
at night we are content with tired sleep,
during these times,
the books are all covered in dust.
Quoted in the Tàipíng Yùlǎn, volume 37.
9.5 Governing the world is like entrusting a fur coat;
employing the worthy is the reality of entrusting the fur coat.
Duke Huán listened to Guǎn Zhòng,
and Zhào Xiāng listened to Wáng Dēng.
This is what is meant by entrusting the fur coat.
*Wénxuǎn*, Rèn Fǎng's "Memorial Recommending Scholars for the Governor of Yángzhōu, Xiao," Lǐ's commentary cites.
9.6 To repair what is on behalf of one's feet, is to repair what is for the market or the dead.
*Běitáng Shūchāo* 45 cites.
9.7 The reason why the ruler is esteemed is the commands.
If the commands are not carried out,
it is as if there is no ruler.
Therefore, a wise ruler is careful about commands.
*Tàipíng Yùlǎn* 638 cites;
*Běitáng Shūchāo* 45,
*Yìwén Lèijù* 54, both cite it as from *Shēn Zǐ*.
9.8 Those whose rank is increasingly high, their intentions are increasingly lower;
those whose official position is increasingly great, their hearts are increasingly smaller;
those whose emoluments are increasingly generous, their benevolence is increasingly widespread.
*Yìwén Lèijù* 23 cites.
9.9 When a person is about to become ill,
they will surely first dislike the taste of fine grain and meat;
when a state is about to perish,
they will surely first resent the words of loyal ministers.
*Yìwén Lèijù* 23 cites.
9.10 Those whose markings are beautiful will surely have their bodies skinned;
those whose horns are magnificent will surely have their bodies slaughtered;
sweet springs will surely dry up.
Straight trees will inevitably be felled.
Quoted in Volume 23 of the *Yìwén Lèijù*.
9.11 Níng Qī wished to present himself to Duke Huán of Qí.
He was impoverished and feeding cattle outside the north gate.
Duke Huán ordered the night watchman to move the gate aside for his chariot.
Qī then beat on the chariot yoke and sang.
Duke Huán took pity and considered him exceptional,
Ordering the chariot behind to carry him.
Quoted in Volume 141 of the *Běitáng Shūchāo*.
9.12 The Marquis of Qí returned from Jiá Gǔ,
and said to Yàn Zǐ:
"I have offended the Lord of Lǔ,
what should be done?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"A gentleman apologizes for his faults with sincerity,
a petty person apologizes with words.
Qí once invaded four towns of Lǔ,
please return them all."
Quoted in Hé Xiū's Commentary on the 10th Year of Duke Dìng in the *Gōngyáng Commentary*.
The *Commentary* states:
"All are from the texts of the *Yàn Zǐ Chūnqiū*, the *Jiā Yǔ*, and
the *Kǒngzǐ Shìjiā*."
9.13 The Marquis of Qí saw Yàn Zǐ off at the Xuě Palace.
Quoted in the *Yuánhé Jùnxiàn Túzhì: Sixth Circuit of Henan, Línzī County*.
9.14 People do not wear coarse clothes,
nor eat dregs and chaff.
Food and drink are not fine.
Faces and appearances
are not worth looking at;
therefore, meals must be of fine grains and meat.
Quoted from *Běitáng Shūchāo* 北堂書鈔, volume 143.
9.15 Guǎn Yíwú 管夷吾 said:
"I have already told you about nurturing life;
what about seeing off the dead?"
Yàn Píngzhòng 晏平仲 said:
"The sending off of the dead is simple;
what is there to tell?"
Guǎn Yíwú 管夷吾 said:
"I indeed wish to hear of it."
Píngzhòng 平仲 said:
"Once dead,
is it in my control?
Burning is acceptable,
sinking is acceptable,
burying is fine,
exposing is fine,
covering with firewood and discarding in a ditch is acceptable,
donning ceremonial robes and embroidered skirts and placing in a stone coffin is acceptable,
only as circumstance dictates."
Seen in *Lièzǐ – Yángzhū Piān* 列子‧楊朱篇;
*Yìlín* 意林 2 quotes *Lièzǐ* 列子, referring to it directly as
"Yan Zi said."
9.16 Clouds gather from the four seas,
rain arrives from a thousand miles.
Quoted from "Ji Zuan Yuanhai," Volume 2.
9.17 Shi Kuang recognized the firewood for the hearth,
Yi Ya distinguished between the Zi and Mian rivers.
Quoted from "Ji Zuan Yuanhai," Volume 61.
